home_pitcher_note: Opening Day starts are nothing new to Hernandez, who will be making his eighth. Still, there will be some newness to the event. A 10-year Major League veteran, Hernandez will be making the shift to the AL for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: With Angels aces John Lackey and Kelvim Escobar out with injuries, Weaver emerged as the club's lead pitcher with a dominant spring, one that helped earn him his first Opening Day gig.

home_pitcher_note: Having shed 25 pounds during the offseason, Bonser is looking to prove that he can pitch deeper into games than he did in 2007. The right-hander suffered a bit of a setback in his sophomore season when he struggled to make it past the fifth or sixth innings of his starts. While his stamina hasn't really been tested yet, Bonser showed more life on his fastball and snap on his breaking pitches this spring.
away_pitcher_note: Garland has been exactly what the Angels thought they were getting when they shipped Orlando Cabrera to the White Sox for him: a strike thrower who keeps his defense in the game and doesn't beat himself. He could be back in the form that made him a back-to-back 18-game winner in 2005 and 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Following an impressive stint in the Arizona Fall League, Blackburn emerged as not only a legitimate prospect in the Twins organization, but a true rotation candidate. A strong spring helped solidify Blackburn's spot.
away_pitcher_note: By his own assessment, Saunders had his best Spring Training. He has been in full command of his repertoire, which features a two-seam fastball that induces a lot of groundouts. He'll sneak a four-seamer past hitters on occasion.

home_pitcher_note: When the Twins sent Slowey down to the Minors last July, he was told to mix in all his pitches. The right-hander did just that in his September callup, posting a 3.34 ERA in six appearances that month.
away_pitcher_note: Which Santana will show up in 2008 -- the one who lost his spot in the rotation in '07, or the one who looked like a budding star in '06? The Angels are betting on the latter, convinced that Santana has corrected a flaw in his delivery.

home_pitcher_note: Baker entered the spring as a legitimate top-of-the-rotation candidate. But a bout with the flu and a strained right lat muscle hindered his progress. Having faced the possibility of a DL stint due to his setbacks, the right-hander will have to continue to regain his stamina and stretch out at the start of the season. His first start comes against a team against which he nearly threw a perfect game last season. Baker is 3-2 with a 2.81 ERA in six career starts vs. Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Bale, signed as a reliever out of Japan, was so impressive down the stretch last season that the Royals tried him as a starter in Spring Training. He won the job and will make his first Major League start since 2003 when he was with the Reds. Bale lost about 25 pounds in the offseason and impressed this spring with his ability to throw hard and straight (11 strikeouts, two walks in 14 2/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Mixing in all of his pitches, including a 60 mph Bugs Bunny curve, Hernandez shut down an aggressive Angels lineup in his last start. The Twins were pleased to see the way that Hernandez not only produced results, but provided a veteran presence on the mound -- even moving his infielders into the correct spots. The right-hander, who switched leagues for the first time in his 10-year career when he joined the Twins, will get his second American League test when he faces the Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Meche hung in against a tough Tigers lineup on Opening Day, giving up eight hits, including four for extra bases, and four walks but just three runs. Fortunately, one runner was thrown out at the plate and Meche forced the Tigers to strand eight others in his six innings. He finished strong with a one-two-three sixth and gave the Royals a chance to win, which they did in 11 innings. Manager Trey Hillman called the performance "gutsy."

home_pitcher_note: Despite some early first-inning jitters, Bonser put together a solid first outing of the 2008 season. Trying to overcome his penchant for not lasting deep into outings in '07, Bonser managed to pitch six innings and throw just 89 pitches over that span. His hope is that he'll only increase that length with each outing. Bonser is set to face the Royals in his second start, a team he's gone 2-4 against with a 4.73 ERA in nine career appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Despite a poor showing in 2007 with the Dodgers, the Royals saw some life in Tomko when he resurfaced with the Padres late in the season. So it was, "Sign here." His 11 seasons in the Majors include 250 starts, so he's no novice at this assignment. He's thrown his usual assortment of hard, hard, hard pitches this spring, but pitching coach Bob McClure gave him some variety with an offspeed curveball. Tomko caught on fast and it's been working rather well.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander struggled with his control during Wednesday's 2008 debut, throwing 103 pitches over just five innings. Vazquez struck out six but also walked four, including Ryan Garko and Franklin Gutierrez consecutively with two outs in the fifth inning to force home a run. A two-out walk given to Kelly Shoppach in the second set up Grady Sizemore's two-run single. Vazquez gets the call for the White Sox home opener against Minnesota, coming off an 8-5 showing with a 3.57 ERA over 16 starts at U.S. Cellular Field in 2007. Vazquez has a 4-5 career mark against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn was impressive in his first Major League start, holding the Angels to just one run on five hits over seven innings. The right-hander didn't appear to be intimidated against a potent Angels lineup, attacking hitters like Vladimir Guerrero, who struck out twice in his three at-bats facing Blackburn. Next up for Blackburn will be a test on the road, as he'll pitch for the first time at U.S. Cellular Field against the White Sox. Last season, he threw two scoreless innings of relief against Chicago in the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: If Thursday's first start serves as any indication, the second-year southpaw appears primed for a big season in 2008. Danks held the Indians hitless for five innings, before allowing Casey Blake's single to center to start the sixth. Danks exited after 6 2/3 innings, giving up one earned run, while striking out two and walking two. Danks also recorded 11 outs via the ground ball. He has a 1-2 record with a 5.63 ERA against Minnesota, and a 3-6 career mark at home.
away_pitcher_note: Baker didn't show any signs of the setbacks he endured in Spring Training during his first start of the season. Baker limited the Royals to just three runs on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings. More importantly he was able to throw 84 pitches without any problems. Baker's health is key for a rotation that's already endured its first setback with Kevin Slowey's strained right biceps muscle. Baker will remain on regular five-day rest and face the White Sox on Wednesday at U.S. Cellular Field in his next start. Baker is 1-2 with a 9.14 ERA in five career starts against Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: Meche was knocked around by the Twins last Saturday to the tune of six runs on six hits in 5 2/3 innings. He started out great, with three near-perfect innings, but suddenly came unraveled and started making mistakes. Justin Morneau crashed a three-run homer and things went downhill. Morneau also had an RBI double against him. Meche had gutted out a tough six innings on Opening Day against the Tigers and that's the kind of performance the Royals came to appreciate last season.
away_pitcher_note: Twins: Hernandez's first stint in the American League has gone as well as could be expected. He pitched efficiently again in his second outing of the season, allowing just four runs to the Royals over seven innings while throwing a total of 74 pitches. The right-hander continues to baffle hitters with his slow, Bugs Bunny curveball, which topped out in the high 60s on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Tomko dodged his way through five scoreless innings against the Twins last Sunday, even though he gave up six hits and a walk. It was his first start this season and he got help from an outfield throw-out and two double plays but he was doggedly difficult when he had to be. The Twins made him work and he expended 92 pitches in his outing. Tomko is well-known for throwing hard but now he's mixing in an offspeed curveball, which seems to keep batters off balance and guessing.
away_pitcher_note: Bonser was effective during his second start of the season. He gave up just three runs on eight hits in seven innings to the Royals. Bonser did not walk a single batter in the outing, stretching his streak to two straight starts without issuing a walk. Despite his record, Bonser hasn't exactly been aided by the Twins offense, either, as they've scored a total of two runs in his first two starts. Bonser will face the Royals for a second straight time in his next start, this one at Kauffman Stadium in Kansas City. Bonser is 1-2 with a 5.85 ERA in four career appearances there.

home_pitcher_note:
Not nearly as sharp as in his season debut at Detroit, Bannister nevertheless limited the Yankees to two runs in five innings in Tuesday's Kansas City opener. 
Bannister, who normally induces a lot of contact, ran up 97 pitches primarily as a result of four walks and six strikeouts. The weather was wet, cold and windy, making precision pitching difficult, and a shifting strike zone also was cited as a troublesome factor. Even so, Bannister notched the victory. Last season he did quite well against the Twins -- 2-0 with a 2.05 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: After being delayed in his arrival to Spring Training by visa troubles, Liriano didn�t quite make the amount of progress the Twins hoped to see. He was sent to the Minors to make two starts, one for Class A Fort Myers and one for Triple-A Rochester. Despite being a little shaky in those two starts, Liriano showed enough to earn himself a callup to take over the starting spot vacated by an injured Kevin Slowey. This will mark Liriano's first career start against the Royals. He's pitched three scoreless innings of relief against Kansas City.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman became the first Tigers pitcher to earn a victory with his five-plus innings of work on Wednesday at Boston, recovering from a pair of early runs to keep the mighty Red Sox lineup relatively in check. He continued to show progression with his offspeed pitch, using it liberally and early to try to get Boston's power hitters off their timing. That could come in handy against a Twins lineup that has put up big innings against him over the years.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn continued to turn heads in his second Major League start. He gave up just two runs on seven hits over five innings against the White Sox at U.S. Cellular Field. With a dominating fastball and cutter, Blackburn has had success by mixing in his offspeed pitches more frequently. He now must try to carry that same plan into his first career start at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: A struggling slider and inconsistent location has left Robertson unable to eat innings like he usually does. He threw 107 pitches over 5 1/3 innings in his last start Thursday at Boston, on the way to a combined 212 pitches from Tigers pitchers on the night, despite Robertson's command of the inside part of the plate the first time through the Red Sox order. He was stingy against the Twins last season, going 2-1 with a 1.93 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: On a chilly night in Chicago, Baker was able to be effective, although not brilliant, against the White Sox. Baker pitched five innings and allowed three runs, all of which came on solo home runs. Baker�s few mistakes came on balls up in the zone, and the pitcher admitted that weather was a factor in his miscues. His next test will come in Detroit at Comerica Park, where the right-hander is 1-1 with a 1.80 ERA in two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: In his first road start for the Twins, Hernandez looked like his transition to the American League has been no sweat. Facing the Royals for the second straight time, Hernandez pitched seven scoreless innings while allowing seven hits and walking just one. The Cuban right-hander continues to shut down opponents with his slow-moving curveball and ability to mix in all of his pitches. Next up will be a start at the Metrodome, where he faces the Rays. He's 2-2 with a 5.77 ERA in six career starts against Tampa Bay.
away_pitcher_note: Currently the Rays' top pitcher, Shields is coming off a solid performance in his '08 Tropicana Field debut, allowing two earned runs over six innings vs. Baltimore. The right-hander will take the mound next vs. Minnesota, a team he has traditionally struggled against. Shields is 1-1 in two games against the Twins, posting a 6.71 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Despite seeing his no-walk streak come to an end in his third start, Bonser was definitely impressive on a cold night at Kauffman Stadium. Bonser held the Royals scoreless over six innings in his second straight start against the club. He allowed just three hits, with the Royals' first hit not coming until the fifth inning. Bonser was also efficient with his pitch count once again, recording 89 pitches over his six innings. The right-hander will now face the Rays at the Metrodome. He's 1-0 against Tampa Bay with a 3.06 ERA in three career starts.
away_pitcher_note: After winning a rotation spot coming out of Spring Training, Hammel is coming off the most impressive start in his career. The righty held Baltimore to two runs, striking out four in a career-long seven-inning appearance on April 12. The 25-year-old said he has made several adjustments this year, including slowing down on the mound, and it has paid dividends. His initial outing, in New York on April 7, was also a strong performance. Hammel held a potent Yankees lineup to four runs over six innings, with two strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano'’s return to the Major Leagues following a 19-month layoff due to Tommy John surgery wasn'’t quite as impressive as the Twins had hoped. In bitter cold conditions in Kansas City, Liriano gave up four runs on six hits over 4 2/3 innings. Walks were the big trouble point for the left-hander as he issued five while struggling to find his command. His next start will be in the warm conditions of the Metrodome, where he faces the Indians. Liriano is 1-1 with a 3.29 ERA in four career starts against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Lee tossed his second straight outstanding start in a victory over the A's Sunday in Cleveland. Continuing to stash aside a disappointing 2007, Lee was as good as he's been in perhaps two years. Lee found himself ahead of almost every hitter, relying virtually solely on a precisely commanded fastball before mixing in a few more off-speed pitches to keep the A's guessing late. In all, Lee allowed only one run on two hits while striking out eight over eight innings. Save for a back-to-back hits in the fourth inning, Lee was perfect. He retired all 23 other hitters he faced. Lee attributes the strong start to a healthy Spring Training, which he missed last year and says contributed to his disastrous 2007 season.

home_pitcher_note: After shutting down two potent offenses in the Angels and the White Sox, Blackburn appeared well on his way to doing the same against the Tigers in his most recent start. But in his final inning of work, the right-hander gave up four runs on four hits. Blackburn is now set to face the Indians at the Metrodome. Last season, Blackburn pitched twice in relief against Cleveland and gave up two runs over his four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook continued his solid '08 season with a quality start -- albeit a no-decision -- against the Red Sox on Monday. He went 6 1/3 innings, allowing just two runs (one earned) on seven hits with three walks and five strikeouts. While he got ahead and got some big ground-ball outs with his trusty sinker, he also had a nasty slider working. Westbrook is 7-8 with a 3.61 ERA in his career against the Twins and 1-6 with a 4.61 ERA in nine career appearances at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander found a bit of trouble late in his last outing getting pitches up in the zone. It led to Baker giving up three home runs to the Tigers, although all were solo shots. Baker said that he's been working better out of his stretch than his windup. It's something he will try to work on during his bullpen session this week. The hope is that he can make more pitches down in the zone from his windup and limit the number of mistakes to another difficult lineup -- the Indians. Baker was 1-1 with a 2.80 ERA in two starts against Cleveland in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd shook off the struggles of his first two starts of the season with a solid outing against the Red Sox on Tuesday. In six innings of work, all he allowed was an unearned run on six hits with no walks and six strikeouts. The fact that he didn't walk anybody was the most encouraging stat. Byrd had endured some uncharacteristic control problems against the A's and Angels, so he was happy to get back to form in this no-decision effort. Byrd is an impressive 6-1 with a 2.11 ERA in nine career starts at the Metrodome, which can be a difficult ballpark for contact pitchers like him.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton has pitched quite a bit better than his numbers suggest, and his most recent outing was a good example of such. Although he gave up three runs in the first inning and was peppered for a career-high-tying 12 hits, he only gave up one run after the first, didn't issue any walks and managed to get through eight innings on 101 pitches. In his first season as Oakland's No. 1 starter, Blanton hasn't received much in the way of offensive support with the exception of a nine-run largesse on April 11. In Blanton's other four starts, he's been backed by a total of six runs.
away_pitcher_note: After winning his first three starts, Hernandez was the recipient of a no-decision against the Rays in his most recent outing. The pitcher gave up five runs (three earned) with four of them courtesy of three home runs. One thing that Hernandez did improve on was getting the ball to catcher Joe Mauer faster in pitch-out situations. Mauer was able to catch two Rays on attempted steals and shut down Tampa Bay�s running game. During Spring Training, Hernandez had problems doing that. He's 2-2 with a 4.76 ERA in four career starts against the A's in his career, with all of the previous meetings occurring in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: Brought off the disabled list about a week earlier than expected in the wake of injuries to A's starters Rich Harden and Justin Duchscherer, Gaudin, who had offseason surgery on his left hip and right foot -- on the same December day -- and made only one Spring Training appearance, was outstanding in his most recent outing. He stifled Kansas City with seven innings of four-hit work, allowing one earned run while striking out eight and walking one on 96 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Heading into the 2008 season, the Twins were looking to Bonser to help lead the starting staff as one of their more experienced starters. But Bonser hasn't exactly lived up to the billing. In his fourth start of the season, Bonser had problems commanding the strike zone. Just 46 of Bonser's 72 pitches were for strikes and the pitcher admittedly didn't have his best stuff.

home_pitcher_note: After two nice starts, Smith stumbled a little bit, allowing four runs (three earned) against the Kansas City Royals on Saturday. He gave up a three-run homer in the first inning and a solo shot in the second. Over his final 13 batters, though, he struck out four, and gave up two singles. He?ll be making his third road start of the season against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Liriano had problems commanding the strike zone. After struggling to locate his fastball against the Royals last Sunday, Liriano had similar issues when he faced the Indians on Friday night. The left-hander walked a total of five batters in his outing while allowing three runs on four hits. Despite the problems with his fastball, Liriano's dominant slider has appeared to be getting back into form.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood is 1-0 with a 3.75 ERA in two starts at home this year and is 8-1 with a 3.52 ERA in his last 13 starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington. In 35 career starts in Arlington, he is 16-11 with a 4.97 ERA. He has never beaten the Twins in his career, going 0-5 with a 5.64 ERA that is his third highest against any American League team.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander made it two straight impressive outings at the Metrodome to start the season. After holding the Angels to just one run in his first start of the year, Blackburn delivered a nearly identical start against the Indians. He pitched 7 2/3 shutout innings, holding Cleveland to eight hits while not issuing a walk in the outing, although he did record one hit-by-pitch. Blackburn has settled in to mix in all of his pitches and most importantly, has started to rely on his sinker, something he'll need at hitter-friendly Ameriquest Field.

home_pitcher_note: The 31-year-old Aruban-born right-hander is expected to be recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma to make his Rangers debut, pitching in the big leagues for the first time since May 12, 2007. Ponson was 1-2 with a 3.47 ERA in five games (four starts) for Oklahoma. He arrives with a career record of 82-101 with a 4.94 ERA in 10 Major League seasons and will be making his 246th career start. He is 9-2 with a 2.62 ERA in 14 career games (13 starts) against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: After giving up three solo home runs in a start at Detroit, Baker worked on making some mechanical adjustments during his windup and those changes paid off in his last start against the Indians. Baker made his third quality start in four outings. Over seven innings, he allowed one run on five hits and struck out a season-high eight. The Twins want Baker to concentrate on keeping pitches down in the zone and making sure that he doesn't give opponents too many chances to hit the ball out of the ballpark. Next up, Baker will face the Rangers in his first career start at Ameriquest Field.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla has made just one of five starts at home so far this season. He lost to Toronto, 8-5, on April 11 when he allowed five runs -- four earned -- on seven hits and three walks in six innings. He is 12-9 with a 4.31 ERA in 29 career starts in Arlington. He was 1-1 with a 4.22 ERA in two starts against the Twins last year and is 1-2 with a 4.32 ERA in his career against them.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez cruised along for the first four innings of his last start in Oakland. But the pitcher found trouble in both the fifth and sixth. Hernandez got some balls up and watched what had been a 3-0 lead quickly disappear into a 4-3 deficit. Hernandez was able to walk away with the no-decision, but the Twins will need him to continue to extend deep into outings and limit the damage. Hernandez will start the last contest of the six-game roadtrip when he faces the Rangers at Ameriquest Field.

home_pitcher_note: Walks once again were the problem for Bonser in his latest start against the A's. The pitcher issued a total of four walks in his outing, including two costly ones. A leadoff walk to Mike Sweeney turned into a run and so did a two-out walk to Daric Barton. Still, Bonser managed to deliver his third quality start of the season, allowing just two runs over six innings. But once again, the starter suffered from a lack of run support. The Twins were shutout against the A's, the fifth straight start by Bonser that the Twin's have scored three runs or fewer. Next up, Bonser will face the White Sox at the Metrodome. He is 1-2 with a 4.24 ERA in six career appearances against Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: Take Floyd's career dominance against the Tigers and move in the other direction to find his lower success rate against a fellow American League Central foe from Minnesota, his opponent to start the White Sox five-game road trip Tuesday at the Metrodome. Floyd has a career 0-2 record in two starts when facing Minnesota, having allowed 10 earned runs on 15 hits over 11 1/3 innings. Five of those hits have gone for home runs, including two by Justin Morneau. Floyd allowed five runs on five hits over six innings during Thursday's twice-rain delayed game, striking out four and walking four. He finished with a no-decision, watching his string of 17 2/3 innings without allowing an earned run come to an end.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander has been one of the most consistent arms for the Twins early this season, but he found trouble with a big inning once again in his last start. Pitching with a 5-0 lead, Blackburn allowed the first seven batters he faced in the third inning to reach base, allowing five runs to score and knotting the game. He would escape the inning without more damage, but the Twins need Blackburn to get rid of that one bad inning -- a problem he's had in two of his five starts. Next up will be Blackburn's second start of the season against the White Sox. In Chicago, he allowed just two runs over seven innings in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Masset is making a spot start for the White Sox, as Ozzie Guillen chose not to use Mark Buehrle or John Danks on three days' rest. Masset has served as the team's middle reliever throughout this season, but he will be making the second start of his young career. He defeated the Cubs last year at Wrigley Field, marking the White Sox lone victory over the North Siders in six regular-season games. Look for Masset to work no more than 75 to 80 pitches, and probably no more than five innings.

home_pitcher_note: The leader of the Twins' starting staff couldn't help the team to save its taxed bullpen in his last start. Hernandez gave up seven earned runs over 2 2/3 innings to the Rangers to pick up his first loss of the season. It was also the first time Hernandez had been unable to pitch at least six innings in a start for the Twins. One other sign of concern is the fact that the right-hander has already shown a penchant for giving up the long ball, allowing a total of six in his last three starts. Next up for Hernandez will be his first start of the year against the Tigers at the Metrodome.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga had another strong outing in his third start after being recalled from Triple-A two weeks ago, this time against an impressive Angels offense. He no-hit them through 5 2/3 innings before Vladimir Guerrero wrecked it with a triple. Galarraga could not get out of the seventh, finishing with three runs allowed -- one earned --  on three hits and two walks. In his three Major League starts this season, he has allowed three earned runs on seven hits in 18 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Baker saw his streak of 12 straight starts in which he held opponents to three runs or less come to an end against the Rangers. Baker allowed five runs over 4 1/3 innings before leaving with a mild groin strain. It's unclear whether that injury might affect his next start, but the pitcher will get an extra day of rest due to the team's number of off-days. Baker's next start would come against the Tigers. The right-hander gave up three runs over seven innings in his lone start vs. Detroit this year.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his first win of the season, Verlander looked sharp through three innings against the Angels, but he ran into trouble in the next three. He allowed one run each in the fourth and fifth, before allowing four in the sixth that knocked him out of the game. Verlander, which many pundits picked to win this year's American League Cy Young award, is off the worst start of his three-year career. He faces Minnesota for the first time this season. Verlander is 3-3 with a 4.00 ERA in six career starts against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander got back to what he does best in his latest start against the Sox and that's use his curveball to offset a strong fastball. It helped Bonser to limit his number of walks, issuing just one over seven innings, and he struck out a season-high eight. Bonser said his biting curve was the best he's had all season. Bonser will now face the Tigers in the three-game series finale. In two career starts against Detroit, Bonser is 2-0 with 3.75 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers earned his first victory at Yankee Stadium in 11 years on Tuesday by holding the Bronx Bombers to two runs over six innings despite walking the bases loaded in the third. He'll try to even his record on the season by continuing his success at the Metrodome, where he's 15-7 with a 3.90 ERA for his career but has only pitched once since joining the Tigers three years ago. He won all three of his starts against the Twins in 2006 but missed them during his injury-shortened 2007 season.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd will have a chance to break his string of bad luck against Minnesota when he faces the Twins at home on Tuesday. Floyd suffered his third loss when facing the Twins in as many career starts, allowing three runs on five hits over six innings during Tuesday's 3-1 setback at the Metrodome. Floyd struck out one and walked three, giving him 15 strikeouts and 15 walks in 31 1/3 innings this season. The big blow against Floyd on Tuesday was Jason Kubel's two-run home run.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander labored a bit in his last start, but he made pitches when necessary. Despite not being completely sharp, Blackburn delivered a quality start, pitching seven innings while allowing three runs on eight hits. Blackburn said that he's pitching better later in outings when some of his adrenaline wears off. The hope is that he can start to transfer that earlier in outings. When Blackburn effectively mixes in his cutter and sinker with a strong curveball and slider, he can be one of the most dangerous pitchers on the Twins staff. He'll face the White Sox for the third time this season. He's 1-0 with a 3.75 ERA in his first two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Facing the Blue Jays in his last start, Buehrle suffered a hard-luck complete-game loss. Over eight innings, the southpaw allowed two unearned runs on five hits, while walking none and striking out seven. In his career against the Twins, Buehrle is 20-10 with a 3.69 ERA. The 20 victories represent the most wins Buehrle has collected against any franchise during his career.
away_pitcher_note: Heading into the season, there were concerns over whether the 10-year National League veteran could handle the more offensively charged lineups in the American League. Hernandez continues to prove there was little reason to worry, as he held one of the most potent lineups, the Tigers', to just one run over seven innings in his last start. Hernandez's location with his fastball was much better in his latest start, and he continues to keep hitters off-balance with his 60 mph Bugs Bunny curveball. Hernandez is set to face the White Sox for the first time in his career, after his first scheduled start in Chicago earlier this season was rained out.

home_pitcher_note: While Danks has enjoyed a strong start to the 2008 campaign, the left-hander struggled in his last start, facing Toronto. The 23-year-old encountered problems with his command, needing 107 pitches to get through his 4 2/3 innings. He allowed two runs and seven hits in the outing, while walking one and striking out five. In four career starts against the Twins, Danks has not fared well, posting a 1-3 record with a 8.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: With Scott Baker'’s strained right groin muscle keeping him a question mark for his next start, the Twins decided to call up Slowey. The right-hander has not pitched in the Majors since April 3, when he left his start after just 3 1/3 innings with a right biceps strain. After letting the injury heal during a DL stint, Slowey headed to the Minors and made three starts there. He last pitched for Triple-A Rochester on May 1, giving up two earned runs over five innings. He allowed two walks and struck out nine. Slowey is 1-0 with a 1.86 ERA in two career starts against Chicago.

home_pitcher_note: After a terrible first inning against the Tigers in which he threw 45 pitches and gave up six runs, Bonser turned into the hero of the game his last time out. The right-hander pitched five consecutive scoreless innings following the first. He retired 17 of the last 19 hitters he faced on just 54 pitches. He attributed it to locating his fastball and gaining control of his off-speed pitches. Bonser will face another tough challenge when he starts the opener of a four-game series against the Red Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Lester snapped a five-start winless streak with his second straight strong outing in a win over the Rays at Fenway Park last Sunday. After going eight innings of one-hit shutout ball in a no-decision against Roy Halladay and the Blue Jays, he struggled at the start but worked six effective innings to beat Tampa Bay. He is 1-0 with a 2.84 ERA in his last four starts. The lefty pitched two scoreless innings of relief against the Twins in the final game of the regular season last year, his only work against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Following the move to put Scott Baker on the disabled list with a strained right groin muscle, the Twins called up Perkins to fill Baker'’s rotation spot. The left-hander struggled early this season with Triple-A Rochester but has settled in recently, going 2-1 with a 2.97 ERA in seven appearances (six starts). Perkins pitched only 28 2/3 innings in the Majors last season after being sidelined with a muscle strain near his left shoulder. The time he’ has spent with the Twins has also been in a relief role; this will be his first career start for Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka did not have his best control in his last start. He allowed just two hits and one earned run in five innings, but he set a new career high with eight walks. He worked out of four two-on jams, disallowing Detroit to put a runner on third base. Matsuzaka has only faced Minnesota once in his short MLB career, but he gave up two runs on six hits in eight innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander hasn't been nearly as sharp in his recent outings as he was to start the season. Blackburn admits that he's not feeling comfortable on the mound right now. Partly to blame is a change in his stride. Last year, the pitcher lengthened his stride and subsequently threw 44 straight scoreless innings for Triple-A Rochester. Somehow over the course of the winter, that stride shortened. Blackburn is trying to re-find it in his bullpen sessions and side work. The hope is he'll have regained it by his next start against the Red Sox. In his lone relief appearance against Boston last season, Blackburn gave up four runs in just one inning.
away_pitcher_note: Wakefield had arguably his best start of the season against the Tigers. He allowed no runs and two hits, while striking out six in eight sharp innings. He allowed just one baserunner in his first six innings. Wakefield has a 13-4 record with a 4.00 ERA in 21 career starts against the Twins. He allowed three earned runs in two starts against them last season.

home_pitcher_note: In his first career start against the White Sox, Hernandez delivered his 44th complete game. The crafty veteran held Chicago to just one run on seven hits with the lone run coming on a  Jermaine Dye solo homer. Mixing in pitches ranging from 59 mph to 85 mph, Hernandez has been teaching the younger arms in the Twins rotation how to keep lineups off-balance by changing speeds. The hope is that Hernandez can do the same in his next start against the Red Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Buchholz did not look good in his last start. After winning two of his last three starts, he earned a no-decision, allowing five runs on 10 hits in just four innings in his first career start against the mighty Tigers' lineup. Buchholz let in four runs in the third and one in the fourth to put the Red Sox in a hole. Buchholz faces the Twins for the first time in his short career on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey cruised through four innings of his first start back with the Twins, retiring 12 of the first 13 White Sox batters he faced. But it was a rough fifth inning that cost Slowey his second loss in as many starts this season. The right-hander gave up three runs, all coming off two home runs he gave up in that fifth inning. Slowey left pitches up in that inning, a problem that has plagued him in previous starts, and he'll need to keep from doing that when he faces the Blue Jays for just the second time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: On Thursday, Litsch picked up a no-decision after giving up three runs on five hits over seven innings for the Jays. The right-hander also issued no walks, giving him a streak of 21 1/3 straight innings without a free pass. That's the longest such streak for a Toronto pitcher since Jimmy Key lasted 35 2/3 consecutive innings without walking a batter in 1990. Litsch is 1-0 with a 3.18 ERA in two career games against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Despite giving up six runs in each of his last two starts, Bonser has failed to pick up a loss in either thanks to some late clutch hitting by the Twins. The right-hander entered his last start against the Red Sox tied for the lowest run support in the American League (2.57). But while he got more runs this time, Bonser admitted that he battled through his four-plus innings against Boston and struggled to make pitches when it counted. He'll have to try and improve upon that against the Blue Jays, a team he’s 0-2 against with a 6.17 ERA in two career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay was dominant through the first six innings of his last outing, limiting the Indians to no runs on three hits and striking out nine over that stretch. In the seventh inning on Friday, though, Halladay loaded the bases with no outs, opening the door for a six-run outburst by Cleveland. Halladay took the loss after being charged with four runs on six hits with three walks in six-plus frames. He is 6-0 with a 2.66 ERA in 10 career games against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start, Perkins looked to be quite comfortable on the mound, commanding the strike zone with a dominating sinker against a difficult Red Sox lineup. The problem was his penchant for giving up the long ball. All three of the runs Perkins allowed came courtesy of solo homers. He allowed nine hits over his six-plus innings and struck out three. Next up for Perkins will be the Blue Jays, a team that, like the Twins, ranks near the bottom of the Majors in home runs hit (24).
away_pitcher_note: On Saturday, McGowan suffered his worst outing of the season, yielding nine runs on nine hits over 3 2/3 innings in a loss to the Indians. The right-hander surrendered a six-spot in the first inning and finished with one strikeout, one walk and one hit batsmen. It was a disastrous outing that followed a pair of stellar starts for McGowan, who had given up just one run over his previous 14 2/3 innings. McGowan is 1-0 with a 0.00 ERA in two career games against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander didn't allow many hits in his last start, but a three-run homer to Adrian Gonzalez proved to be the back-breaker. Jimenez allowed three runs on five hits and three walks with a career-high 11 strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings to take the loss for his first decision in his last five starts. His lone win came at home against the Braves on April 15 and Jimenez has failed to get past six innings in seven of his eight starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn earned his third victory of the season in a 9-6 victory over the Red Sox on Sunday. At times the right-hander struggled, but worked through six innings, giving up four earned runs on nine hits. He also struck out five batters, walked one and hit two batters. The Twins rookie showed some grit in working out of two jams that could have led to big innings for Boston. He will look to build on his success as Minnesota opens up Interleague Play against the Rockies on Friday in Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old right-hander was not in awe of big leaguers in his Major League debut and will likely get another shot. The Rockies have optioned left-hander Mark Redman to Triple-A Colorado Springs to get regular work and are hoping Reynolds can pitch well enough to keep the spot in the rotation. Reynolds allowed four runs on six hits and two walks with a strikeout, but also gave up two homers to take the loss.
away_pitcher_note: The Twins knew that they were getting an innings-eater when they signed Hernandez at the start of Spring Training. But he's been even better than expected to start the year. Hernandez picked up his sixth win of the season, holding the Red Sox to just three runs on 10 hits over six innings. He didn't get his sixth win in 2007 until July 24. The Twins are now 8-1 in games that Hernandez starts, giving the team lots of confidence when he's on the mound. He's gotten his fair share of run support too, but he'll have the chance to help his own cause when he faces the Rockies at Coors Field in Interleague Play. Renowned for his bat, Hernandez is a career .232 hitter with nine home runs in 789 at-bats.

home_pitcher_note: Francis gave up 13 hits, matching a career high, and eight runs in 4 2/3 innings of a loss at Arizona on Tuesday night. He left insisting he pitched better than his numbers. It was true that a number of the hits were soft, but his difficulties pitching inside against right-handed hitters and the slight location misses with his fastball and changeup were every bit as much a problem. After a good three-start string, Francis has given up 25 hits in 15 innings over his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey was effective if not efficient in his last start. The right-hander allowed just three runs over his 5 2/3 innings, throwing a total of 107 pitches in that span. The Blue Jays put together some long at-bats against Slowey, raising him pitch count quickly. Home runs also continue to be a problem. He's given up 20 homers over 16 career appearances. For his next start he'll face the Rockies for the first time in his career at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time in his last three starts, Bonser suffered through a disastrous first inning. This time Bonser gave up a grand slam to the Blue Jays DH, Matt Stairs, to put the Twins in a big hole. He would recover to allow just one more run over his final five innings. But the Twins seem to be getting frustrated with Bonser's inability to stop yanking the ball early in his starts. That tendency to overthrow has hurt Bonser and the feeling is that only he can correct the problem. He'll get his next chance when he faces the Rangers for the first time this season.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman is making just his second start on the road this season. He pitched six scoreless innings against the Athletics on May 4 in Oakland, but allowed three runs in the seventh and ended up losing, 3-1. He has made one relief appearance against the Twins, giving up three runs in two innings on April 26 at the Ballpark. He has a 5.79 ERA in six career relief appearances against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins pitched six strong innings in a 3-2, extra-inning loss to Toronto on Thursday and didn't figure into the decision. In the outing he gave up two runs on five hits, walked two and struck out a career-high six batters. Perkins has given the Twins a chance to win in each of his first two career starts this season since being called up from Triple-A Rochester. He will face the Texas Rangers in the second game of a three-game series at the Metrodome on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: After three relief appearances, Mathis is making his first Major League start. He earned it on May 12 with a scoreless inning of relief against the Mariners in a 13-12 victory. He was the first Rangers reliever to get his first Major League victory in his debut appearance. He was 5-0 with a 3.55 ERA in seven starts for Triple-A Oklahoma before being called to the Major Leagues.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander has started to show progress, after hitting a bit of a skid recently. Blackburn pitched seven innings against the Rockies, allowing just two runs on six hits. He didn't issue a single walk and struck out five. The Twins have been wanting Blackburn to slow down and not overthrow when he gets into trouble. Something he did in the one inning where the Rockies tagged him for runs. After giving up two straight hits, he settled down to get key outs and mixed in all of his pitches. Next up for Blackburn is a start against the Rangers. He received a no-decision in his only start against the club this season, allowing five runs over six innings to Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Ponson is facing one for his former teams. He pitched for the Twins in 2007 and made seven starts, going 2-5 with a 6.93 ERA before he was released. This is only his second start on the road this season. He beat the Mariners, 10-1, on May 6, holding them to one run in seven innings. He is 9-2 with a 2.56 ERA against the Twins in his career, his lowest ERA against any American League team.

home_pitcher_note: In his return to National League action, Hernandez looked very much at ease. He held the Rockies to just three runs on eight hits over 7 1/3 innings. All of that damage after Hernandez carried a perfect game into the sixth inning. The veteran pitcher continues to baffle hitters with his slow curveball around 60 mph and his fastball registering at 85 mph. Next up will be his second start of the season against the Rangers and the challenge will be to see if he can improve from that last outing vs. Texas. Hernandez gave up seven runs over 2 2/3 innings to the Rangers on April 27 in Arlington, in what was clearly his worst start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla has won four consecutive decisions after allowing two runs in seven innings against Houston on Saturday. Padilla has a 1.60 ERA for his last five starts. He has been automatic when he reaches 100 pitches. Padilla is 5-0 with a no-decision in his six starts where he has thrown more than 100 pitches. The win against the Astros matched his win total from last season. The Rangers are 8-2 when Padilla starts.

home_pitcher_note: With Dontrelle Willis heading to the bullpen for now, Galarraga remains in Detroit's rotation, where his ability to throw strikes and avoid serious damage has allow the Tigers to win five of his six starts. Four of those outings have been quality starts, tying him with Kenny Rogers for the team lead. One of those, however, was his only loss of the season, to the Twins on May 2 at the Metrodome, where two of his four runs allowed were unearned in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander appeared to make more progress in his latest start, despite picking up his fourth straight loss. Slowey allowed just three runs on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings to the Rockies in his first Interleague start at Coors Field. It was a bit of a laborious outing though for Slowey, as he threw 109 pitches in that time. The pitcher said his goal in his next start will be to make more pitches down in the zone. He'll get to test that in Detroit when he faces the Tigers for the first time this season. Slowey is 1-0 with a 6.00 ERA in one career start at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson retired 10 of the first 11 batters he faced and didn't allow a hit until the fourth inning in his latest outing Sunday at Arizona. A two-run fifth and two more in the sixth, however, sent him to defeat and continued the roughest start to a season in his big-league career.
away_pitcher_note: Bonser gave up more than one home run in a start for the first time this season, allowing two solo shots to the Rangers over his 6 1/3 innings Monday. Bonser delivered his sixth quality start of the season only allowing three earned runs in the outing. He ran into some late trouble against the Rangers which forced him out of the  game in the seventh. Bonser got back on track by rectifying a problem from earlier this season of overthrowing the ball. The right-hander had five strikeouts and did not issue a walk. Bonser will next take the mound Saturday at Comerica Park in the middle of a three-game set against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander made one of his best starts in his baffling year against the Mariners on Tuesday. He gave up a single and a home run in the first inning, but he allowed only two hits over the next five frames. He gave the Mariners a steady helping of offspeed pitches, which helped him post a season-high seven strikeouts. Verlander faced Minnesota once this season, a loss that saw him allow four earned runs on seven hits in seven innings. For his career, he has a 3-4 record and 4.19 ERA in seven starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins struck out three and didn't walk a batter in 6 1/3 strong innings Tuesday during an 11-4 victory over Texas. It was Perkins' third consecutive quality start. The lefty sailed through six scoreless innings before getting into trouble in the seventh by throwing up in the zone. Perkins was deceptive throughout, primarily relying on his changeup as an out pitch but effectively mixing the rest of his repertoire. He has been solid since being recalled from the minors after not making the team out of Spring Training. Next up for Perkins is a road start at Detroit on Sunday which will cap a three-game series.

home_pitcher_note: That unusual day-split that Bannister had going was shredded last Thursday afternoon at Boston. He'd been 4-0 without allowing a home run in day games (and 0-5 at night with six homers) until J.D. Drew blasted a grand slam. Now that Bannister is 4-1 in the daylight maybe he can finally post a victory on his nocturnal record in this game. The thinking man's pitcher, his latest concern in that he might be tipping pitches somehow with runners on base because he's been getting hammered in those situations. He's got the matter under study. In three starts against the Twins last year he was 2-0 with a 2.05 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander had an interesting outing Wednesday against Texas. While his team lost, 10-1, and Blackburn surrendered 10 hits total while being touched for a seven-run sixth inning, only one of those runs was earned after a key Alexi Casilla error. Blackburn has struck out nine and walked only one in his last two outings after experiencing a recent mini-skid. Blackburn will next take the mound Tuesday at Kansas City in the first contest of a three-game set. Blackburn hasn't faced the Royals this season, but he pitched 2 2/3 scoreless innings at Kauffman  Stadium on Sept. 10 during a 4-2 Twins victory.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke suffered his worst start of the season on Friday against the Blue Jays. The right-hander allowed a season-high six runs on nine hits over five innings. Prior to that start, Greinke had not allowed more than three runs in an outing this season. He has also allowed nine hits in each of his last three starts. In his career against the Twins, he is 2-3 with a 3.65 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The big right-hander is happy Texas has left town. Hernandez struggled for the second time this season against the Rangers on Thursday, going 5 1/3 innings and surrendering five earned runs, including four in the first inning. Hernandez had earlier given up seven runs over 2 2/3 innings to the Rangers on April 27 in Arlington. Hernandez will look to continue his mastery over the Royals this season. The right-hander has already faced Kansas City twice this season, winning both starts and allowing a combined four runs over 14 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar suffered his second straight loss on Saturday against the Blue Jays. He allowed a first-inning grand slam to Jays outfielder Brad Wilkerson, but did manage to settle down for the rest of his outing. He finished his day allowing five runs -- four earned -- on six hits over six innings. In his seven starts this season, the Royals have scored just 10 runs.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey finally got his fist win of the season in a masterful performance against the Detroit Tigers at Comerica Park on Friday. He pitched six shutout innings, allowing only four hits. He kept Tigers' hitters off balance as he changed speeds and worked on both corners of the plate. He only allowed two base runners in the same inning twice.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins was outstanding in his last outing, a 6-1 win over the Detroit Tigers at Comerica Park on May 25. He only allowed a run, on Carlos Guillen's home run, and seven hits in 7 2/3 innings. He walked two and struck out four. He established the inside half of the plate and then moved the ball in and out using his curve and changeup to keep the Tigers off balance.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching against the Mariners last Saturday afternoon, Mussina erased some of the ugliness of his previous start -- but not all of it. He gave up four runs in five innings, leaving after 74 pitches in part due to ineffectiveness, but mostly due to the Yankees' plan to use Joba Chamberlain for 45 pitches worth of relief. Still, it was an improvement from his previous start, in which Mussina could not escape the first inning. His next start comes in Minnesota, where he is 10-5 with a 3.42 ERA for his career.

home_pitcher_note: Bonser is still a member of the Twins' rotation. However, his job security is a bit shaky at this point. Bonser fell to 0-2 and raised his ERA to 9.29 for the month of May after getting pounded by the Tigers on Saturday at Comerica Park. The 26-year-old gave up a season-high nine earned runs in a season-short three innings of work, as Detroit cruised to a 19-3 victory. To add insult to injury, Bonser committed his second error of the season while remaining winless since April 29.
away_pitcher_note: Wang will try to turn around a recent trend as he takes the mound against the Twins at the Metrodome, looking to improve on his last two starts, when he allowed 12 runs in 14 innings. He took a no-decision on May 25 vs. Seattle but did not pitch particularly well, allowing five runs on seven hits over 6 1/3 innings, including four walks. After rocketing to a 6-0 start, Wang has not won since May 2 vs. Seattle, but he beat the Twins in his only start against them in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander delivered his longest outing of the season, holding the Royals scoreless for 8 1/3 innings. But he would walk away with a no-decision after leaving runners on first and second when he departed the game. Kansas City tallied two runs while scattering eight hits off Blackburn, who delivered his seventh quality start of the season. Blackburn will next face the Yankees for the first time in his career. He is 3-2 with a 2.41 ERA in five starts at the Metrodome this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rasner suffered his first loss of the season on May 26 in hard-luck fashion, blanking the Orioles over the first five innings before allowing a solo home run to Nick Markakis with one out in the sixth. It was the first run Rasner had allowed to the Orioles through 12 1/3 innings this season and, when the Yankees allowed five runs in relief, cemented his first defeat of an overall impressive campaign thus far. Rasner breaks in June for the Yankees against the Twins, whom he has not faced since 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Despite walking away with a no-decision in his third start against the Royals this season, Hernandez found trouble against Kansas City. He allowed eight runs (six earned) on 13 hits over six-plus innings. The 13 hits were the most that Hernandez has allowed since May 30, 2001 against Arizona while pitching for the Giants. It was also the most hits allowed by a Twins starter this season. Hernandez will see if he can recover against the Yankees. He's 4-0 with a 4.23 ERA in six starts at the Metrodome this year.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte draws the call, looking for his third consecutive victory, wrapping up a four-game series at the Metrodome. He last pitched on Wednesday at Baltimore and limited the Orioles to two runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings, improving to 5-5 after he'd gone 0-4 with a no-decision from April 25 to May 17. Pettitte last faced the Twins on April 10, 2007, at the Metrodome, and got the win in a 10-1 decision.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey picked up his second straight victory as he pitched his first career complete game against the Royals. The right-hander held Kansas City to just one run on six hits, with his lone run coming in the ninth inning. Slowey did not issue a single walk and showed the kind of solid command that he was known for during his rapid rise through the Minor Leagues. Slowey will next face the Orioles, a team he has never faced in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The Orioles called up Liz to start on Tuesday, taking the rotation slot vacated by Steve Trachsel. Liz was pulled after an inning in his most recent start to save his arm, and since contingency plan Matt Albers pitched in relief on Monday, Liz got the nod to make his season debut.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins struggled in his last outing, a 6-5 loss against the Yankees at the Metrodome on Friday. He allowed a career-high five runs and 10 hits in the game. It was the first start of his career in which he did not log at least six innings. He lasted four against New York. Perkins said after the game that he and catcher Joe Mauer had a good game plan entering the game, but that he had difficulty hitting his spots. Perkins will next take on Baltimore, against whom he has never started. The young lefty made two relief appearances against the Orioles in September 2006, securing two outs total in the appearances while surrendering two hits, but no runs.
away_pitcher_note: Cabrera pitched seven strong innings against Boston his last time out, giving him nine quality starts in his last 10 outings. The right-hander's walk-rate has been reduced by nearly a full walk per nine innings from last season, and he no longer seems to be a threat to lead the league in free passes. Cabrera has been working deep in games and is a solid bet to crack 200 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Baker has taken the rotation spot formerly occupied by Boof Bonser, who was sent to the bullpen after compiling a 2-6 record with a 5.97 ERA. Baker strained his groin throwing a pitch to Michael Young in Arlington and aggravated it during his next start against Detroit on May 3. He hasn't pitched since. Baker will take the hill in the final contest of a three-game set against Baltimore at the Metrodome. He last started against the Orioles on Aug. 26, going six innings and allowing two earned runs in an 11-3 Minnesota victory. The Twins are 5-1 in his six starts in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Olson only lasted five innings in his last start, and he gave up back-to-back home runs to two Boston batters. The southpaw had only allowed two homers in a start one other time in his big league career -- and that came in his second career outing. Olson has completed five innings in six of his seven starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez reached double-digit strikeouts for the 34th time in his career, fanning 10 against the Rays on Saturday night, but it still wasn't enough to prevent his fourth loss of the season. Vazquez allowed five hits over seven innings, one being a home run to Cliff Floyd, during the 2-0 setback. He has 77 strikeouts in 78 2/3 innings in 12 starts during the 2008 campaign. Vazquez has a 1-0 record with a 3.86 ERA in his one start against Minnesota this season. He has a 5-5 record lifetime against the Twins. Justin Morneau has been tough on Vazquez with a .361 average, six career home runs and 12 RBIs.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander was knocked out of his last start after being struck in the face with a line drive off the bat of Bobby Abreu. He had pitched well up until that point, going 4 1/3 innings while surrendering one earned run on five hits. Previously, Blackburn had delivered his longest outing of the season, holding the Royals scoreless for 8 1/3 innings. Blackburn's next start will kick off a three-game series on the road. He has already faced Chicago three times this season, most recently giving up three earned runs in six innings on May 6. Blackburn is 1-1 against the White Sox this year.

home_pitcher_note: The Rays scored all three of their runs off Buehrle during a six-pitch stretch in the fifth inning, knocking out a single, double and triple in consecutive at-bats. Buehrle stranded Gabe Gross at third, eventually leaving after six innings and 102 pitches with a no-decision. Buehrle allowed seven hits, striking out five, and moving within 15 of 1,000 strikeouts for his career. Buehrle has an 0-1 record with an 11.12 ERA against the Twins this year, but his lifetime mark of 20-11 stands as the most career wins for the left-hander against any individual team. Craig Monroe has a .389 average and two career home runs against Buehrle, while Michael Cuddyer has driven home seven against the White Sox left-handed ace. He has one win in his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Livan Hernandez labored on Monday against the Yankees, but he worked himself out of trouble and kept his team in the game. The Twins ended up winning 6-5. The veteran right-hander went six innings and allowed five earned runs on 13 hits. Hernandez has now allowed 13 hits in consecutive starts. His next start will come at Chicago. He will look to get back on track against the White Sox, whom he pitched a complete game against on May 7. The Twins rolled 13-1. He scattered nine hits while allowing one earned run.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd won his second consecutive start Tuesday against the Royals. He allowed four runs -- two earned -- over seven innings. He also hasn't walked a single batter in his last two starts, thereby helping his own cause. It was his eighth quality start of the season. Floyd has faced Minnesota twice this year, with quality performances in both, but with mixed results. He lost his first matchup with the Twins, giving up three runs over six innings, but nearly no-hit them a week later, allowing one hit over 8 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey struggled a bit keeping the ball down in the zone during his last outing. He allowed four earned runs on seven hits to the Orioles, picking up his first loss in his past three starts. The pitcher gave up two home runs in his start, marking the ninth time in his career that Slowey has given up two-or-more homers in an outing. Next up will be a start against the White Sox. Slowey gave up three runs over five innings in his lone start vs. Chicago at U.S. Cellular Field this season.

home_pitcher_note: Danks continues to pitch well, but often struggles to get deep into games. He lasted 5 2/3 innings against the Royals on Wednesday and allowed two runs on six hits and two walks. He hasn't managed to get through the seventh inning since his start on April 20 against the Rays. But, he hasn't allowed more than three earned runs since April 9, when Minnesota roughed him up for seven runs. He's faced the Twins one other time this season and picked up a win, allowing two runs over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: It was a difficult night on the mound for Perkins in his last start. He lasted just four innings against the Orioles, giving up four earned runs on nine hits. That included back-to-back, solo home runs with two outs in the first. The southpaw walked two and struck out two as he threw 77 pitches in that span. Next up for Perkins will be his first career start against the White Sox. In three relief appearances against Chicago, Perkins is 0-0 with a 2.70 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The hitting-friendly elements of Rangers Ballpark and a costly fielding error made behind him might have contributed to his demise, but it was nonetheless apparent Sabathia wasn't quite as dominant in Texas on Thursday as he had been recently. In six innings, he gave up five runs, four of which were earned, on nine hits with three walks and eight strikeouts. Before the outing, Sabathia had posted a 2.01 ERA over his previous eight starts. He'll look to get back to that trend in the comforts of home against a Twins team he has yet to face this year. Sabathia was 4-1 with a 1.51 ERA in five starts against Minnesota last year.
away_pitcher_note: Baker reclaimed his spot in the rotation on Thursday. He was effective, going five innings and giving up two earned runs to get the no-decision in a 3-2 loss. Baker didn't appear to be bothered by the strained groin that put him on the 15-day disabled list. Baker went seven innings and allowed only one run while striking out eight against the Indians on April 20, a 2-1 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd earned his 100th career win Friday the way he earned the vast majority of the others. He worked ahead, mixed up his pitches, commanded the ball to both sides of the plate and generally left the Tigers perplexed for seven innings in which he allowed just two runs on four hits with no walks and two strikeouts. Byrd needed just 80 pitches to get through the outing. But he's still having trouble keeping the ball in the yard. He gave up another two homers to bring his league-leading total to 16. Byrd held the Twins to a run on six hits in seven innings in a no-decision on April 20.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start since taking a Bobby Abreu line drive to the face, Blackburn appeared on track early to perhaps make up for his streak of failed wins. Instead, he found trouble �- and lots of it �- in the fifth inning. Blackburn allowed five straight hits before being pulled, giving up a total of seven earned runs on eight hits in his four-plus innings. Next up for Blackburn will be his second start of the year against the Indians. The right-hander held the Indians scoreless for 7 2/3 innings in that start at the Metrodome on April 19.

home_pitcher_note: Injuries this season to Jake Westbrook and Fausto Carmona have allowed Laffey to claim a rotation spot, but he's certainly earned the position. After enduring his first rough start of the season in Texas, he rebounded nicely against the Tigers on Saturday, giving up just two runs on six hits with two walks and two strikeouts in 6 2/3 innings. Laffey has the confidence and ability to get out of jams with his grounder-inducing sinkerball. He's held the opposition to two runs or less in six of his eight starts. Laffey went 0-1 with a 7.71 ERA in two starts against the Twins last year.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching a near shutout against the White Sox in his first start vs. the club, Hernandez struggled mightily in his second outing at Chicago. The right-hander allowed seven earned runs on eight hits over just four innings. Next up for Hernandez will be to face the only team in the Majors he's never pitched against, the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: When Bush gets through the first inning, he's usually OK. In his 11 first innings this season, opponents have batted .319 (15-for-47) with four doubles, five home runs and seven walks. He has surrendered more runs (11), hits and homers in the first inning than in any other frame. Bush has surrendered a first-inning homer in each of his last three starts, including two on Saturday at Coors Field, a grand slam to Brad Hawpe and a Chris Iannetta solo shot on the next pitch. Bush has surrendered a first-inning homer four times this season, but before Saturday, all of those games ended in Brewers wins. Bush is 2-1 with a 3.45 ERA in his five Miller Park starts, vs. 0-5 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey continued a recent rough patch for the Twins' starting staff, lasting just three innings and giving up eight runs in a 12-2 loss to the White Sox. The right-hander allowed 10 hits and gave up one home run. It marked the ninth time this season that Slowey has given up a long ball. Prior to this rough start, Slowey had gone 2-1 with a 2.14 ERA in his previous three outings. Next up for the pitcher is the Brewers, facing them for only the second time in his career. In his first start against Milwaukee, Slowey allowed four earned runs over his 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Relievers Carlos Villanueva and Salomon Torres preserved Suppan's second straight win on Sunday at Coors Field, each escaping one-out jams with the tying runner on third base. Suppan pitched the first 5 1/3 innings and was not necessarily efficient, but limited the Rockies to two runs, only one of them earned, on four hits. It was just his second road win in eight starts, but Suppan has been very good at Miller Park, where he is 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander delivered a solid, if somewhat short outing —against the White Sox in his last start. Perkins allowed three runs on five hits over his 5 1/3 innings. Perkins hasn't pitched a full six innings in each of his last three starts. He's been getting back to pitching more inside -- something that made him effective early in his return to the Twins. Next up for Perkins will be his first career appearance vs. Milwaukee. He's 1-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: McClung was fighting a stomach flu when he pitched against the Astros on Tuesday, twice running to the bathroom to get sick. You wouldn't know by the results, as the right-hander limited Houston to three hits including Lance Berkman's short-porch home run in a disappointing Brewers loss. It was McClung's second so-called "quality" start of at least six innings with three or fewer runs and his fourth start since moving to the rotation from the bullpen. He threw 85 pitches, a season-high.
away_pitcher_note: In just his second start following a month-long stint on the DL with a strained groin muscle, Baker looked much more like himself. He limited the Indians to just one run on eight hits over seven innings to deliver the Twins' first quality start in 12 games. Baker still picked up the loss when the Twins were shut out in the game. The right-hander will now head to Milwaukee, where he delivered a gem of a start in his return to the rotation last season. He pitched 8 1/3 innings, allowing two runs on six hits.

home_pitcher_note: After a very solid start to the year, Hernandez has started to look like a much different pitcher recently. He struggled mightily in his first career start against the Indians, giving up seven runs on 12 hits over just three-plus innings. It was the fifth straight start that he had been tagged for at least five earned runs. He's now allowed 136 hits on the season, putting him in line become the first Major League pitcher to give up more than 300 hits in a single season since Phil Niekro, who allowed 311 for Atlanta in 1979. Hernandez will next face a former team of his, the Nationals, in Interleague Play. He is 6-5 with a 4.19 ERA in 12 career appearances vs. Washington.
away_pitcher_note: The first time Lannan faced the Pirates in May, he made it only three innings into the game. The second time in June, he went out and threw six quality innings, giving up only two runs on seven hits. He said he wanted to establish his territory with his fastball. He did just that by throwing 61 of his 93 pitches for strikes. Lannan has yet to face Minnesota during his two-year career.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey rebounded from two so-so starts to deliver a stellar performance in the Twins' series opener against the Brewers. The right-hander allowed just two runs on five hits over eight innings in the start, but he provided almost as much support with his bat by tallying two RBIs on the night. For only the third time this season, Slowey kept the ball in the park and did not give up a single home run. He'll try to repeat that trend when he faces the Nationals in the series finale, marking his first career appearance against the club.
away_pitcher_note: Bergman's struggles continued again the Pirates in his last start on June 12. The Bucs connected for eight hits and six runs to knock the right hander out of the game after 4 2/3 innings. Bergman has now given up 18 hits and 11 runs in his last two starts. He has not faced Seattle in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins delivered his fifth quality start of the season in his last outing against the Brewers in Milwaukee. He pitched six innings, giving up three runs on eight hits. Perkins walked just one in his start and struck out six, tying his career-high. One thing the left-hander could work on is limiting his pitch count. He threw a total of 93 pitches over his six innings. Next up for Perkins will be his first start against the Diamondbacks at the Metrodome. The Minnesota native has struggled at home this season, going 1-2 with a 5.47 ERA in five starts there.
away_pitcher_note: Hill picked up his first win since Sept. 10, 2007, after getting plenty of run support early against the Mariners. Hill allowed 12 hits but just four earned runs -- five total -- over five innings and got plenty of backup from the bullpen as the Nationals took a game in Seattle, winning, 7-6. Hill also struck out three.

home_pitcher_note: Baker became the first Twins pitcher to record four strikeouts in an inning in his last start against the Brewers. In his second straight quality start where he pitched six innings and allowed just three runs, Baker tied his career high for strikeouts with nine. The right-hander has started to find his form following a month-long absence from the rotation due to a groin strain. Next up for Baker will be his first career start against the Diamondbacks at the Metrodome. He is 1-0 with a 2.49 ERA in four starts there this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Big Unit was roughed up in his last outing, allowing eight runs (seven earned) and 10 hits to the Kansas City Royals. In recent outings, Johnson had been the victim of a lack of run support and poor defensive play behind him, but against the Royals, he was flat out roughed up. For Johnson, who hasn't won since May 18, it was his third consecutive loss after starting the season 4-1.

home_pitcher_note: Unlike his previous start against the White Sox in which he found trouble with a big inning, Blackburn avoided such problems against the Indians. The right-hander delivered his seventh quality start of the season, pitching six innings and allowing just two runs on seven hits in his outing at Progressive Field. Blackburn will now return home to face the Nationals for the first time in his career. The Metrodome has been kind to Blackburn this season, as he's 3-2 with a 6.37 ERA in six starts there.
away_pitcher_note: Owings has had a string of four consecutive poor outings. He has allowed 21 runs the last 19 innings for an ERA of 9.94, raising his season ERA to 5.18. Against the Royals, he was one batter away from escaping a fifth inning unscathed, but allowed a grand slam to David DeJesus, as part of his seven earned runs. Owings has never faced the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez went seven innings on Tuesday against Washington, giving up one earned run on five hits. He struck out only one but didn't surrender a walk. The Twins won 2-1. It was a needed quality start for Hernandez, who was 6-1 record with a 3.90 ERA on May 13, but had since struggled mightily. In his last six starts, the veteran had sputtered to an 0-3 record with a 9.38 ERA. After lengthy bullpen sessions with pitching coach Rick Anderson, Hernandez believes he has everything ironed out. He will rely less on his fastball and more on his slider and sinker. The veteran will next get a shot at Arizona, with whom he pitched last season.
away_pitcher_note: Webb was roughed up in his last outing against the A's at Chase Field. The right-hander felt like he had his good stuff when he warmed up, but the A's wound up scoring seven runs against him in just 3 1/3 innings. Webb lacked the command that he typically has particularly when it came to his sinker. After walking six guys in his previous eight starts, Webb allowed five free passes. In his start before that, he was removed after just five innings against the Mets as the D-backs tried to give him a bit of a breather since his velocity had recently been down.

home_pitcher_note: Peavy allowed three earned runs in four innings in his second start since coming off the disabled list, an 8-5 loss at Yankee Stadium on June 18. Peavy wasn't so much hit hard as he was hurt by a high pitch count that was a result of deep counts and no shortage of fly balls. Peavy walked two and struck out four and said his elbow, which caused him to go on the disabled list last month, felt fine. Peavy threw 54 pitches over the first two innings alone.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey made it two straight quality starts with another strong performance in his last outing against the Nationals. Slowey held Washington to just one run on seven hits over his six innings. His lone run came in the fifth inning on a home run by Felipe Lopez. Home runs have been common for Slowey. He's given up 26 over 23 career appearances, including 24 in his 21 starts. He'll try to see if he can keep that number from increasing in his next start against the Padres in San Diego. It will be the first time Slowey has ever faced the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Maddux will move up a day in the rotation to stay on regular rest. The right-hander allowed a run on five hits and a walk over seven innings for a no-decision against the Tigers in his last start. Maddux has been stuck on 350 career wins since getting past the milestone May 10. In eight succeeding starts. Maddux is 0-1. He has one career start against the Twins. The result? A no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins worked his way out of several jams in his last start against Washington on Thursday at the Metrodome. The left-hander went eight innings, allowed 10 hits and three earned runs, but was in trouble during four of those innings. He was aided by a strong defense and an ability to make pitches with runners on base. He will have to cut his pitch count down, as he threw 106 pitches against Washington after throwing 93 in his previous start. He will next take the hill in Interleague Play on Wednesday at San Diego.

home_pitcher_note: Banks continues to pitch well as a fill-in for a starting rotation that is still missing Chris Young and Shawn Estes (both are on the disabled list). Banks allowed two runs on just four hits in his last start against the Yankees on June 19. He was hurt more by the four stolen bases the Yankees swiped (two ended up coming around to score) than any one particular hit, though Alex Rodriguez's RBI single in the sixth inning broke a tie. Banks, a waiver wire claim from the Blue Jays for $20,000 last month, has allowed six earned runs in 25 1/3 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Baker outdueled veteran Randy Johnson in his last start. The Twins defeated the Diamondbacks, 7-2, as Baker went six innings, striking out seven while allowing only one earned run Friday at the Metrodome. The right-hander has found his stride following a month-long absence due to a groin strain.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn was very effective against Arizona in his last start, going seven innings and allowing only one earned run on three hits, a 6-1 Twins victory.
