Blackburn mixed his fastball, curveball, slider and changeup effectively to keep the D-backs off balance. Blackburn will next have a home start against Milwaukee in the Metrodome. It will be his first career start against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: McClung has really found a home in the Brewers rotation and solidified his spot on the team since moving over from the bullpen in late May. In his last start, McClung threw 6 2/3 innings, not allowing a hit until the fifth, and gave up two runs in picking up his fifth win of the season. The big righty is now 5-3 with a 3.79 ERA on the season, but McClung is still not taking anything for granted. "I feel like I can be replaced at any time," McClung said. "That keeps me hungry."

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez had a happy reunion against Arizona on Sunday, going seven innings while only allowing one earned run on nine hits. It was the second consecutive quality start for Hernandez, who has experienced more success by relying less on his fastball and more on his slider and sinker. Hernandez's next start will come against the Brewers, whom he has not faced this year.
away_pitcher_note: Parra is coming off a performance in which he scuffled badly, but was able to battle through it and come away with a win. Parra managed to make it through five innings and allowed three runs, but the damage could have been much worse. The lefty walked six batters and gave up five hits, but the Brewers bats saved him. Four home runs -- two by Prince Fielder -- and stellar defensive play in the infield took Parra off the hook for the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey delivered his third straight quality start, pitching six scoreless innings against the Padres at PETCO Park. He scattered just four hits in the outing and did not walk a single batter while striking out a season-high seven batters. Slowey has continued to look more comfortable on the mound after a rough start to the season. He was 0-4 with a 5.49 ERA in his first four starts. Slowey will now face the Brewers for the second time this month. He picked up the victory in that contest after allowing just two runs over eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets threw his National League-leading third complete game of the season on Monday against the Braves. He allowed four hits, struck out seven and retired the last 16 batters he faced. Sheets has now won five straight decisions. He has pitched at least six innings in 10 consecutive starts, and in 13 of 15 starts this season. Sheets is 1-1 with a 2.18 ERA in three career starts against the Twins. He last pitched against Minnesota on June 18, 2004, when he allowed one run on four hits in six innings and got the win. In 20 2/3 innings against the Twins, he has allowed five runs.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins had to work to get through five innings against the Padres, despite giving up only three runs. The left-hander threw a total of 91 pitches in that span, scattering six hits while walking two and striking out two. A strong night defensively behind Perkins aided the pitcher, who will next face the Tigers at the Metrodome. Perkins won his only other start against Detroit earlier this season, allowing just one run on seven hits over 7 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga gave up five runs over 4 2/3 innings, including three solo home runs, on Wednesday against the Cardinals before a rain delay knocked him out of the game. Now he'll get back to American League competition with his third matchup against the Twins this year. Both of his previous meetings with Minnesota have been losses, with seven earned runs allowed on 13 hits and seven walks over 12 innings. He had won three consecutive starts before the Cardinals roughed him up.

home_pitcher_note: Some early troubles plagued Baker in his last start as he gave up three runs over his first three innings to the Padres. But while it wasn't the prettiest of outings, Baker managed to settle down to hold them to just those three runs on six hits over six innings. The Twins are still hoping to see Baker's pitch counts go down, as he threw 101 over that span. Next up for Baker will be his third start of the year against Detroit.  He is 0-0, having allowed just four runs over 10 innings in the first two starts. He's had success at the Metrodome this season, going 2-0 with a 2.28 ERA in five starts there.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson, one of the Tigers' most consistent pitchers during their recent hot streak, allowed no earned runs for the second time in three starts on Thursday, though he wiggled out of trouble all afternoon. He allowed a season-high 11 hits in 6 1/3 innings, but stranded 10 runners (four in scoring position) with the help of key strikeouts and double plays. He kept the ball down, which translated into 11 of his 14 outs coming on the ground. In two starts against the Twins this season, he has allowed seven runs on 13 hits in 12 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn struggled to keep the ball in the ballpark during his last start against the Brewers. In his 4 2/3 innings, the right-hander gave up a total of six runs -- all coming on four homers. Blackburn didn't issue a walk in the start but the sinkerball pitcher needs to keep the ball down in the zone more than he did in his last start to be successful. Next up will be his second start of the season against Detroit. Blackburn gave up four runs over 5 2/3 innings in that start at Comerica Park.
away_pitcher_note: Bonine threw eight innings of one-run ball in his third Major League start Friday against the Rockies. While keeping Colorado hitless through four innings, he threw plenty of strikes down in the zone, which translated into 17 of his 22 outs coming via ground balls. The right-hander stayed true to his reputation as a strike-thrower, tossing 69 of his 99 pitches over the plate. All three of his starts occurred during Interleague Play, but now Bonine will get his first taste of an American League lineup.

home_pitcher_note: After two dominant outings against his former National League foes, Hernandez gave up five runs -- four earned -- on seven hits in his start against the Brewers, – all of which were scored by the third inning. Despite the early troubles, Hernandez managed to pitch seven innings to help save the Twins bullpen. The leader of the Twins staff has seen his share of ups and downs this season and he’'ll try to fix one disappointment in his second career start against the Indians. Hernandez delivered his worst start of the year in Cleveland last month, allowing seven runs on 12 hits in just three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd scuffled again in his last outing, but he didn't let the game get out of hand. Struggling to find his command in Saturday's loss to the Reds, Byrd threw just 57 strikes out of 95 pitches. He again had trouble keeping the ball in the park, allowing his Major League-worst 21st home run of the season to Adam Dunn. Byrd has had mixed results against the Twins this season. He allowed just one run in seven innings in April at the Metrodome, but when he faced the Twins in Cleveland two months later, he was torched for six runs in three innings. The veteran right-hander is 10-4 with a 3.79 ERA in his career against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey continues to demonstrate why he was so coveted by other teams during his rapid ascent through the Twins Minor League system. The right-hander pitched his first career shutout on Sunday against the Brewers, holding Milwaukee to just three hits while striking out eight batters and not issuing a single walk. It was the fourth straight quality start for Slowey and he is now 3-0 with a 0.93 ERA over that span.  Next up for Slowey will be his first start of the season against Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Constantly having a knack to find trouble  but somehow being able to escape it, the left-handed Laffey finally got punished. Laffey's ability to get crucial double-play balls has been his way out of sticky situations, but he couldn't do it on Sunday. The Reds erupted for a five-run fifth inning to give the rookie his fifth loss of the season. In his only start against the Twins this season, Laffey was the benefactor of a 12-run outburst from the Indians lineup, but wasn't too shabby himself, allowing just one run in six innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: The Twins have preached to their pitching staff to throw inside this season and one pitcher who has listened is Perkins. The southpaw has found particular success in doing that against the Tigers. He limited Detroit to just two runs over 6 1/3 innings while striking out a career-high seven batters in his last start. Perkins will try to continue that same approach when he faces the Indians for the first time this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians will take advantage of Thursday's off-day to keep Lee on his fifth day. They have every reason to do so, given that Lee has had a first half worthy of an All-Star starting bid. He has refined his command, regained the confidence that helped make him an 18-game winner in 2005 and been a steady force in the rotation. His bid for his 12th win was thwarted by the lack of run support he received Tuesday against the White Sox, when he gave up just one run on six hits with a walk and three strikeouts but took a no-decision. Lee worked eight shutout innings in a win over the Twins on April 18.

home_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka's only real problem in his last start was a familiar one -- he wasn't economical. The righty threw 101 pitches and walked five over just five innings. All the same, he allowed just two hits and a run against the Rays and was in position to get the win, only to have the Red Sox squander a 4-1 lead. Matsuzaka has given up 55 hits over 75 innings and is holding opponents to a .201 average. In seven Fenway starts, Matsuzaka is 5-1 with a 4.10 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Baker looked to be in complete control at the start of his last outing, retiring 10 of the first 11 batters he faced against the Tigers. Baker would give up three runs on seven hits over his six innings. He didn't issue a single walk and struck out five. Baker has started to settle in since health issues plagued him early in the year. Next up for Baker will be a start at Fenway Park. It will be his first start of the season against the Red Sox. Baker is 0-0 with a 3.00 ERA against the club in one career appearance.

home_pitcher_note: Lester pitched an outstanding game to shut out the Yankees on Thursday night. The lefty gave up just five hits and struck out eight to pick up his seventh win. Lester worked ahead in the count throughout the night to keep the Yankees off the scoreboard and off the bases. He recorded two consecutive walks to start off his performance, but they remained the only two walks he gave up. Lester threw 105 pitches and retired the final four batters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: After finding trouble against the Tigers in two previous outings, Blackburn made some key adjustments in his last start. Catcher Joe Mauer credited the change to Blackburn's ability to rely more on his curveball to keep hitters off his fastball. He'll try to see if he can do that once again in his next start at Fenway Park against the Red Sox. Blackburn allowed four runs in an inning during his lone career appearance against Boston last season.

home_pitcher_note: Beckett made his ninth straight start with at least six innings in the Red Sox's 6-4 win over the Yankees on Friday, allowing three earned runs, four hits and two walks in six frames. He wasn't perfect -- the Yankees made him work during his 102-pitch start -- but he got the job done. In two career starts against Minnesota, he's 1-1 with a 3.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After delivering his worst start of the year in Cleveland last month when he allowed seven runs in just three innings, Hernandez rebounded in his second career start against the Tribe. The right-hander delivered his 10th quality start of the season by allowing just three runs on five hits over six innings. Hernandez has been better with his location lately and the Twins hope that's the case when he faces Boston for the second time this season. Hernandez allowed just three runs over six innings while picking up the win in that contest.

home_pitcher_note: The good news for Rogers out of his last outing Friday at Seattle was that he used a cutter effectively against right-handed hitters, something he hasn't done a lot with that kind of pitch. However, it couldn't help him through a pitching duel with Erik Bedard and the Mariners bullpen. He gave up a tape-measure solo homer to Raul Ibanez, a left-handed hitter, but stayed in the game until the Mariners wore him down in the eighth for two more runs, giving him four over 7 2/3 innings and returning his record to .500. Rogers gave up three earned runs on six hits with six strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings May 4 at the Metrodome in his only outing against the Twins this season.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey saw his streak of 16 consecutive scoreless innings come to an end in the second inning of his last start against the Indians. The right-hander allowed five runs in the inning on three hits and two walks. But following a three-run homer by Grady Sizemore, Slowey recovered to retire 14 of his next 15 batters. Slowey's ability to bounce back speaks volumes to how far he's come this season in his first full year as a starter. Next up for Slowey will be his second start of the season in Detroit. He pitched six scoreless innings, allowing just four hits, in a win there on May 23.

home_pitcher_note: Though Galarraga battled command of his fastball for most of his last outing Thursday at Seattle, he tossed five scoreless innings before Jeff Clement's solo homer put some damage on his ledger in the sixth. He left with a lead that eventually slipped away, but his third straight no-decision nonetheless extended his unbeaten streak to eight consecutive starts since his last defeat May 28. One of those no-decisions came two starts ago against the Twins at Minnesota on June 30, when he gave up three earned runs and one unearned tally on nine hits over six innings. He lost twice to the Twins in May.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins is fresh off a start where he outdueled All-Star Cliff Lee of the Indians. The Twins lefty went seven innings, surrendering three earned runs on seven hits and one walk. The Twins prevailed, 4-3, while Perkins secured his fifth win. Perkins will next take on the Tigers. Perkins is 1-0 against Detroit in two 2008 starts, going a total of 14 innings and allowing only three earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Just when Robertson seemed doomed to a summer of high pitch counts and quick hooks, the sixth-year veteran turned in arguably his best start in two years. He ended up with no decision Sunday at Seattle, but his nine innings of work with a lone run allowed on four hits essentially won the game for Detroit by allowing the Tigers' bullpen to outlast its Mariners counterpart. Any similar effort against the Twins would be a big boost for a Tigers club looking to close out the season's first half strong.
away_pitcher_note: Baker continued to impress against potent lineups as he held the Red Sox scoreless over seven innings at Fenway Park. The right-hander allowed just five hits, walking two and striking out seven while throwing 94 pitches. The heat and humidity in Boston seemed to wear Baker down a bit late in his outing, but he still managed to produce yet another quality start. He'll face the Tigers for the fourth time this season in his final start before the All-Star break. He's 1-0 with a 3.38 ERA in those three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Verlander yielded two runs on two hits in the first inning of his last start, but followed with six hitless frames. Only one batter reached in that span on a walk. In his last four starts, the righty has looked every bit the ace most predicted before this season. He won three of those starts, allowing eight earned runs in 24 innings. He has not lost since June 6. Verlander can help end the Tigers' pre-All Star schedule on a positive note. In two starts this season against Minnesota, he's 0-1 with a 3.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn more than made up for his rough relief outing at Fenway last season, when he gave up four runs in an inning. In his return to the famed ballpark, Blackburn pitched 6 2/3 innings and allowed just two runs on six hits to the Red Sox. Blackburn even retired a stretch of 10 straight batters during the outing. The right-hander has continued to make adjustments in each one of his starts and he'll have to do so again when he faces the Tigers for the third time this season. He is 1-0 with a 2.24 ERA in those first two starts against Detroit.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins was one of the surprises for the Twins in the first half. The left-hander provided nine quality starts in his 13 tries before the All-Star break. His ability to pitch inside and challenge hitters has been a welcome addition, and the Twins will need to see more of that in the second half. He'll face Texas in his first post-break appearance. He gave up two earned runs over 6 1/3 innings in his lone start vs. Texas this season.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers need an improved second half from Millwood, who didn't get past the sixth inning in any of his last four starts. Millwood allowed 10 hits and five runs in Saturday's 9-7 loss to the Chicago White Sox. Millwood did a nice break after struggling with a groin injury the last few weeks. He has struggled against the Twins the last three years, going 0-4 with a 5.59 ERA. Millwood has pitched better against the Twins in the Metrodome, where he is 0-2 with a 2.81 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: It was a rough finish to the first half for the lone veteran of the Twins staff. The right-hander gave up six runs in 4 1/3 innings to the Red Sox at Fenway Park. A pleasant surprise early in the season, Hernandez is looking to rebound from some recent difficult starts. Most of that trouble has come on the road where Hernandez holds a 7.48 ERA on the season. Despite his woes, the Twins are 13-7 in Hernandez's starts. Next up is a start against Texas. He's 0-1 with a 13.50 ERA in two starts vs. the Rangers this season.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison struggled with his command in his previous start against the White Sox, allowing five runs in 2 2/3 innings. He had trouble throwing his slider for strikes, and allowed Chicago to tee off on his fastball for seven hits and a home run. Harrison will be making his third Major League start.

home_pitcher_note: Baker continues to emerge as the true ace of the Twins staff. Although he gave up four runs over seven innings to the Tigers his last time out, it was the first time in nine starts that Baker had allowed more than three earned runs in an outing. Now that the right-hander is healthy, he's expected to have an even bigger impact on the club's rotation in the second half. The Twins were 9-5 in Baker's 14 starts in the first half. He'll now face Texas in his first start after the All-Star break. He picked up a no-decision after giving up five runs in 4 1/3 innings in his lone start vs. the Rangers this season.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla has been on the disabled list with neck stiffness. No, it's not from the 15 earned runs he's allowed in his last two starts. The Rangers are hoping the Padilla that does comes back is the one for most of the first half that was one of the most consistent starters in the American League. Padilla had allowed three earned runs or less in six of his last eight starts before his recent hiccup.

home_pitcher_note: Ponson, who signed with New York on June 18, will be making just his fourth start in a Yankees uniform this season. During his last outing he surrendered just one earned run over six innings while recording two strikeouts against Tampa Bay. He is 1-0 with a 4.24 ERA so far in his brief tenure in New York. Ponson possesses a 10-2 record with a 2.42 ERA in 15 career appearances against Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: A stellar first half has Blackburn being mentioned as a potential Rookie of the Year candidate. The sinkerball pitcher has started to become more consistent, delivering quality starts in five of his last six outings. He's started to eliminate his problems with the big inning and could be a big factor for the Twins in the second half. He'll make his second start against the Yankees. In the first, he left having pitched just 4 1/3 innings after he was struck in the face by a Bobby Abreu line drive.

home_pitcher_note: Rasner battled through five innings en route to his fifth victory of the season during his last outing against the Blue Jays. The 27-year-old allowed four runs in the first inning of the game but settled in and managed to get through five innings on 108 pitches. He finished his outing with six strikeouts for his first victory since June 18. After starting the season with three straight victories, Rasner is now 2-7 with a 6.19 ERA over his past nine outings. He is 1-1 with a 3.97 ERA in his two career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: An infected fingernail on Slowey's right middle finger pushed him back to the end of the rotation. The right-hander had initially been tabbed to start the first contest after the All-Star break. After a string of good starts, Slowey has found some trouble recently. He's given up at least five earned runs in each of his last two starts. The Twins need Slowey to make quicker adjustments on the mound and keep the ball down in the zone. He'll try to do just that when he faces the Yankees for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Mussina surpassed his win total from the entire 2007 season when he picked up his 12th win Friday night against the A's. He threw six innings of one-run ball and scattered nine hits to quiet the Oakland offense. Mussina struck out six -- four looking -- and did not record a walk for the second straight game. He is now 11-3 with a 3.00 ERA in his last 16 starts.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander continues to impress the Twins with his performance in a starting role. Perkins held a hot-hitting Rangers lineup scoreless for six innings, allowing just three hits and walking three. He's 3-0 in his last three starts and has not lost since May 30, going 5-0 with a 3.81 ERA over that span. That last loss came against the Yankees, the club he will face next in New York. Perkins gave up five earned runs on 10 hits over just four innings in that first outing at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Lee was pegged for 11 hits against the Mariners on Sunday, but that didn't prevent him from turning in his second complete game of the season. In nine innings, he limited the damage to a pair of runs with no walks and four strikeouts. He threw 77 percent of his pitches for strikes in the outing, and that's really been the key to his impressive '08 season, in which he became the first AL pitcher to reach 13 wins. Lee is 1-1 with a 2.41 ERA in two starts against the Twins this season.
away_pitcher_note: The lone veteran in the Twins rotation continued to show his dominance at home in his last start. Hernandez extended his record at the Metrodome to 8-1 after holding the Rangers to just two runs on five hits over seven innings. But it's away from the Metrodome where the right-hander has found trouble. He's just 2-5 with a 7.48 ERA in nine road starts. And next up, he'll face a Cleveland team that pounded him at Progressive Field in his first start there on June 12, allowing seven runs on 12 hits in just three innings.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona will rejoin the Indians' rotation after missing two months with a left hip strain suffered May 23 against the Rangers. He made two rehab starts with Class A Lake County and Double-A Akron and has had no physical problems after a brief setback in late June. The Indians hope Carmona's return will see him return to his form of 2007, when he won 19 games. He was struggling with his command before getting hurt, walking 38 batters in 58 innings. Carmona was 3-1 with a 1.45 ERA in four starts against the Twins last year.
away_pitcher_note: Baker continues to be the unfortunate recipient of some bad breaks. Although he allowed just one run on two hits over eight innings against Texas, Baker picked up the loss in a 1-0 defeat. Baker has delivered 10 quality starts in the 15 games he's pitched this season. His consistent performance has him emerging as the true ace of this young Twins staff. In his next start, he'll try to see if his offense can have better luck while he's facing the Indians. Baker is 0-1 vs. Cleveland this season, despite having allowed just one earned run in each of his two starts against the club.

home_pitcher_note: Sowers received a permanent spot in the Indians' rotation because of injuries to Jake Westbrook and Fausto Carmona and the trade of CC Sabathia. Generally, he's struggled to prove he's worthy of the job, though he had an encouraging outing against the Mariners on July 19. Sowers gave up four runs on five hits with three walks and three strikeouts in six innings. The Indians believe he is taking baby steps toward becoming a reliable member of their starting five. He'll look  to take more steps against the Twins. He is 1-1 with a 3.13 ERA in three career starts against Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn won't remember his first two starts against the Yankees fondly. After being struck by a Bobby Abreu line drive in the first of those starts, Blackburn exited his second outing vs. the Yankees early once again -- this time due to a poor start. The right-hander lasted just 1 2/3 innings, giving up six runs (three earned) on seven hits. A failure to make adjustments proved costly in that start and Blackburn will try to rebound against the Indians. Blackburn is 2-0 in two starts against the Tribe this season, allowing just two runs over 13 2/3 total innings.

home_pitcher_note: Some late struggles by the right-hander turned a good start against the Yankees into a less than pleasing one. Slowey gave up three runs in his final one-third of an inning, including a two-run homer to Bobby Abreu. The homer by the Yankees right fielder was the 13th long ball that Slowey has given up in 15 starts this season. Keeping the ball inside the park has been a challenge for the pitcher and one he'll have to do better with as he faces the White Sox for the third time this season. He is 0-2 against Chicago in two starts in ’08, having allowed 11 earned runs over just eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on just three days' rest for the fourth time in his career, Buehrle was as dominant as he has been since the start of June. The southpaw allowed one run on six hits over 7 1/3 innings, striking out three and not issuing a walk in winning his second straight decision. He improved to 6-2 over his last nine starts and 7-3 in his last 13, picking up his 10th career victory against Texas. Buehrle has a 1-1 record with a 5.27 ERA in two starts this season against the Twins but has not yet pitched at the Metrodome in 2008. Buehrle has a career 21-11 record against the Twins, more wins than against any other opponent for the left-hander, including a 10-5 mark in Minneapolis.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins allowed five earned runs on eights hits in six innings in his last start, a 5-1 Twins loss to the Yankees. The rookie left-hander cruised through the contest's first four innings but surrendered two runs in the fifth and three in the sixth before being removed. Perkins will next take on the White Sox, against whom he received a no-decision on June 9, going 5 1/3 innings while giving up three earned runs in a 7-5 Minnesota loss in Chicago.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander earned rave reviews in his Major League debut on Wednesday by striking out seven over four innings, marking the highest total for a White Sox big league debut since Ravelo Manzanillo fanned eight on Sept. 25, 1988. Richard allowed four earned runs on seven hits over four innings, walking just one, but didn't get great support from his defense. He threw 50 of his 85 pitches for strikes, and the one-time University of Michigan quarterback did enough to earn a second start, at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander was rocked early in his start Friday at Cleveland, allowing four runs in the first inning of the Twins' 5-4 loss. But after the tough start, Hernandez battled and only allowed one run thereafter, skirting trouble with timely double-play balls to pick up his second complete game of the season, albeit in a losing effort. Hernandez has had mixed success against the White Sox this season, compiling a 1-1 record with a 5.54 ERA in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd wasn't exactly economical, throwing 109 pitches in just six innings, but he did keep the White Sox in the game Friday during their 6-5 victory over the Tigers at Comerica Park. Floyd gave up four runs, three earned, on nine hits, striking out four and walking three, as he remained unbeaten in seven career starts against Detroit. He has not won a start since beating Oakland on July 5. Floyd has a 2-1 record with a 2.11 ERA over three starts against the Twins this season, although he is 0-1 at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Baker worked five innings and allowed three runs in halting a five-game losing streak for the Twins on Saturday (July 27). The Twins right-hander walked three and struck out five in earning his seventh victory of the season. Baker owns a 3.38 season ERA, best among Minnesota's starting corps. He has allowed three earned runs or less in 23 of his 25 starts this season. ... In four seasons (2005-08), Baker has a 3.96 ERA post-break.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander battled through six innings to earn his first victory of the second half, allowing four earned runs on five hits. He struck out five and minimized the damage by not walking a hitter. Danks makes his next start on the same night as the non-waiver trade deadline, although he is in extremely little danger of moving anywhere. Danks also closes out this four-game set at the Metrodome, carrying a 1-1 record with an 8.78 ERA over three starts against the Twins this year. In fact, 13 of the 44 earned runs allowed by Danks in 2008 have been scored by Minnesota. Danks is 2-3 lifetime with a 7.06 ERA when facing the Twins, and 1-1 at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn takes the mound against the Indians, five days after facing the Tribe in Cleveland. The right-hander ended up with a no-decision, but pitched well, allowing one run and four hits in seven innings. He left with a 2-1 lead but the Indians tied the game in the eighth. Blackburn is 2-0 in three starts against Cleveland this season. He has allowed three earned runs in 20 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sowers had his best start in nearly two years Sunday and it looks like the left-hander may have found a groove. In his longest outing since July 28, 2006, Sowers flirted with perfection, retiring the first 15 Twins in order, before bowing out after eight innings of the work. The only damage he allowed were two runs on a couple soft hits, but they were more than enough to force him to settle for a no-decision. Sowers has not faced the Twins this year, but in 2006 he picked up one of his two career complete-game shutouts against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey capped a difficult July on a stellar note. The right-hander had struggled mightily in his first three starts of the month -- going 1-1 with a 9.00 ERA. But Slowey pitched a gem against the White Sox in his last July start, throwing a complete-game shutout in the 7-0 Twins win. Slowey's first start of August will come against the Indians, whom he beat on July 5, going six innings while surrendering five earned runs in a 9-6 Twins victory.
away_pitcher_note: Byrd picked his second consecutive win Monday with his best start of the season. Over 7 2/3 strong innings, Byrd was barely touched, allowing just four hits and striking four to pick up his fifth win of what has been a disappointing season for the veteran right-hander. It was unlike most of his other starts where he's struggled keeping the ball in the park and runners off the bases. Over his last two starts, he has allowed just one run in 13 innings of work. He has struggled against the Twins this season, compiling a 0-2 record with a 7.04 ERA in three starts. Lifetime, he is 10-5 with a 4.06 ERA against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano struggled with the club in April after returning from injury. The 24-year-old left-hander was 0-3 with a 11.32 ERA in three starts. But he was dominant at Triple-A Rochester prior to being recalled on Friday. In his last 11 starts with the Red Wings, Liriano was 10-0 with a 2.67 ERA. His return to the Twins will come at the Metrodome on Sunday against the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: After two quality starts in a spot role for the Tribe, Ginter has been given a more extended look in the Indians' rotation, and ran into trouble Tuesday in a loss to the Tigers. Ginter lasted just four innings, allowing four runs on eight hits with a walk, three strikeouts and one homer allowed. He didn't have quite the command he had in his previous two starts, as he burned 77 pitches to get through the short outing. Until the Indians feel Aaron Laffey has righted himself at Triple-A Buffalo, Ginter will remain in the rotation. So he'll get his first crack at the Twins in three years.

home_pitcher_note: His last outing made it two straight strong starts, as he held the run-happy Rangers to three runs -- two earned -- over six innings in Arlington. He had excellent control, throwing just 28 balls during an 88-pitch outing. The various ailments that have bothered him off and on most of the season appear to be behind him heading into the final two months of the season. This will be his -- and the Mariners' -- first appearance against the Twins this season. He is 2-1 with a 4.70 ERA in his career against the Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins received the victory in his last start against Chicago, but he was not at his best. The rookie left-hander went six innings while allowing four earned runs on seven hits and two walks in the 6-5 Twins triumph. The Twins are 10-6 in Perkins' 16 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey got things back on track on Thursday by giving up two earned runs and six hits in 7 2/3 innings to pick up the win against the Rangers. He struck out two and walked one. In his previous two starts, the knuckleballer had given up eight and four earned runs, respectively. Those two starts were quite different than the four that preceded them -- a stretch that saw Dickey gave up a combined four earned runs. Dickey has a 4.78 ERA at home this season, and right-handed hitters are batting above .300 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Baker allowed four earned runs on five hits and three walks while receiving a no-decision in his last start against Chicago. He labored early, throwing 61 pitches through three innings, but ended up striking out eight batters. Despite the less than stellar start, Baker has still allowed three earned runs or less in 23 of his 26 starts this season. Baker will next take the bump against Seattle, a club he has not faced in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander stayed put as the Trade Deadline came and went, and his first start since didn't go the way he wanted. Facing the Orioles in the fifth inning, a two-out, none-on situation turned into an eight-run rally and Washburn's 96th career loss. It was his rockiest outing in more than two months. Washburn, who is 6-5 with a 3.46 ERA in his career against the Twins, went 1-2 with a 3.26 ERA against them in 2007. He needs two more victories to reach 100 in his MLB career.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander was superb in his most recent start, against Cleveland on Friday, lasting seven innings while allowing one earned run on six hits and one walk in Minnesota's 4-1 victory. It was Blackburn's second consecutive stellar start against the Indians in a week -- going 2-0 in 14 innings while allowing only two earned runs in those outings. Blackburn will next face Seattle for the first time of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Davies got his second straight victory on Saturday against Chicago, but it didn't seem like he would in the second inning. Then, he gave up a hit and a walk before leg cramps from the heat forced him to leave the game. Davies went 5 1/3 innings, allowing five hits and three runs.
away_pitcher_note: A pair two-run homers off the bats of Kelly Shoppach and David Dellucci doomed Slowey's last start against Cleveland. The right-hander went six innings while allowing five earned runs. He is at his best in the first inning-Slowey has not allowed a run in that frame all season, spanning 17 starts. Slowey will next head to Kansas City to kick off a three-game set against the Royals. He earned a complete-game victory in Kansas City on May 29 in the Twins' 5-1 victory.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke threw six shutout innings in his last outing, then got ejected in the seventh for hitting Chicago's Nick Swisher with a pitch. The umpires had already issued a warning, so Greinke was automatically tossed. He said that hitting Swisher was unintentional. Before the seventh inning, Greinke shined. The last time he faced the White Sox, they crushed his first-pitch fastballs. This time, Kansas City manager Trey Hillman said that Greinke had better command. As a result, the righty earned the win, limiting Chicago to two runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start back in the Majors since being recalled from Triple-A Rochester, Liriano didn't have the same electric stuff he did in 2006, but the results were similar. The 24-year-old lefty craftily wriggled out of jams in three separate frames during his outing against the Indians, pitching six shutout innings while allowing three hits and three walks, striking out five. An elevated pitch count -- 96 in six frames -- prevented him from going further. Liriano will next travel to Kansas City to take on the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Meche's last outing didn't start so well -- he allowed two runs to the Red Sox in the first inning -- but from there, he settled down -- striking out nine -- en route to a victory, his seventh in his last 11 starts. It was a strange win, though. Meche agreed with manager Trey Hillman that he was effectively wild. Meche walked five batters, and Boston often swung at several pitches out of the strike zone on those strikeouts. Meche is cruising; his ERA has gone down from 5.54 since June 5.
away_pitcher_note: Baker didn't exactly have his best stuff in his last start against the Mariners. The right-hander delivered perhaps his worst outing of the season, giving up a season-high six runs on nine hits over just 5 1/3 innings. The outing marked only the fourth time in 18 starts this season that Baker has allowed more than three earned runs. It was an inability to make an adjustment to get the ball down that cost Baker. He'll try to rebound when he faces the Royals, a team he beat in his first start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The southpaw appeared to be cruising in his last start against Seattle until he got to the seventh inning. Perkins had allowed just one run through six before giving up a grand slam to Raul Ibanez with one out in the seventh. It ended Perkins' night, having allowed five earned runs on 12 hits over his 6 1/3 innings. Although he has just one loss since May 30 at the All-Star Break, Perkins has struggled a bit in his last three starts. He has given up at least four earned runs in each of those outings. Next up, he will face the Yankees, against whom he is 0-2 this season.
away_pitcher_note: Though Ponson allowed two runs to the Rangers in the second inning on Wednesday, he settled down to allow only one more run the rest of the way. Ponson lasted 6 1/3 innings and gave up six hits and a walk, achieving his goal of back-to-back solid starts. In three starts against the Twins this season, Ponson is 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA -- including a complete game victory at the Metrodome back in May.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander was forced to work his way out of a few jams in his last start, on Wednesday against the Mariners. Blackburn admitted he didn't have his best stuff in the contest and never "felt good" on the mound. Still, the rookie managed to give up just three earned runs over six innings to a Seattle club that had taken its toll on the Twins' pitching staff. Blackburn will try to see if he can get through his next start a little easier. He'll face the Yankees for the third time this season. He's 0-1 with a 6.00 ERA in two starts against New York this season.
away_pitcher_note: Mussina turned in perhaps the finest outing of his resurgent season last Thursday, blanking a hot Rangers offense for seven innings and leading the Yankees to a victory. Though Mussina allowed base runners in each of the first six innings, he induced two double plays and didn't allow the Rangers to mount a serious threat. He's now won five of his last six decisions, and is 2-0 with a 1.29 ERA this season against the Twins, his next opponent.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey gave another solid effort in a win against the Royals on Friday. He went 5 2/3 innings, giving up just one run. A challenge awaits Slowey in his next start. The last time he faced the Yankees, he gave up four runs in just 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Darrell Rasner will rejoin the rotation after pitching in long relief of Ian Kennedy on Saturday. Rasner hurled 4 1/3 effective innings, striking out four and walking none. He will be making his third start this season against Minnesota, coming off a no-decision in his last outing against the Twins on July 22, when he threw 5 2/3 innings of two-run, four-hit ball, walking four and striking out two in New York's 8-2 win at Yankee Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano's second start brought him back even closer to the form he showed in 2006, but still not quite there. He went 5 2/3 inning and gave up three runs in earning the win. In his two starts since returning from Triple-A, Liriano is 2-0 with a 2.31 ERA. He said he felt more relaxed physically and mentally on the mound against the Royals on Saturday. Liriano also threw more sliders, a sign that he is getting closer to where he used to be.
away_pitcher_note: The trials and tribulations of Silva's first season with the Mariners continue in his old stomping grounds -- the Metrodome. The veteran right-hander, who won 47 games for the Twins between 2004 and 2007, including 13 last season, has won one game with the Mariners since the end of April. away_pitcher_note: Baker was extremely effective in the early game of the Twins' doubleheader on Saturday, holding the Orioles to just one run on four hits over six innings. The right-hander was all set to come back out for the seventh, but a long top of the inning prevented Baker from running back out to the mound. Baker will be throwing on short rest, but manager Ron Gardenhire seemed convinced that of all the young pitchers on his staff, Baker would be the easiest hurler to do that with. Baker is 1-1 in three starts against the Indians this season, allowing seven earned runs in 18 combined innings.

home_pitcher_note: Shields earned his career-high 13th win of the season on Saturday at Yankee Stadium when he pitched eight scoreless innings, allowed just five hits while walking none and striking out six. Shields is 1-1 with a 5.94 ERA in three career starts against the Twins, and he is 8-2 with a 2.33 ERA in 15 starts at Tropicana Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins will be looking to rebound from one of his worst starts of the season, going just three innings, allowing six earned runs off five hits. Fortunately for Perkins, his line didn't matter, as the Twins had already put the game out of reach early on with a 12-run onslaught on the Orioles on Saturday night. The left-hander struggled with his control, leaving almost everything up in the zone and surrendering a three-run homer to Oscar Salazar in the third that effectively ended his night. Perkins has not faced the Rays yet this season.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson took his 11th loss of the season Sunday afternoon when he allowed six runs on six hits in two innings. The right-hander looked unsettled from the outset, when he gave up consecutive singles and a walk in the first inning before surrendering a grand slam to Alex Rodriguez. For Jackson, it was his shortest stint since June 13, 2007, when he lasted just one-third of an inning against the Padres. If Jackson is locating his 97 mph fastball, his other pitches can work well, particularly his slider. Jackson is 0-2 with a 18.90 ERA in five career appearances against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn was ineffective at best in his last start, going just four innings and surrendering four home runs, two each, to Orioles Nick Markakis and Oscar Salazar. The rookie right-hander said he was having trouble mechanically, balancing himself with his back leg, and as a result was leaving the majority of his pitches up in the zone. The outing tied the shortest start of Blackburn's career; the last time he was only able to go four innings was June 6 against the White Sox. Blackburn has not pitched against the Rays yet this season.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir is coming off a disastrous outing on Monday in which the Rays ace was lifted after tossing to five batters in the fourth inning without recording an out. He appeared to be off from the game's onset, walking the first two Red Sox batters faced, before David Ortiz connected for a three-run homer. Four of Kazmir's six hits allowed were of the long variety, as the southpaw was rocked for a season-high nine earned runs in the loss. Kazmir has struggled with his mechanics all season, particularly with his slider, which has historically been his best pitch. He will be facing Minnesota for the first time this season, and fifth time in his career. Kazmir is 1-3 against the Twins, with a 3.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey gave his club yet another quality start against the Indians, allowing three runs on seven hits over six innings, but it wasn't enough to earn him -- or his team -- a victory. Slowey suffered his second loss in his last three starts. He allowed two home runs in a start for the first time since his start against the Indians on Aug. 2. The road hasn't exactly been kind to the starter this season. He's 5-6 away from the Metrodome and his next start will come against the Rays at Tropicana Field. It will be Slowey's first start against the Rays this season.

home_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine fared well on Tuesday night, as the right-hander allowed just three Boston hits over six innings and was touched for one unearned run in the no-decision. A crafty pitcher, Sonnanstine is at his best when he pitches off his fastball and uses his command to his advantage. He threw 60 of his 93 pitches for strikes against the Red Sox and remains one win shy of the Rays' club record. He will look to notch victory No. 14 facing the Twins for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano suffered his worst start since rejoining the Twins on Aug. 1. The left-hander pitched only 2 2/3 innings while giving up eight runs (four earned). A penchant for the long ball -- he gave up two in the contest -- and an inability to put hitters away with two strikes proved costly for Liriano, as he picked up a no-decision. The road has not been as kind to Liriano as the Metrodome this season. He's now 1-3 with a 6.41 ERA in six road starts this season. He'll try to reverse that trend in his next start when he faces the Rays at Tropicana Field. It marks his first start of the season against Tampa Bay.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching on only three days rest, Baker was forced to throw a lot of pitches early in his last start against the Indians. He lasted just 4 2/3 innings, giving up four runs on six hits. Baker didn't want to use the short rest as an excuse, but it appeared to affect him. The right-hander will now get an extra day before his next start against the White Sox thanks to Monday's off-day. Baker is 2-2 with a 7.99 ERA in seven career starts against Chicago, including going 1-0 with a 5.73 ERA in two starts vs. the South Siders this season.
away_pitcher_note: Working on three days rest has not exactly been a recipe for success during Vazquez's career. The right-hander made his third start while coming back in this short period and slipped to 0-3 overall in Thursday's 9-2 loss to the Yankees. Vazquez allowed seven runs -- six earned -- on six hits over 3 2/3 innings. He struck out four, walked four and threw 88 pitches during his trip to the mound. The White Sox brought back Vazquez on three days, in part, to have him rested and ready for the start of the series in the Metrodome on Tuesday. Vazquez has a 2-0 record with a 5.11 ERA against Minnesota this season and holds a 6-5 career mark against the Twins. Vazquez also has a 1-4 ledger in the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Fatigue has seemed to plague the Twins' starting staff of late, and Blackburn was its latest victim. The right-hander lasted just 1 1/3 innings against the Rays in his last start, giving up six earned runs on six hits. He faced 12 batters while recording just the four outs. Blackburn has already topped his career high in innings in a season, with 181 1/3. The Twins will try to see if Blackburn might be able to push through one more regular-season start against the White Sox. The right-hander is 1-2 with a 6.14 ERA in four starts vs. Chicago this season.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on three days' rest, Buehrle handcuffed the Royals over six innings during a 9-4 victory on Friday. The southpaw allowed three runs, all in the bottom of the fourth and courtesy of Mark Teahen's home run, over six innings, striking out two and walking one. Buehrle threw 93 pitches, so he should be more than ready to go on regular rest at the Metrodome. Buehrle also became the only active pitcher to make 30 starts, pitch 200 innings and win 10 games for eight straight seasons. Buehrle has a 1-2 record with a 5.79 ERA against Minnesota this season and an 0-1 mark at the Metrodome. Lifetime, Buehrle stands at 21-12 against the Twins -- his most wins against any opponent. He also has 10 wins at the Metrodome, second-most to his 67 at U.S. Cellular Field.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey looked to be locked in early during his last start, but like many of the other Twins starters lately, he could not make it through the fifth inning. Slowey allowed five runs over 4 1/3 innings, taking his third loss in his last four starts. That lone win came at the Metrodome, where Slowey has found most of his success this season. The right-hander is 7-4 with a 3.04 ERA in 11 starts there. This will be Slowey's fourth start vs. Chicago this season. In his lone outing against them at the Metrodome, he pitched a shutout.
away_pitcher_note: The official White Sox ledger concerning starters pitching on three days' rest this week fell to 1-2 as Floyd suffered the loss against the Royals on Saturday night. The right-hander actually kept the White Sox in contention, but was victimized by three long balls, including David DeJesus' inside-the-park homer. Floyd yielded five runs on eight hits over 6 1/3 innings, although he didn't get any bullpen help to keep that run total down, striking out four and not issuing a walk. Floyd has dominated the Twins this season, posting a 3-1 record with a 1.86 ERA in four starts. Minnesota has just 17 hits over 29 innings in 2008 against Floyd, who also has a 1-1 mark at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano rebounded from his roughest start since being recalled on Aug. 1 to deliver a gem against the Rays at Tropicana Field. The left-hander allowed just one run over seven innings to the playoff-bound Rays. Liriano struck out seven but found some trouble, issuing four walks. He is 6-0 with a 2.05 ERA in 10 starts since returning to the Majors. He’ll face the Royals for the fourth time this season. Two of those have come during his second stint with the Twins, and in those, Liriano has allowed just five earned runs over a combined 13 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davies has burst into prominence in his last two starts. After throwing eight shutout innings against the Mariners, he got through the opening seven innings on Saturday against the White Sox without surrendering a run. Davies faced the minimum over that span and wound up surrendering just two runs and taking his second victory of the week. Davies has cited a quick tempo as the key to his recent success. He's challenging the strike zone with his best stuff and therefore has gotten away from his earlier penchant for high pitch counts.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins will be looking to rebound from his worst start of the season, when he lasted just two-thirds of an inning while giving up five runs (two earned) to the Rays. Fatigue was cited as a concern by the Twins following the start, and the club skipped Perkins' next start, placing him at the end of the rotation. The hope is the extra rest will get Perkins back on track to face the Royals. It will be the first time the lefty has faced Kansas City this season.
away_pitcher_note: Meche has one last shot at achieving his goal of a sub-4.00 ERA. He held the Tigers to two runs in six innings on Monday night, but that reduced his 4.08 mark only slightly. Meche rolled through the first five innings with no problems, but gave up two runs on three hits and a walk in the sixth. He's won three of his last four starts for the most victories since his 15-13 record in 2003 for Seattle. This year, he's 0-2 with a no-decision in three starts against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Baker allowed one earned run on five hits and one walk in seven innings of Tuesday's crucial 9-3 Twins victory over the White Sox. Baker remained in control for the game's duration, striking out four. He will next take on Kansas City in what will be the last regular-season game of the season for both squads. Baker is 1-0 with a 3.29 ERA in two starts against the Royals this year.
away_pitcher_note: Zack Greinke was the probable starter for this game but he was scratched after a seven-inning, 107-pitch outing against the Tigers. The Royals decided he'd pitched enough this season. So Duckworth, who was supposed to be skipped over this weekend, instead will start the season's final game. Duckworth has been a capable rotation fill-in since being recalled from Triple-A Omaha in late August. In his last start, he lost, 3-0, to the White Sox but pitched well. He received no decision, giving up two runs in five innings of a 3-2 victory at Minnesota on Sept. 11.

home_pitcher_note: Danks will be pitching on short rest, but he did not work very long on Friday against Cleveland, lasting four innings and allowing seven runs on seven hits. He threw 80 pitches in that game, which means he should still be relatively fresh come Tuesday. He's struggled since late August, posting a 4.91 ERA over his past seven starts. He earned a win in only one of those starts. Danks is 1-1 with a 7.91 in four starts against Minnesota this season.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn will take the hill for Tuesday's one-game tiebreaker in place of injured right-hander Kevin Slowey. Blackburn started the year 9-6 with a 3.60 ERA but he is 2-4 in his past nine starts with a 5.74 ERA. He's only gone more than five innings in four of those nine starts. However, he received the win in the Twins' 3-2 victory over the White Sox on Wednesday when he gave up two runs on eight hits and two walks over five innings. Blackburn is 2-2 with a 5.67 ERA in five starts against Chicago in 2008.

summary: 2009-03-05 - Kingdom of the Netherlands (2) @ Minnesota Twins (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note:
This will mark Liriano's first career Opening Day start, a significant achievement for the pitcher who is just 2 1/2 years removed from Tommy John elbow ligament replacement surgery. Liriano was given the nod in the contest after the club's projected Opening Day starter, Scott Baker, was placed on the 15-day disabled list with right shoulder stiffness.

As for Liriano, he's looking to deliver a standout season in his second full season back from surgery. The pitcher's velocity and trademark slider might not be the same as they were back in 2006, his breakout rookie season, but Liriano's pitching repertoire can still intimidate hitters. That's particularly true now thanks to his new changeup, which manager Ron Gardenhire described as "Santana-like" this spring.

After posting a 6-1 record with a 2.74 ERA in 11 starts when he returned to the Twins rotation on Aug.1 of last year, Liriano went 1-2 with a 4.94 ERA in eight Grapefruit League starts this spring.
away_pitcher_note:
The ace of the Mariners' starting rotation makes his second career Opening Night start in the past three seasons. The first one was an eight-inning shutout effort against the Athletic two years ago.

Hernandez is coming off an up-and-down Spring Training, pitching superbly for Venezuela in two World Baseball Classic appearances but scuffling a bit in Cactus League games. He finished camp with a 0-0 record and 8.36 ERA. But he pronounced himself healthy and ready to go in the opener against the Twins after his final outing of the spring and is looking for his first career victory at the Metrodome, have lost his only decision in the Teflon-roofed facility.

After finishing among the AL leaders in several categories last season, including the eighth-lowest ERA, sixth in road ERA (3.01), seventh with 7.8 strikeouts per nine innings, he is due for some run support. King Felix had a 2.72 ERA in the 11 games that he received a no-decision, allowing three or fewer runs in nine of those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn was limited for a time this spring by a sore left knee, which he had surgically repaired during the offseason, but the knee issue appears to be behind him now. Having logged close to 200 innings, Blackburn tired at the end of last season but he worked this winter to improve his stamina in order to try to pitch 200-plus innings in his second full Major League season. He'll be pitching on six days' rest for his first start of the season due to some late rotation changes, but the Twins still expect him to throw around 90 pitches when he faces the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard (6-4, 3.67 in '08) had a pain-free Spring Training, and that was the primary issue after having shoulder surgery last September. The Mariners' Opening Day starter last season had an injury-plagued first season with the Mariners. He was 1-1 with a 5.56 ERA during the Cactus League.

home_pitcher_note: The Twins starter who possesses the best command of his pitches, Slowey showed this spring why he's considered to be on the verge of a breakout season. Having averaged just 1.4 walks per nine innings in his career, Slowey continued that trend this spring. Heading into his final spring start, Slowey had issued just one walk in 20 1/3 innings. Another reason for optimism is that Slowey continues to improve his offspeed pitches as he starts the season in the rotation for the second consecutive year.
away_pitcher_note: Silva (4-15, 6.46 in '08) begins pursuit of a comeback season in his old stomping grounds. He had his best years with the Twins, from 2004-07, reaching double digits in wins three times and pitching at least 200 innings twice. He finished the spring strong, tossing four shutout innings before surrendering a two-run home run in the fifth.

home_pitcher_note: One of the surprises for the Twins in the rotation last season, Perkins will try to see if he can duplicate that success in just his second stint as a starter in the Majors. One key for Perkins will be to limit the number of long balls that he gives up. The lefty has been working on a slider this spring to use against right-handers, which the Twins hope will be an additional pitch that he can trust in critical situations.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn (5-14, 4.69 in '08) begins the final year of his four-year contract with fingers crossed that he receives more run support. That has been an issue practically from the day he joined the Mariners, for whom he has a 23-43 record. He was 2-2 record with a 6.12 ERA in seven Cactus League outings.

home_pitcher_note: Contreras' comeback from a ruptured left achilles tendon has been impressive. Contreras suffered the injury covering first base during a game against Boston on Aug. 9. Contreras bounced back from a rough 2007 campaign to finish above .500 and lower his ERA from 5.57 to 4.54. He attacks hitters from a couple of different angles to keep them off stride and was able to throw all of his pitches during his Spring Training recovery. Contreras has a 4-3 record with a 4.13 ERA against the Twins and has a lifetime 26-20 mark with a 4.22 ERA at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: Considered on the bubble for a roster spot heading into the final week of spring, Dickey earned the No. 5 spot in the rotation after Scott Baker was placed on the 15-day disabled list. The knuckleballer is coming off perhaps his best spring, having posted a 2.04 ERA in 11 appearances. That included striking out 18 batters in his 17 2/3 innings. A key to Dickey's success has been a more consistent knuckleball, which he worked on this past winter with the legendary Phil Niekro. Now the hope of the Twins and Dickey is that he can translate the improved pitch into regular season success.

home_pitcher_note: Colon was as durable as any starter on the White Sox staff when he threw nine complete games for the team back in 2003. But after having bone chips removed from his pitching elbow in October, the White Sox don't expect a lot of nine-inning efforts from the burly right-hander. Colon made seven starts for the Red Sox last year but has made just 35 starts over the past three seasons combined. Colon's velocity topped out in the low 90s during his Cactus League starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano didn't walk away with a win in his first career Opening Day outing, but the Twins were pleased with what they saw from the left-hander. He was able to pitch seven innings, allowing four runs on four hits. His trouble was limited to a couple of mistake pitches, including a hanging slider that he left up for Ken Griffey Jr. to hit for a home run. Liriano will face his first road test of the season when he takes on the White Sox at U.S. Cellular Field. The lefty is 0-1 with a 5.14 ERA in two contests there.

home_pitcher_note: It was not a typical start for Buehrle, as he was consistently behind Royals' hitters and had to work his way out of trouble in each of five innings pitched during his seventh Opening Day trip to the mound. By the time Clayton Richard replaced Buehrle, the White Sox ace had walked three, hit two and given up six hits, but yielded just two earned runs. Buehrle threw 97 pitches, with just 58 of them going for strikes. Buehrle blamed his Opening Day woes on being too amped up and overthrowing instead of just trying to hit his spots. He has the most wins in the history of U.S. Cellular Field at 68 and holds a 21-13 career mark against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't the prettiest of starts for Blackburn in his first outing of the year against the Mariners. The right-hander had to battle through five innings, giving up four runs on eight hits. The feeling of the Twins staff was that the numbers were a tad worse than Blackburn's actual performance as many of the hits were bloopers or jammed shots. But the pitcher said that he was going to work between starts on keeping his ball down in the zone as some of his pitches were a little high -- although that was perhaps a result of some first-outing jitters. In his next start, Blackburn will return to Chicago, where he delivered a gem of a performance in the club's 1-0 loss to the White Sox in a one-game tiebreaker for the AL Central title last September.

home_pitcher_note: Usually known for his stellar command of his pitches, Slowey struggled to make adjustments early in his last start against the Mariners. But when the Twins really needed him to settle down, Slowey did just that, managing to toss six innings and allow five runs on nine hits. He had one wild pitch in the contest that scored a run, which is an unusual occurrence for the pitcher who had just one wild pitch in 27 starts last year. Now Slowey will have to see if he can relax and keep his pitches down when he faces the Blue Jays. He is 0-2 with a 5.51 ERA in three career starts vs. Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: Litsch struggled in his season debut on Wednesday, matching an unfortunate career high with three home runs allowed. The 24-year-old right-hander gave up two blasts to Tigers slugger Miguel Cabrera -- both on sinkers -- and yielded another on a cutter to Brandon Inge. Overall, Litsch was tagged for five runs on seven hits and finished with five strikeouts and one walk over six innings, finishing with 106 pitches (64 strikes). In his career against the Twins, Litsch is 3-0 with a 2.08 ERA in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins delivered a stellar outing in his first start of the season, allowing just one run on five hits over eight innings to the Mariners. But it was not enough to get him the win as Seattle's left-hander Jarrod Washburn held the Twins scoreless over eight innings. Perkins' eight-inning outing tied his career high and while he threw 106 pitches in the start, he could have gone longer had it not been for two, 11-pitch at-bats by the Mariners in the seventh inning. Next up for Perkins will be a start against the Blue Jays. In two career starts against Toronto, Perkins is 0-0 with a 4.91 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Romero was part of a unique moment in baseball history on Thursday afternoon. Romero (the sixth overall pick in the 2005 First-Year Player Draft) squared off against Detroit starter Rick Porcello (27th overall in the '07 Draft). It marked the first time since the Draft began in 1965 that a pair of first-round picks faced each other in their respective Major League debuts. Romero came out on top, limiting the Tigers to two runs on seven hits with five strikeouts and two walks over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Baker will make his first start of the season against the Blue Jays. The right-hander began the year on the disabled list with right shoulder stiffness. It was not a problem that the Twins felt would keep Baker out for long, but they didn't want to risk it considering that Baker had trouble keeping his arm loose between innings during his final Spring Training outing. All of that appears to be behind Baker now and he'll focus on building off his success last season. The right-hander has shown more consistency in each of the last two seasons and showed his focus under pressure by going 3-0 with 2.53 ERA during the Twins' pennant chase last September. Baker is 0-1 with a 3.72 ERA in three starts vs. Toronto.
away_pitcher_note: In his season debut on Friday, Richmond was only able to work four innings against the Indians before a lengthy rain delay -- the longest in Jays franchise history -- forced him from the game. In his abbreviated appearance, the 29-year-old rookie allowed three runs on five hits with four strikeouts and two walks in a no-decision. The three runs Richmond allowed were each driven in by Cleveland's Travis Hafner, who tagged the pitcher for a two-run double and a solo homer. Richmond has never faced the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano had problems with his command in his last start against the White Sox. The left-hander allowed five runs on six hits over his 4 2/3 innings on Saturday, but it was his four walks that stood out in the contest. Two of those scored runs as Liriano issued free passes to Jermaine Dye and Paul Konerko with the bases loaded. Next up he'll face the Blue Jays at home. This will be Liriano's first career start vs. Toronto. He pitched two scoreless innings of relief in his only appearance against the club.
away_pitcher_note: After a shaky season debut, Halladay rebounded with a strong showing against the Indians on Saturday. Over seven innings, Doc yielded only one run -- courtesy of an RBI double off the bat of Grady Sizemore -- on five hits. The ace of Toronto's staff finished with seven strikeouts, two walks and 12 outs created via grounders. In his career against the Twins, Halladay is 7-0 with a 2.92 ERA in 11 outings. Halladay has gone 3-0 with a 4.46 ERA in his career at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Once again, it was a Jim Thome home run that came back to haunt Blackburn. After giving up the solo shot to Thome last September in the one-game tiebreaker, Blackburn gave up a two-run blast to the White Sox DH in his last start. It was the only real mistake for the right-hander in his six-plus innings. He allowed four runs, three earned, on six hits while walking one and striking out one. But afterward, Blackburn said that he felt he was on top of his pitches and was pleased with the way he threw. Next up for Blackburn will be a start against the Angels at the Metrodome. He is 0-2 with a 3.09 ERA in two career starts vs. the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Moseley has delivered impressively in his first two starts, keeping the Angels in games with quality efforts. He went 5 2/3 innings against the Red Sox on Sunday, holding them to three runs (two earned) on six hits and two walks, one intentional, while striking out three men. Moseley is committed to pounding the strike zone with his two-seam and four-seam fastballs along with his off-speed stuff, and it shows: two walks (one intentional) in 11 2/3 innings against seven strikeouts. Moseley has faced Minnesota three times in his career, all as a reliever, with a 5.40 ERA in 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey was left looking for answers after a second rough outing in an 8-6 loss to Toronto on Monday. Slowey gave up five earned runs in just over five innings, increasing his ERA to 7.94. Slowey threw 88 pitches and gave up two home runs in his first loss of the season. In his season debut against Seattle, he pitched six innings and gave up four earned runs in a victory. The right-hander out of Winthrop University, thought by many to have the best Spring Training of all of Minnesota's starters, has yet to duplicate that in the regular season.
away_pitcher_note: The Angels are leaning toward giving Oliver, a veteran southpaw who has excelled for two years in their bullpen, his first Major League start since 2004 in the wake of the death of Nick Adenhart. Oliver went as deep as four innings in a camp game this spring and has made only one appearance this season, lasting two-thirds of an inning. Oliver pitched six brilliant innings of long relief in Game 3 of the 2006 NLCS for the Mets and has the stuff and knowledge to get into the middle innings if called upon. He likes to come inside with hard stuff and then go with breaking stuff away. Oliver is 2-5 with a 5.99 career ERA against the Mariners and is 1-2 with a 3.18 ERA at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins has pitched well in both outings so far this year, but has no victories to show for it and one loss. On Tuesday, the Twins left-hander pitched eight innings, giving up two runs on seven hits and striking out four, but didn't factor into the decision. He's gone eight innings in both starts and thrown over 100 pitches each time, compiling a season ERA of just 1.69. Once an odd man out of the Twins' rotation plans, Perkins now seems like an anchor and has been Minnesota's best starter early in the season. The University of Minnesota product has credited his strong start to the season with his willingness to pitch inside and make hitters uncomfortable.
away_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start in six years, facing Ken Griffey Jr. in his return to Seattle in front of a packed home-opening crowd, Loux had a strong effort on Tuesday. In frigid conditions, he lasted 5 1/3 innings and held the Mariners to two earned runs on five hits and three walks, striking out two men. His heavy sinker got him out of trouble on several occasions with ground balls, and he managed the emotional duress of pitching for the first time since the loss of good friend Nick Adenhart, killed five days earlier with two companions in a hit-and-run auto accident. Loux waited a long time for this, and he delivered handsomely.

home_pitcher_note: The knuckleballer comes off a masterful performance last Wednesday in Oakland, where he threw a complete game in just his second start of the season. Wakefield carried a no-hitter one out deep into the eighth inning before Kurt Suzuki singled cleanly to break up the bid. Wakefield allowed four hits and two runs while walking two and striking out four. Wakefield is 13-5 lifetime with a 4.38 ERA lifetime against the Twins. He was tagged for seven hits and seven runs, six earned, over 2 2/3 innings in his only appearance against them last season.
away_pitcher_note: Baker missed his Opening Day start with right shoulder stiffness, then was hammered for four home runs in four innings on Wednesday in his season debut against Toronto. This time, he'll need an effort like his last one against the Red Sox. Baker pitched masterfully last July 7 at Fenway Park, throwing seven scoreless innings in a no-decision. But the Twins lost, 1-0, on Manny Ramirez's RBI single off reliever Brian Bass in the eighth.

Wakefield carried a no-hitter one out deep into the eighth inning before Kurt Suzuki singled cleanly to break up the bid. Wakefield allowed four hits and two runs while walking two and striking out four. Wakefield is 13-5 lifetime with a 4.38 ERA lifetime against the Twins. He was tagged for seven hits and seven runs, six earned, over 2 2/3 innings in his only appearance against them last season.
