This time, he'll need an effort like his last one against the Red Sox. Baker pitched masterfully last July 7 at Fenway Park, throwing seven scoreless innings in a no-decision. But the Twins lost, 1-0, on Manny Ramirez's RBI single off reliever Brian Bass in the eighth.
summary: 2009-04-22 - Minnesota Twins @ Boston Red Sox (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: The big right-hander took a step back in his second start with the Red Sox, getting shelled for six hits and eight runs over three innings against the Orioles. The only consolation in that outing for Penny is that the Red Sox rallied back from a 7-0 deficit to notch a 10-8 win. Penny's debut was far more successful, as he earned the win with six quality innings (five hits, three runs) against the Angels. In Penny's only previous career start against the Twins, he gave up nine hits and five earned runs over six innings, taking a no decision.
away_pitcher_note: Despite suffering his third straight loss to begin the year 0-3, Liriano delivered his best outing of the season against the Blue Jays. The left-hander pitched six innings and allowed just two runs (one earned) on seven hits to a hot-hitting Toronto ballclub. Liriano said he had better command of his fastball in this last start, something he's been working on since the start of Spring Training. Although his club was trailing, 2-1, when Liriano left the game, the Twins bullpen proceeded to give up seven runs in the seventh. The left-hander will try for his first win of the season as he makes his first career appearance against the Red Sox at Fenway Park.

home_pitcher_note: Staked to 14 runs of support in the second inning Saturday in New York, Carmona was able to use his start as a work day, of sorts. He got his work in by going six innings, allowing four runs on six hits with four walks and a strikeout. He induced 11 groundball outs, so that's a sign that he had good action on his sinking fastball. But the walks continue to be a concern. He's walked more (10) than he's struck out (eight) this season -- a trend that began last year. Carmona is 3-3 with a 3.83 ERA in 10 career appearances against the Twins. He gave up nine runs in just 2 1/3 innings in his lone start against them last year.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn managed to pitch into the seventh inning in his last start, but once again, the Twins' offense couldn't produce early enough to get the right-hander a win. He allowed four runs on eight hits in 6 1/3 innings against the Angels, but it wasn't until a seven-run comeback in the eighth inning that the Twins pulled away. The club is 2-1 when Blackburn is on the hill and will hope to improve that record when the righty faces Cleveland at Progressive Field, where he is 1-0 with a 2.08 ERA in two career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Silencing the wrath of Yankees fans still bitter about his four unfortunate years in New York, Pavano pitched a gem at Yankee Stadium on Sunday. He went six innings, allowing just a run on four hits with a walk and four strikeouts before the bullpen blew the game and saddled him with a no-decision. Pavano felt he didn't have his best fastball, but he got quality results from his slider and changeup. All in all, he's made major strides since allowing nine runs in one-plus inning of work in his Tribe debut in Texas on April 8.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Slowey finally found the form that he had during Spring Training. After allowing 22 hits in 10 1/3 innings in his first two starts of the season, Slowey held the Angels to just two runs on six hits in seven innings, lowering his ERA from 7.94 to 5.89 in the outing, with his only two runs coming on a two-run homer by former Twins center fielder Torii Hunter. Slowey said that a key to his success was throwing a few more pitches out of the strike zone. Known for his stellar command, Slowey has realized that he has often been throwing too many strikes, and by making his misses less hittable, he feels he can produce better results. Next up for Slowey will be a start against the Indians. He is 1-2 with a 5.48 ERA in four career starts against the Tribe.

home_pitcher_note: Laffey doesn't know how long his spot in the Indians' rotation will last, but he's certainly made the most out of the opportunity, to this point. Laffey was strong against the Royals in his first start on April 15 and even stronger in his second appearance against them six days later. He went seven innings, allowing just a run on seven hits with three walks, two strikeouts and a hit batter. What was most impressive was the way the sinkerball-tossing lefty always had a double-play ball in his back pocket. He induced five double plays in all. Laffey, who is filling in for an injured Scott Lewis, is 1-1 with a 5.75 ERA in four career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins was finally rewarded with a victory after delivering his third straight eight-inning outing, holding the Angels to one run on four hits. Despite getting drilled in the left thigh by a Bobby Abreu liner for the first out of the seventh inning, Perkins managed to make it through eight innings while throwing just 84 pitches. He likely would have completed the game had his leg not started to stiffen up. Perkins is the first Twins pitcher in almost four years to log three successive eight-inning outings. The last to do so was Johan Santana, who accomplished the feat June 2-14, 2005.

home_pitcher_note: The righty makes his third start of the season after starting the year on the disabled list with right shoulder stiffness. His first two outings didn't go well. He made his debut on April 15 and allowed five hits and six runs over four innings against Toronto. His second start, last Wednesday at Fenway Park, wasn't much better. The right-hander allowed three two-run homers to the Red Sox and was roughed up for six runs on 10 hits in the first game of a day-night doubleheader. He has surrendered 15 hits and 12 earned runs over 8 2/3 innings. All of which adds up to a 12.46 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Niemann had his best outing of the young season Wednesday in Seattle when he pitched four perfect frames before allowing a three-run homer to Jose Lopez in the fifth.  The 6-foot-9, 280 pound right-hander, who was the Rays' No. 1 pick of the 2004 June Draft (fourth overall), had a slower than expected path to the Major Leagues due to injuries and problems with his mechanics. This spring he showed marked improvement in pitching down with his fastball and with his breaking ball command, which proved exceptional all spring. While getting everything coordinated might be difficult for a taller pitcher, the downward angle of Niemann's pitches can make the baseball extremely hard to hit. He is 0-0 with a 0.00 ERA in one career appearance against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty allowed four hits and seven runs and lasted just four innings in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader as he suffered his fourth loss in as many starts in 2009. He walked four while striking out six but also hit a batter. Liriano said afterward he is still struggling to find command of his two-seam fastball, a pitch that was drilled for a three-run homer by Red Sox utility man Jeff Bailey.  He has lost five straight starts dating back to last Sept. 26, the most consecutive losses by a Twins pitcher since Kevin Slowey lost five straight between Sept. 28, 2007-May 18, 2008. Liriano's four innings also marked his shortest outing since lasting just 2 2/3 on Sept. 16, 2008 at Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: Shields locked horns with Seattle's Felix Hernandez on Thursday and took his second loss of the season despite pitching brilliantly, allowing just one run on four hits in 7 1/3 innings. Shields has built a reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to pitch into the seventh or eighth inning, which is evidenced by two consecutive seasons with 215 innings pitched. Shields is 1-1 with a 6.26 ERA in four career starts against the Twins and went 0-0 with a 6.35 ERA in two 2008 starts; he is 0-1 with a 7.71 ERA in two career starts at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: After a back-to-back rocky starts by Scott Baker and Francisco Liriano in Boston, it was Blackburn who got the starting pitching on the right track with his outing in Cleveland on Friday night. Blackburn allowed just one run on six hits over seven innings to earn his first win of the season. He improved his record at Progressive Field to 3-0 in three career starts and has a 1.80 ERA over that span. Blackburn's sinker was working well in his latest start -- something that's been critical to the right-hander's success. He struck out four and didn't walk a batter in the outing.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir made his fourth start of the season Friday night against the A's and appeared headed for trouble from the outset when he walked three batters in the first three innings. But he managed to sort out his control issues en route to posting six scoreless innings while holding the A's to just two hits to earn his third win of the season. Kazmir is 2-3 with a 3.18 ERA in five career starts against the Twins and he is 1-2 with a 3.43 ERA in three career starts at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey delivered his best performance of the season in his last start against the Indians, holding Cleveland to one run on eight hits over eight-plus innings. The right-hander carried a five-hit shutout into the ninth inning, but gave up three straight hits to the middle of the Indians order before he was replaced on the mound by Luis Ayala. Slowey finally appears to have gotten back to the form that made him so effective in Spring Training, mixing in his offspeed pitches while showing strong command of his fastball. Next up for Slowey will be a start against the Royals. He is 3-0 with a 2.16 ERA in four career appearances (three starts) vs. Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: The Royals are still trying to cautiously figure out what they have in starter Sidney Ponson. After lasting 3 1/3 innings and giving up six runs against Cleveland on April 21, Ponson returned to better form against Detroit in his last start. Ponson pitched eight innings and gave up three runs -- two on a homer from Brandon Inge -- but was tagged for another loss, dropping his record to 0-3. The Royals need Ponson to be a reliable innings eater, and Royals manager Trey Hillman is confident that Ponson's slip-up in Cleveland was a mechanical problem and not the beginning of a trend.

home_pitcher_note: After beginning the season with three straight eight-inning starts, Perkins found himself in a little early trouble in his last outing against the Indians. The left-hander gave up four runs on seven hits over five innings. Perkins fell behind in the count throughout most of his outing and said that he was fighting himself, a result of perhaps the six days of rest he had between starts. But Perkins didn't want to use excuses for his struggles, saying that his goal next time out was to get back to the form he showed in his first three outings of the year. Perkins will try to find that form when he faces the Royals, a team he is 0-0 with a 2.16 ERA against in four career appearances (one start).
away_pitcher_note: After a disastrous 2008 and a short stint at Triple-A Omaha, Brian Bannister has been a revelation. Bannister got shelled during Spring Training and was promptly sent to Omaha. But after getting recalled, he is 2-0 with a 0.69 ERA. His last time out, he shut down a Blue Jays offense that came into the game leading the Majors in runs scored. This is the Bannister the Royals saw in 2007, when he went 12-9 with a 3.87 ERA. After his last start, Bannister said he thought he might have figured out the source of some of his struggles. He's had success in his career against Minnesota, too. He's 3-1 with a 3.40 ERA in six games.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off two rough starts, Baker showed slight improvement in his last outing against the Rays. After giving up seven home runs over 8 2/3 innings in his first two starts of the year, Baker did not allow a single long ball in his six-inning outing vs. Tampa Bay. He still gave up four runs on six hits to the Rays, earning him his third loss in three starts. Baker will try to continue to focus on keeping the ball down in the zone when he faces the Royals in his next start. The right-hander is 5-2 with a 2.60 ERA in nine career starts against Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Meche's status for Sunday's start in Minnesota is in question after Meche left his last start against Toronto on Tuesday with lower back tightness. The Royals list Meche as day-to-day, and Meche is confident he'll be able to pitch, but he's coming off the shortest outing of his season. He lasted just 3 2/3 innings against the Blue Jays while giving up five runs on seven hits. He entered the game with four walks in his first four starts, then eclipsed his season total with five walks against Toronto. Meche said his lower back has been nagging him since Spring Training, but he did post a 2.63 ERA in four starts before his disappointing outcome against Toronto.

home_pitcher_note: Usually, the new guy gets a little better welcome than this. Jackson has taken a scoreless performance into the seventh inning in three of his first five starts as a Tiger, but has only one win to show for it. He threw 117 pitches over six innings in his last start to keep the Tigers in a scoreless game against the Yankees before New York erupted for 10 runs in the seventh. He's 1-2 with a 9.42 ERA in six career appearances, including three starts, against the Twins, but his lone meeting with Minnesota last year featured 7 2/3 innings of one-run ball for a much-needed victory at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty looked to be in his line for his first win of the season, after allowing just two runs over 6 2/3 innings to the Rays in his last start. But the Twins were unable to hold on to the lead, winning on a walkoff fielder’s choice in the ninth inning. For Liriano, it was a positive outing in that he started to show better command of his fastball while also mixing in his breaking. He’ll try to avoid becoming the second Twins Opening Day starter to begin a season at 0-5, the only other being Frank Viola back in 1989. Liriano is 2-1 with a 4.93 ERA in seven career appearances (five starts) against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: The Tigers put Porcello in their season-opening rotation fully expecting he would struggle at times, and his last start hit the mark. He struggled to get his sinker down and his curveball on the corners, and the Yankees pounced, roughing him up for six runs on six hits over 3 2/3 innings. He isn't going anywhere, but look for the Tigers to work with the youngster on adjustments as he prepares for a Twins lineup that could pick him apart if he can't locate.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander delivered his second straight seven-inning outing in his last time out on the mound against the Rays. He held Tampa Bay to just two runs on eight hits while walking one and striking out three. The sinkerball pitcher was able to get plenty of groundouts despite the fact that he feeling light-headed and a little wobbly for most of his outing. After a little bit of a shaky start to the season, Blackburn is now 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA in his last two starts. His next start will come against the Tigers at Comerica Park, where he is 0-2 with a 6.14 ERA in three appearances (two starts).

home_pitcher_note: In his loss to Blue Jays ace Roy Halladay on May 1, Hendrickson had a good curveball for the first three innings and then got a couple of pitches up in the zone, and he gave up four runs in the fourth that proved his undoing. Hendrickson allowed too many baserunners in his stint of five-plus innings, as the Blue Jays had nine hits, two walks and a hit batter against him.
away_pitcher_note: After retiring the first six batters he faced in his start against the Royals, Slowey found himself in trouble in each of his next three innings. The right-hander would pitch just five innings in the contest, allowing five runs on eight hits while striking out four. But Slowey was able to come out with a win as he received plenty of run support once again. He came into his last start receiving an average of 9.57 runs per outing -- the highest of any of the Twins' starters. He did not issue a walk for the third time in five starts this season. He leads all active pitchers in the Majors since the start of the 2008 season with the fewest walks allowed -- having issued just six over that span. Next up for Slowey will be his first career start against the Orioles at Camden Yards. He's 0-1 with a 6.00 ERA in one career start vs. Baltimore.
summary: 2009-05-06 - Minnesota Twins @ Baltimore Orioles (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Bergesen recorded his first quality start in three Major League starts on May 1 against the Blue Jays. He allowed six hits and three walks with one strikeout in six innings. Bergesen gave up three runs in the second inning of that no-decision against the Blue Jays. He finished up strong in a 90-pitch outing. It was an improvement against a hot-hitting team in Toronto over his previous outing when he allowed five earned runs and 10 hits in four innings to the Rangers on April 26 in a game the Orioles went on to win, 8-5.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins had to work to get through six innings in his last start against the Royals. The left-hander allowed five runs on 10 hits while striking out four. Two-out hits proved to be a problem for Perkins late in his outing. He gave up a two-out solo home run to Willie Bloomquist in the fifth inning of his start -- the first homer for the Royals second baseman since June 6, 2007. He also gave up three straight two-out hits in the sixth inning that scored two runs and erased his club's one-run lead. In his next start against the Orioles, Perkins will try to see if he can find the form he had at the start of the year when he delivered three straight eight-inning outings. Perkins is 0-0 with an 11.74 ERA in four career appearances (two starts) vs. Baltimore.

home_pitcher_note: Baker carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning of his last start against the Royals but things quickly went downhill for the starter. He gave up five straight hits to start the seventh, including a three-run homer to Jose Guillen that cut the Twins lead to one. Baker was eventually charged with five runs over his six-plus innings and suffered his fourth loss in four starts so far this season. While it was another loss, the Twins took a positive in that Baker was throwing the ball down for those first six innings and was mixing in his pitches better than his previous outings. Next up for Baker will be a start at home against the Mariners -- the team he was supposed to face on Opening Day before a DL stint sidelined those plans. Baker is 0-3 with a 5.50 ERA in six career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: One rough inning seems to be all the rookie right-hander needs to ruin an otherwise solid outing. The three runs he surrendered in the first inning against the Athletics last Sunday did most of the damage, and an opposite-field home run produced two of those runs. Jakubauskas made the mistake of leaving a fastball out over the plate to Athletics slugger Jack Cust, who became the first opposing hitter to go deep against the Mariners pitcher. He had tossed 21 1/3 innings without allowing a home run.

home_pitcher_note: After beginning the season 0-4 over his first five starts, Liriano finally got his first win on Monday against the Tigers. He pitched 7 1/3 innings, allowing just two runs on four hits. He struck out a season-high nine batters in the contest as he held Detroit scoreless over the first five innings of the contest. With a fastball averaging around 91-92 mph and better command of his slider and changeup, Liriano was able to keep the Tigers hitters off-balance for most of the outing. The left-hander said after the start that he hopes he can keep pitching like he did on Monday night -- with better command of all of his pitches. Next he'll face the Mariners, against whom he opened the season. In that start he gave up four runs on four hits over seven innings to take the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez looks to bounce back from his roughest outing of the season, a six-inning stint against the Rangers in Seattle. The right-hander didn't walk a batter while recording nine strikeouts, but he also surrendered 10 hits and six earned runs, only three fewer than he had allowed all season. He had a 22-inning scoreless streak end in the fourth innings. After surrendering one home run in his first 37 innings this season, he was touched for two dingers against Texas.

home_pitcher_note: The sinkerball pitcher couldn't find control of his fastball in his last start, causing problems early in his outing against the Tigers. Blackburn gave up a career-high nine runs (six earned) in just 3 1/3 innings vs. Detroit. It was his shortest start since Sept. 19, 2008, when he went just 1 1/3 innings. Blackburn wasn't helped by a handful of defensive miscues early in his outing, but manager Ron Gardenhire said that Blackburn needs to learn how to take a step back and make pitches when it counts. Five of his runs came in the second inning after Blackburn had retired the first two batters he faced. Blackburn will next face Seattle for the second time this season. He's 1-0 with a 5.73 ERA in two career starts vs. the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander continued his early-season success, holding the Rangers to one run -- a solo home run -- over seven innings. But that long ball erased a one-run lead and Bedard ended up with his third no-decision of the season. He struck out seven and walked none and now has 39 whiffs and six free passes in 38 innings over his first six starts of the season. He has surrendered three home runs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey received his first loss of the season on Wednesday against the Orioles. It came under unfortunate circumstances: The game had four rain delays that totaled nearly four hours. Slowey was pulled after a long delay, giving up three earned runs in three innings. Slowey has had an interesting season. He's 4-1 but has a disappointing 5.50 ERA. He's given up eight or more hits in four of six starts, but has a superb 25-2 K/BB ratio. Next up is Detroit, a team that Slowey is 2-0 with a 5.74 ERA against in three career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Five of the six innings Galarraga threw Thursday against the White Sox were solid, but it only took one to cause problems. The right-hander gave up five runs on three hits and two walks in the first inning. He scattered only three more hits over his next five innings. It was the second start in a row that Galarraga surrendered five runs or more, and he's watched his ERA balloon from 1.85 to 4.08 in that span. Hell have his work cut out for him in Minnesota. In six career games against the Twins, Galarraga is 0-4 with a 5.23 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins went six innings in his last start against the Orioles. The left-hander allowed four earned runs on five hits while striking out two. Perkins went 2-1 with a 2.73 ERA in four starts against the Tigers last season. The Twins are 2-4 in his starts in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Willis will be activated to make his first start of the season after spending the past month and a half on the 15-day disabled list with an anxiety disorder. Tigers manager Jim Leyland said Willis will not be on any sort of pitch count -- he threw 118 pitches in his final rehab start for Triple-A Toledo. In that start, Willis gave up two runs in 7 2/3 innings, fanning four and walking four. The left-hander has only made one appearance against the Twins, giving up one run in an inning of relief.

home_pitcher_note: Scott Baker pitched precisely the sort of game that he needed to get back on track Friday against Seattle. Baker dealt seven shutout innings, striking out five and walking none in Minnesota's 11-0 victory. The previously struggling Twins ace was 0-4 with a 9.15 ERA in four starts coming into the game. This start came after Baker carried a no-hitter through six innings against the Royals but surrendered five earned runs in the seventh inning. Baker gets Detroit next. He is 4-3 in 12 career starts against the Tigers with a 3.69 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After going winless in his first four starts, Justin Verlander is back to dominating opposing hitters. His fastballs are hitting the upper 90s with ease, his curveballs are dropping for strikes and he's learning to use his abundance of adrenaline in his favor. The result is a string of three stingy starts, covering 23 innings of one-run ball with five walks, 31 strikeouts and only two extra-base hits allowed. He'll get a test of that new form at the Metrodome, where good pitches can turn into bad habits on a fast artificial surface.

home_pitcher_note: Hughes is scheduled to open a homestand at Yankee Stadium looking to rebound from a horrid performance on Saturday against the Orioles. Making his third start of the season after being joining the club from Triple-A, Hughes' night was over almost before it began. The touted hurler set a new career high with eight runs allowed as Baltimore sent 13 batters to the plate in the second inning. Hughes trudged off the field charged with eight hits, walking two and striking out none. In two starts thus far at the big league level, Hughes hasn't had his good stuff, though he turned in one where he looked exceptional, two hits in six scoreless innings at Detroit on April 28.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano has won consecutive starts since beginning the season 0-4. He was a good-luck winner in Saturday's 9-6 victory over the Mariners, the benefactor of great run support. Liriano surrendered five earned runs on six hits and two walks while striking out four in five innings. He will have to be more sharp in his next start against the Yankees to secure a third consecutive victory. This will be Liriano's first career start against New York.

home_pitcher_note: Chamberlain will be looking for answers to his first-inning woes when he starts the second game of a series with the Twins at Yankee Stadium. For whatever reason, Chamberlain has struggled to get his juices flowing in the first inning through six starts. He has surrendered nine first-inning runs -- including three home runs -- and allowed opponents to hit .481 (13-for-27). Chamberlain's first-inning issues with velocity continued in his last start, on Sunday at Baltimore, where his fastball mostly sat near 90 mph before gaining speed later. This will be Chamberlain's first career appearance against Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Nick Blackburn was superb in his last start, tying a career-high with six strikeouts in seven shutout innings against the Mariners, scattering five hits with one walk. He lowered his ERA by nearly a run. Unfortunately for him, the Twins bullpen blew the lead when he exited after having thrown 99 pitches, and Minnesota lost 5-3. Blackburn will make his first start at the Yankees' new stadium on Saturday. Maybe it will change his luck against the Bronx Bombers -- he is 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA in three career starts against New York.

away_pitcher_note: Slowey had to labor a bit through his last outing against the Tigers, throwing 98 pitches in six innings while allowing just one run. He allowed the leadoff hitter to reach base in five of his six innings, which included Jeff Larish'’s solo home run to start the sixth. The home run was the lone run that Slowey allowed in his outing. He scattered eight hits to the Tigers and also issued two walks in the contest, equaling his total for the season. Slowey next will face the Yankees. He is 1-1 with a 6.00 ERA in three career starts vs. New York.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte worked six solid innings against the Blue Jays at Rogers Centre on Wednesday, recording his first win since April 21 against Oakland. He allowed two runs, but only one was earned, as Toronto's Aaron Hill scored on what would have been the third out of the first inning, if not for a throwing error by Yankees second baseman Robinson Cano. Pettitte allowed five hits and four walks while striking out two. He allowed two extra-base hits, both doubles. He has now pitched at least six innings in six of his seven starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: After starting the season with three straight eight-inning outings, Perkins has been unable to get past the sixth inning in each of his last four starts. The left-hander pitched just 5 1/3 innings against the Tigers and gave up five runs on five hits. It was also the fourth straight outing that Perkins has allowed at least four earned runs. Perkins was not exactly sharp with his command in this last outing, issuing a career-high four walks to the Tigers. Next up Perkins will start the series finale against the Yankees at the new Yankee Stadium. The left-hander is 1-2 with a 5.00 ERA in three career starts vs. New York

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle saw his personal-best five-game winning streak to start a season come to an end Wednesday in Cleveland, falling to the only American League Central team with a winning record against him. Buehrle allowed four runs on seven hits over seven innings, striking out six, walking one and yielding home runs to Victor Martinez and Ryan Garko. Buehrle has pitched at least five innings in all seven of his starts this season, has gone at least six innings in six of the seven starts and has tossed 15 innings over his last two trips to the mound, with just eight hits against him. With Thursday's off-day factored in, Buehrle once again will be pitching with an extra day of rest. The left-hander has a 1-0 record against the Twins this season and a 22-13 mark lifetime against them. That's the most victories against any one team for Buehrle.
away_pitcher_note: Baker continued some of his late-inning struggles in his last start. After allowing just one hit to the Tigers over his first five innings, the right-hander gave up five runs on six hits in his final inning of work. Twins manager Ron Gardenhire said that Baker needs to work on limiting the damage, as he's now given up five-plus earned runs in four of his six starts this season. Next up for Baker will be a start against the White Sox in Chicago. It will be the first time he's faced the Sox this season. He's 2-0 with a 9.00 ERA in two career starts at U.S. Cellular Field.

home_pitcher_note: Danks did not fare well against the Blue Jays in his last start. In fact, it was his worst outing of the year. The left-hander allowed a season-high seven runs on nine hits across just three innings. During the poor performance, Danks watched as his ERA ballooned from 3.41 to 4.82. He has not won since April 22 -- a span of four starts.
away_pitcher_note: To say that Liriano struggled with a lack of command in his outing against the Yankees might be an understatement. The Twins southpaw walked six batters in six innings, but he somehow managed to hold New York to just one run on four hits. The lone run came on a solo homer by Derek Jeter with one out in the fifth inning. While Liriano missed with various pitches, it was his fastball that he struggled with the most. Only 51 of Liriano’s 101 pitches on the night were for strikes. The left-hander will next face the White Sox at U.S. Cellular Field, where he’s 0-2 with a 6.94 ERA in three career appearances (two starts).

home_pitcher_note: Colon's previous start lasted just 62 pitches, as the right-hander was forced to exit early with a minor stomach problem. That was unfortunate, given that Colon was cruising against the Blue Jays. He allowed just five hits over five scoreless innings in the no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn managed to hold the Yankees to just three runs through his first seven innings, all coming on Mark Teixeira's homer in the third inning. But it was the run he gave up in the eighth of that start which knotted the game at 4 and handed the starter yet another no-decision. The right-hander scattered six hits over 7 2/3 innings as he threw a season-high 111 pitches. It may not have been a 'W,' but it was a continuation of the success Blackburn had in his previous start when he pitched seven scoreless innings against the Mariners. Blackburn will now face the White Sox in his next start. He allowed four runs (three earned) in six innings in his only start vs. Chicago this season.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey delivered a gem of a performance against the Yankees his last time out, holding the club to just two runs on seven hits over 7 2/3 innings. Five of those hits came after the start of the seventh inning as Slowey had to work his way out of a few jams. The right-hander did not issue a walk in the start and struck out a season-high eight batters. Slowey next will face the Brewers, a team he's pitched well against. In three career starts vs. Milwaukee, Slowey is 2-0 with a 2.42.
away_pitcher_note: Parra will happily strike out to end the first inning every time. Parra batted before he pitched on Sunday in St. Louis, when the Brewers batted around to spot him a 4-0 lead. Parra made it hold, allowing two runs on five hits in six innings to win his third straight start after losing his first four. He wasn't happy with walking four Cardinals batters, and he's walked four in three of his last four starts. Still, he's 3-0 with a 2.25 ERA this month and has worked six innings in each of those games. He won his only start against the Twins last season with seven shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: Swarzak will be making his first Major League start Saturday after being promoted from Triple-A Rochester on Wednesday to fill in for injured starter Glen Perkins. Swarzak was 3-4 with a 2.25 ERA allowing 40 hits with 11 walks and 32 strikeouts in seven starts for the Red Wings this season. He will likely make just one more start before Perkins returns from the 15-day disabled list. If the Twins like what they see, Swarzak might be in line for a relief role, manager Ron Gardenhire said Wednesday.
away_pitcher_note: Facing his former team in St. Louis on Monday, Looper bounced back nicely from a pair of starts in which he surrendered five runs in each. Looper worked six innings and surrendered three runs, only one of which was earned, because of a pair of Brewers errors. Looper is 2-1 with a 3.52 ERA in his three road starts this season. He has made three appearances at the Metrodome but all three were in relief before he moved into the Cardinals rotation three years ago. He surrendered two runs on six hits in 3 2/3 innings in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Baker continued to struggle Tuesday against the White Sox. The right-hander couldn't get the ball down in the zone with favorable counts and too often fell behind Chicago hitters. He lasted just five innings, walking four and surrendering four runs to pick up his fifth loss of the season. Baker has allowed at least four runs in six of his seven starts this season. In four career starts against Milwaukee, he is 2-2 with a 5.62 ERA. Baker is 5-2 with a 4.61 ERA lifetime in seven Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bush has been a quality-start machine this season, pitching at least six innings while allowing three or fewer earned runs in seven of his eight outings. Last year, he ranked second on the staff to Ben Sheets with 16 such starts. Bush doesn't particularly buy the notion that three runs in six innings is a quality start, but he does talk often about the importance of keeping his team in the game, and that's just what he's done, particularly in May. In his four starts this month, all "quality," he's 2-0 with a 3.00 ERA. Bush didn't pitch against the Cardinals during the team's swing through St. Louis, so this will be his first chance to improve on his career 2-4 record and 6.06 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: One bad inning did Liriano in Wednesday night against the White Sox, and in a big way. The left-hander threw 37 pitches in a seven-run fourth inning that included two doubles and two home runs. He was relieved after four innings, having watched his ERA balloon to 6.04. Liriano said he was missing his spots, working too quickly, and overthrowing when runners got on base. The loss was his first since April 22 at Boston. The left-hander gave up seven runs in four innings to the Red Sox that time, and will look to improve upon that outing this time around.
away_pitcher_note: Penny pitched into the seventh inning for the third time in as many starts last Wednesday at Fenway Park, handcuffing the potent Blue Jays to pick up his fourth victory of the season. The power-righty kept Toronto in check with a steady diet of fastballs, inducing a bevy of flyball outs over 6 2/3 innings of two-run ball. In two career starts against Minnesota, Penny is 1-0 with a 5.25 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn pitched seven scoreless innings Thursday in a 20-1 victory over the White Sox. The Twins scored so many runs that Blackburn had to do extra stretching between innings and it wasn't worth risking injury to try to have him finish the game, even though both he and manager Ron Gardenhire agreed that he could have. Blackburn scattered four hits and three walks and struck out two to pick up his first victory since April 29 against Tampa Bay. He has struggled in three career appearances (two starts) against Boston, going 1-1 with a 6.59 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The 25-year-old southpaw improved to 4-2 in his past six decisions last Thursday against the Blue Jays, scattering eight hits over 6 1/3 frames of one-run ball at Fenway Park. Despite allowing 10 baserunners, Lester worked his way out of trouble on several occasions to emerge relatively unscathed. He has been tagged for eight earned runs in 14 2/3 career innings against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: One start after throwing 7 2/3 innings against the Yankees in a no-decision in New York, Slowey picked up his sixth win of the season on Friday by going 7 1/3 innings against a red-hot Milwaukee Brewers team. He allowed just two earned runs in the start, lowering his ERA to 4.23. Unlike during his start in New York, Slowey benefited from some run support, as Michael Cuddyer's cycle propelled the Twins to an 11-3 victory. He'll be facing the Red Sox for the first time this season.
away_pitcher_note: The enigmatic right-hander was unimpressive in his return from the disabled list on Friday, yielding four runs on five hits over five innings against the Mets at Fenway Park. He came undone in a three-run fourth inning, when New York strung together three RBI singles in a span of four at-bats against the Japanese righty. Still winless in three starts this season, Matsuzaka is 2-0 with a 1.61 ERA in three career appearances against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Filling in for the injured Glen Perkins against the Brewers on Saturday, Swarzak dazzled in his Major League debut, pitching seven scoreless innings for his first win. He scattered five hits, working out of a jam in the sixth inning. Fighting nerves in front of 40,547 at the Metrodome, Swarzak seemed to gain more confidence as the game went on. His performance marked the first time in Twins history that a pitcher went seven scoreless innings in his Major League debut.
away_pitcher_note: The ace righty continued his recent string of sharp outings on Saturday at Fenway Park, logging a season-high eight innings in a no-decision against the Mets. After allowing a first-inning RBI single, Beckett yielded nothing further, striking out five while dominating a makeshift New York lineup to the tune of one run on five hits. In three career starts against the Twins, Beckett is 2-1 with a 4.74 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Coming out of the bullpen for his eventual no-decision against the Marlins on Sunday, Shields said he knew from the beginning he didn't have his best stuff. But despite giving up three runs in the third inning, he battled through it and ended up with a half-way decent start. The 27-year-old gave up four runs in 6 2/3 innings while surrendering a season-high 12 hits, striking out seven and walking two. With two outs in the seventh, he got hit by a hard comebacker off the bat of Ross Gload and then came out. But manager Joe Maddon said Shields -- who didn't appear hurt -- was taken out because he had 102 pitches under him, not because he was injured. Shields is 1-1 with a 5.76 ERA in five career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Baker worked between starts with pitching coach Rick Anderson on staying taller in his delivery to help keep his pitches down in the zone more consistently. The extra work seemed to pay off as Baker threw 8 1/3 innings against the Brewers, allowing three runs on six hits and delivering just his second quality start of the season. By throwing more pitches down in the zone, Baker's high fastball was able to be more effective against hitters. The Twins hope he can continue that trend when he faces the Rays at Tropicana Field. Baker is 1-1 with a 4.85 ERA in three career appearances (two starts) vs. Tampa Bay.

home_pitcher_note: A high pitch count -- 100 to be precise -- cut short Price's season debut against the Indians on Monday. He allowed two runs, which came on Ryan Garko's homer in the fourth, in 3 1/3 innings. Price struck out six and walked five as his teammates built a 10-0 lead. The left-hander gave up four hits and needs to be more economical with his pitches so he can remain in the game longer. Price took some responsbility for the eventual 11-10 loss, pointing out he needs to pitch deeper into games. He allowed the first two hitters of the game to reach base,  but struck out Victor Martinez, Jhonny Peralta and Shin-Soo Choo to end the inning.
away_pitcher_note: Before his start against the Red Sox, Liriano said he didn't hit his spots in his previous two starts, against the Yankees and White Sox. The left-hander didn't locate much better Monday, giving up five runs on 11 hits and lasting just four innings. It took Liriano 84 pitches to get through four before, then he was removed. Liriano managed to strike out seven, but he allowed five straight hits in the third before finally retiring the side.

home_pitcher_note: The home run ball was Garza's downfall in his last start against the Indians. He allowed three, including homers to Ryan Garko and Mark DeRosa, the first he has given up to right-handed hitters all season. He also gave up a home run to switch-hitter Asdrubal Cabrera. The homers were a season high and the most he allowed since giving up a career-high four on Aug. 20, 2007 against Seattle. Garza allowed five hits and struck out seven in six innings. His outing did give some much-needed rest to Tampa Bay's bullpen, which has seen a lot of work lately.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn struck out a career-high seven batters Tuesday against Boston, picking up his fourth win of the season. He was effective in working the corners of the plate for most of the game, mixing in a variety of pitches with his four-seam fastball. Blackburn scattered eight hits through seven and allowed just one earned run. Blackburn has gone at least seven innings in eight of his 10 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey delivered his fourth straight quality start for the Twins in his last outing vs. the Red Sox. The right-hander pitched six innings, allowing just two runs on six hits. He issued a rare walk while striking out five. Since his rough outing in Baltimore on May 6, Slowey has not given up more than two earned runs in each of his last four starts and he's currently on a three-game winning streak. Next up he'll face the Indians for the second time this season.  He pitched eight innings, allowing just one run, in his only other start vs. Cleveland this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rain got in the way of Huff's strong early showing against the Rays on Thursday. The young left-hander, making his third start in the bigs, went four scoreless innings, allowing four hits with a walk and two strikeouts. When rain delayed the game for two hours, 40 minutes, Huff didn't come back out. Still, the early showing was a marked improvement over Huff's first two Major League starts, so he can certainly take some positives from it.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander has been impressive since being called up to fill in for an injured Glen Perkins. Swarzak has allowed just three earned runs over 13 innings, delivering a quality start in both of his outings. That included his start against the Red Sox, in which he pitched six innings and allowed three runs on five hits. With Perkins not scheduled to return for at least another week, Swarzak will get a few more starts to show the club what he can do. He'll face the Indians for the first time in his career at the Metrodome.
away_pitcher_note: For the second outing in a row, Lee didn't work ahead and didn't work efficiently against the Yankees on Friday. But once again, he limited the damage against him and turned in a quality start. Lee allowed three runs on nine hits with two walks and five strikeouts. Keeping with a trend that has been taking place all season, Lee didn't get much run support, and he took the loss. The Indians have averaged just 2.73 runs in the games Lee starts. Lee is 7-3 with a 3.78 ERA in 16 career starts against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Baker failed to deliver a second straight quality start when he faced the Rays, pitching 5 2/3 innings and allowing four earned runs on six hits. Like his previous start, Baker allowed nearly all of his runs at the end of the outing. He held the Rays to just one run on three hits through the first five innings, with the lone run coming on Carl Crawford's two-out solo home run in the third. But in the sixth, Baker gave up three straight hits -- which concluded with Evan Longoria's three-run shot to deep center field.  Next up, Baker faces the Indians. He is 3-5 with a 4.00 ERA in 11 career starts vs. Cleveland.
away_pitcher_note: It's not getting any better for Carmona, who has battled control problems all season. In his latest start against the Yankees, Carmona lasted just four innings, allowing seven runs, four of which were earned, on eight hits with three walks and two strikeouts. Carmona didn't get much help from his defense, but he didn't make pitches when it mattered, either. He served up a pair of home runs. In his last start against the Twins, Carmona allowed five runs (four earned) on eight hits over six innings in a loss on April 24.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez was superb against the Angels, as the right-hander didn't allow an earned run over 6 1/3 innings on Saturday, but earned the no-decision. Hernandez, though, put together his second successive solid start, striking out six batters and walking just one. Hernandez is 3-3 with a 2.98 ERA in eight career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano's woes continued in his last start against the Rays. The left-hander lasted only four innings for the third straight start, giving up four runs on seven hits. Liriano's 6.60 ERA has him tied with the Indians' Fausto Carmona for the worst in the A.L., and his seven losses are the most in the A.L. as well. Much of Liriano's damage has come in big innings, and the pitcher seemed frustrated after this last loss by his inability to correct the problem.  Despite posting a 12.00 ERA over his last three starts, he'll remain in the rotation for at least the time being. Liriano faces the Mariners, against whom he's 3-2 with a 3.25 in six career starts.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander held the Orioles to one run over seven innings in his last start, the seventh time in 10 starts this season surrendered two or fewer runs. But for the third time in those outings, he did not win as the Mariners scored no runs. He is holding left-handed batters to a .157 average this season, nearly 90 points below his career average against them.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn has become one of the Twins' more reliable starters. He delivered his third straight quality start, and his fourth in the last five outings, against the Rays last Sunday. Blackburn held the Rays to just two runs on seven hits over six innings, both runs coming on solo homers. The right-hander has been using his sinker effectively and working the corners with his four-seam fastball. He'll try to continue that trend when he faces the Mariners. Blackburn is 1-0 with a 3.50 ERA in three career starts vs. Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander continues to be the Mariners' most reliable starter, holding the Orioles to one run over 6 2/3 innings with seven strikeouts in his last start. He has been so locked into the strike zone that 148 of his last 220 pitches have been strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey moved into second place in wins among American League pitchers when he captured No. 8 of the season in his last start against the Indians. The right-hander held Cleveland to just two runs on six hits over 6 2/3 innings. It marked Slowey's fifth straight quality start and his seventh of the season. For only the fourth time this season, Slowey did not give up a long ball to Cleveland -- allowing both of his runs on a Kelly Shoppach two-run double in the seventh inning. Slowey will next face the Mariners. He is 1-0 with a 7.50 ERA in one career start vs. Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Outman, who went 2-0 with a 2.45 ERA in six May starts, opened June with another fine outing, holding the host White Sox to two earned runs on seven hits and a walk over 6 2/3 innings. Armed with a 94-mph heater that he can pump up to 97 when it's needed, Outman is the least-hyped member of a starting rotation that features four rookies and nobody over the age of 25. But Outman, a 24-year-old rookie, has been Oakland's best pitcher by a mile over the past several weeks. He's never faced the Twins in his career.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing just three total runs in his first two big league starts, Swarzak finally had a bad inning, giving up five runs to Cleveland in Wednesday's loss. Swarzak retired the first two batters in the third inning before giving up six straight hits, including a three-run homer by Jhonny Peralta. Swarzak left the game after just five innings, the shortest of his three outings. He struck out three and gave up nine hits.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson, a 21-year-old rookie, allowed a career-high six earned runs in his previous outing before allowing no runs on six hits and no walks while striking out four over seven innings on June 4 against the host White Sox. Haunted by poor run support for most of the season, Anderson has experienced many of the ups and downs expected of such a young hurler, often following sub-par innings -- and outings -- with flashes of brilliance and vice-versa. His command, however, has been solid throughout the season, and when he's on top of his game, his lively four-seam fastball and fading offspeed stuff can give opponents fits. Anderson has never faced the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Baker rebounded from a disappointing start in Tampa to deliver a solid outing against the Indians, pitching  seven innings and allowing three runs (two earned) on six hits. He struck out a career-high 10 batters in the contest. Baker credited a mechanical adjustment in which he's standing taller in his delivery to some of the improvement he's shown in recent outings. Baker's outing against Cleveland marked only his third quality start of the season, all of which have come at the Metrodome. Baker will try to see if he can carry that success on the road when he faces the A's for the first time this season. Baker is 2-0 with a 3.27 ERA in two career starts at Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Braden proved his status as leader of the A's young pitching staff in his last start against Baltimore, limiting the Orioles to one earned run over seven innings of five-hit ball with seven strikeouts to even his record. The 25-year-old carried a shutout performance into the seventh inning before surrendering a two-out homer. In two career starts against Minnesota, Braden owns a 0-1 record with a respectable 3.09 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano finally found a way to get himself back on track in his last start against the Mariners. The left-hander snapped a streak of three consecutive four-inning outings by pitching six innings and allowing just one run on two hits. The lefty walked four in his outing, but unlike previous outings, he managed to escape his way out of jams by not overthrowing. Next up Liriano will face the A's. He is 0-2 with a 10.32 ERA in three career starts at Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Behind a brilliant showing of offensive support, Cahill scattered just two runs on six hits in six-plus innings, walking none and fanning five. The 21-year-old breezed through the first six innings before being forced out of the game in the seventh having thrown 91 pitches, 58 for strikes. Following his 12th career start, A's skipper Bob Geren expressed delight in his rookie's continuing improvement on keeping the ball low in the strike zone and forcing groundball outs. This will mark Cahills first career start against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed sinkerball pitcher has quietly become one of the most effective starters for the Twins this season. Blackburn delivered yet another gem for the Twins in his last outing vs. Seattle, giving up just one run on six hits over his seven innings. But yet again, Blackburn walked away with a no-decision based on a lack of run support. The starter has just five wins this season despite delivering quality starts in eight of his 12 outings, five of which he's allowed one earned run or less. He'll try to see if he can capture win No. 6 of the season when he faces the A's.  He is 0-1 with a 3.29 ERA in two career starts vs. Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Maybe Wells needs to face an American League team to get a win. The rookie has thrown five consecutive quality starts, has a sub 2.00 ERA, has held opponents to a .220 batting average against him, and he can't get a win. In his last start, Wells gave up two runs over 6 2/3 innings against the Reds. He's been solid, hasn't complained, and now will open the Interleague portion of the Cubs' schedule.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey struggled to keep the ball down in the zone during his last start, at Seattle, where he gave up four runs on 10 hits in 4 2/3 innings in taking the loss. Three of the four runs Slowey allowed came via solo home run. Of the 35 runs that he has allowed this season, 16 have come via the homer -- good for 46 percent. The loss against the Mariners snapped a career-high four-game winning streak for Slowey. He'll try to start up a new run when he faces the Cubs for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Harden's first start since going on the disabled list with a back sprain on May 18. In his last start, May 17 against Houston, he gave up four runs on six hits and three walks over six innings while striking out seven. Harden was expected to be able to go five innings and at least 85 pitches in this game. He has a 1-0 record and 2.13 ERA in four career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Only one start remains for Swarzak until Glen Perkins is ready to rejoin the rotation and the rookie certainly didn't make a strong push to stay up with the club in his last start. The right-hander gave up three runs on four hits and walked three in just 3 2/3 innings against the A's. All of the runs came in a disastrous fourth inning. It included Swarzak throwing 10 straight balls to start the frame and striking Aaron Cunningham in the head with an errant 91-mph fastball. Swarzak will get one final shot against the Cubs to show improvement.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly is coming off a win against the Astros in which he held them to three hits over 6 2/3 innings. The lefty also notched his first Major League triple in the game and joked after that he didn't realize how hard it was to run from home to third. He is 3-1 with a 3.52 ERA in his career against the Twins, which covers six starts. He's had great success at home so far, posting a 4-1 record and 1.29 ERA in five games at Wrigley Field.
away_pitcher_note: In his first eight innings against the A's, Baker allowed just three batters to reach base -- one on a hit-by-pitch and the other two on hits. But his scoreless streak was snapped in the ninth when he loaded the bases before being taken out and then was charged for three runs. He struck out eight batters in the contest and picked up his second straight win. It's the first time this season that Baker has earned wins in back-to-back starts. The right-hander will next face the Cubs for the first time in his career. He's 6-2 with a 3.88 ERA in eight career Interleague starts.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins is scheduled to make his return from the disabled list and his return to the rotation in the series opener against the Pirates at the Metrodome. The left-hander, who went on the DL with an inflamed nerve in his left elbow, pitched seven scoreless innings in the second of two rehab starts for Class A Fort Myers. This will mark Perkins' first career start against Pittsburgh. The lefty is 2-0 with a 4.26 ERA in three career Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: After a stretch of up-and-down results, Maholm steadied himself in his most recent outing. He limited the Braves to one unearned run on four hits in seven innings on Thursday. Though he's not known for being an overpowering pitcher, Maholm also finished the game with eight strikeouts, a new season high. Efficiency and first-pitch strikes continue to be the key for Maholm, who has just one win in his last nine starts. This will be Maholm's second career start against Minnesota. He did not factor in the decision of his 2006 start against the Twins in which he allowed three runs on five hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano wasn't lights-out in his last start against the A's on Wednesday, but he was effective enough. He delivered his second straight quality start, giving up three runs on five hits over his six innings while striking out seven. It still wasn't enough to earn him a "W," but the Twins have been pleased by the fact that Liriano has limited the big inning in each of his last two starts after going just four innings in each of his previous three. The left-hander will try to continue the success in his next start against the Pirates. Liriano has faced Pittsburgh just once in his career, allowing two runs over seven innings while earning the win in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Though his record doesn't show it, Snell has actually pitched decently in his last two starts. After struggling with his efficiency through much of the first two months of the season, Snell has pitched at least six innings in each of his last three games. His last two outings have each been quality starts. Still, Snell hasn't picked up a win since April 18, which could be weighing on his psyche just a bit. Snell lost to the Twins back in 2006, allowing three earned runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-handed sinkerball pitcher has quietly become one of the most effective starters for the Twins this season. Blackburn was cruising through his last start against the A's, throwing seven scoreless innings while allowing just three hits, before finding trouble in the eighth. He gave up three runs in the inning and erased what had been a 3-0 Twins lead. He's still managed to deliver quality starts in nine of his 13 outings, five of which he's allowed one earned run or none. He'll next face the Pirates for the first time in his career. Blackburn is 2-0 with a 4.34 ERA in three career Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: For the fifth time this season, Duke finished eight innings his last time out. Only four of his 13 starts this year have lasted fewer than six innings. The only concern for Duke may be that he has given up five homers in his last two starts after allowing just four in his first 11 games of the season. This will be Duke's first career start against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey produced a season-high 10-strikeout game in his last outing, a 7-4 victory against the Cubs on Friday. He surpassed his previous season high of eight strikeouts by the fifth inning. In fact, 10 of Slowey's first 16 outs came via the strikeout, and he struck out the side in both the second and fifth innings. He faltered a bit in the sixth, allowing three runs, but he protected the lead to earn his team-high ninth victory.
away_pitcher_note: Working on six days' rest worked wonders for Oswalt in his last start on Saturday, when he held Arizona to five hits for seven innings and claimed total control of both his fastball and curve for the first time this season. A touch of tendinitis in his right wrist had pushed back that start, and the little breather may prove to have been enough to launch him on an extended streak. Oswalt certainly sounded confident following the victory over the D-backs, which restored his faith in his breaking pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Baker yielded two runs on five hits while striking out five and walking none in seven innings, earning a no-decision against the Cubs on Sunday. He was in command for much of the game, throwing 70 of his 98 pitches for strikes. It marked his third consecutive quality start and his fifth on the season. Over his last three starts, Baker is 2-0 with a 2.86 ERA. He has never faced the Astros but owns a 6-2 mark in Interleague Play in nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler picked up his third win of the season Sunday in Arizona by holding the Diamondbacks to three runs and six hits in six innings in another twist in his up-and-down season. The outing prior to beating the Diamondbacks, he gave up eight hits and five runs in three innings in a loss to the Cubs. Because he pitched so many years with Detroit, Moehler is not stranger to the Twins. He's 2-4 with a 4.65 ERA in 10 career starts against Minnesota, and is 8-10 with a 4.07 ERA in 33 games (27 starts) in Interleague play. He's never won in two career starts in Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins allowed just two runs on seven hits over six innings Tuesday in his first start after coming off the disabled list. The left-hander walked one and struck out four while earning the win. It was a bit of an up-and-down start for Perkins. He retired the side in three of his six innings but gave up a two-run homer in the third and loaded the bases with one out in the fifth before getting an inning-ending double play. Perkins will next face the Astros, a team he has never faced. But Perkins holds a 3-0 record with a 3.96 ERA in four Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off one of his better performances of the 2009 season June 10 against Chicago, the left-hander was roughed up Tuesday against the Texas Rangers in Arlington when he gave up six hits, including three home runs, six runs and walked six batters. Rodriguez started the season 5-2, but has lost four of his last five starts and four consecutive decisions. In his only previous career appearance against the Twins, he pitched 6 2/3 innings and allowed three runs (two earned) on June 21, 2006, in Houston. Rodriguez is 5-5 with a 4.59 ERA in 13 career Interleague starts.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan didn't appear in the Brewers' three-game trip to Minnesota, a three-game Twins sweep in which Milwaukee was outscored, 23-8. He has mostly struggled in his five starts at home this season, going 1-3 with a 5.47 ERA at Miller Park and a .314 opponents' average. But he did hold the White Sox to two runs in 6 2/3 innings in his last home start, despite allowing nine hits. Suppan will be working on regular rest for this start despite the team's off-day on Monday because the Brewers are using a four-man rotation until June 27.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano went six or more innings for the third straight game, but came up short Wednesday against Pittsburgh. The lefty made two mistake pitches as he allowed a pair of two-run Pirates homers en route to picking up his eighth loss, with his last win coming on May 9. He's 5-1 lifetime in Interleague Play, and all five wins were in 2006. Liriano is 2-0 in two career starts against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Looper surrendered three home runs and had a fourth overturned by instant replay on Friday in Detroit but nearly got a mulligan when rains set in with the teams four outs shy of an official game. Alas, Mother Nature let up just long enough for the Tigers to score a rain-shortened win. Looper is winless in his four June starts with a 7.97 ERA and a .322 opponents' batting average. He faced the Twins at the Metrodome on May 23 and was charged with four earned runs in six innings of a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn picked up his first career complete game his last time out, going the distance and giving up just one run on six hits against Pittsburgh. He continued to effectively use his sinker and slider down in the zone, inducing ground ball outs against the first six batters he faced. Most of his outs came on ground balls, as he struck out just two Pirates batters.

home_pitcher_note: Burns was recalled from Triple-A Nashville on Tuesday, and Brewers manager Ken Macha said Burns will start Thursday in place of Dave Bush, who went on the 15-day disabled list with triceps tear in his right arm. Macha said Bush will be on the disabled for two or three weeks, with Burns taking Bush's spot in the rotation for that time. This will be the first career start for Burns, who is in his second stint with Milwaukee this year. He made his Brewers debut on June 2 in Florida, scattering four hits over four scoreless innings in a 10-3 loss. It was his only appearance with the Brewers this season. In 12 starts for the Sounds this year, Burns is 7-2 with a 2.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't his best performance of the year, but Saturday marked the third straight quality start for Baker. He had to labor through the outing, however, throwing 101 pitches in 6 1/3 innings against Houston, allowing three runs. Baker didn't factor in the 6-5 Astros win. It was the first time in four starts he wasn't able to complete the seventh inning. He'll go his fourth quality start in a row against the Brewers. He is 3-2 with a 5.01 ERA in five career starts vs. Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright threw six innings and allowed five runs against the Royals in his last start. The Cardinals' offense piled up the runs, so Wainwright scored another victory, his third in a row. But it wasn't exactly easy. Wainwright surrendered three runs in the first inning and a solo homer in the second. But after the early trouble, Wainwright settled down and pitched scoreless frames in innings three, four and five. He allowed another homer in the sixth and exited after throwing 90 pitches. Wainwright has been an innings eater in 2009 -- he's lasted at least six innings in 12 consecutive starts. And lately, he's been the beneficiary of some great run support. The Cardinals have averaged 12 runs per game in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Some early trouble in the first inning proved costly for Perkins in his last start. Three runs by the Astros was all that Houston needed as the Twins suffered a 4-1 loss. Perkins wasn't helped by the fact that his defense missed a couple of plays in the inning, but the left-hander settled in after the trouble. He allowed just one run on five hits after that first inning as he went seven innings on the day. He walked one and struck out one in earning his fourth loss of the season. Next up for Perkins will be his first career start vs. the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Wellemeyer's getting frustrated, and so are the Cardinals. Neither manager Tony La Russa nor pitching coach Dave Duncan will actually say that Wellemeyer is on thin ice, but once Kyle Lohse returns to the rotation, they'll surely have to at least consider bumping Wellemeyer rather than Brad Thompson. He's got at least one more chance to get sorted out, though, and Saturday's home game against the Twins is it.
away_pitcher_note: Even on a night when Slowey clearly didn't have his best stuff, he limited the Astros to just one run over six innings. He scattered just three hits and struck out six but walked four, tying his career high set on June 17, 2007 vs. Milwaukee. He also battled some stiffness in his right side (soreness in his ribs) that caused the Twins to push back his start to the end of the rotation. The 25-year-old is now tied with Roy Halladay for the Major League lead in wins (10). With Halladay on the DL, Slowey will try to take the lead on his own when he faces the Cardinals in his next start. It will be his first career appearance vs. St. Louis

home_pitcher_note: Pineiro lost five straight starts before his last one, but he was much better than that. It's still remarkable that he's sitting on eight losses, as he's been consistently solid. He's throwing his fastball, and more specifically his sinking fastball, more than ever before. And it's working out nicely. Pineiro loves pitching at home, so this could be another good one.
away_pitcher_note: It had been six weeks since his last win but Liriano picked up a "W" for the first time since May 9 in his last start vs. the Brewers. The win wasn't the easiest as Liriano labored through five innings, allowing three runs on seven hits and walking five. He threw a career-high 117 pitches in the outing and barely did enough to earn the win. But still, a win is a win and the Twins will see if Liriano can earn his second in a row when he faces the Cardinals for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar had a perfect game going through four innings last Wednesday night at Houston, indicating he'd regained the sharpness he seemingly lost in his previous start. Hochevar went seven innings against the Astros, giving up just two runs on three hits, although he didn't get a decision. He threw 93 pitches, not quite up to his spectacular 80-pitch complete game on June 12 against the Reds but pretty satisfying. In his last four starts since being sent briefly to Triple-A Omaha, Hochevar has a 3.71 ERA with a 2-1 record.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn became the first Twins pitcher in more than a decade to pitch back-to-back complete games -- the last being Brad Radke in June 1998 -- but the Blackburn's second one was a loss. After allowing just two runs to the Brewers over his first 7 2/3 innings, Blackburn gave up two in the bottom of the eighth and the winning run scored on his throwing error. Despite the disappointing finish, Blackburn continues to be a model of consistency. He is 1-0 with a 2.00 ERA in three career appearances (two starts) vs. the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Basically, Bannister was beaten by Lance Berkman virtually single-handedly in last Thursday's 5-4 Royals loss at Houston. Berkman's two homers knocked in four of the Astros' runs, and he contributed to the other with a single. Other than that, Bannister gave up just three hits in his six innings. A couple of his three walks turned into runs, too. However, Bannister continued to induce more ground-ball outs (nine) than flyouts (six), an indication that he has been able to keep his pitches down. Bannister has been pretty effective in his past four starts, though he has just one win to show for it. He faced the Twins on May 2 and gave up six runs (three earned) in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Baker extended his winning streak to three in his last start, against the Brewers, giving up three runs on four hits over six innings. All three of those runs came in Baker's final inning, during which he gave up two home runs. Baker has started to get things back on track, having delivered five straight quality starts after a shaky start to the season. He will next face the Royals. Baker is 5-3 with a 3.03 ERA in 10 career starts against Kansas City.

home_pitcher_note: Meche has given up four home runs in his last two starts. He had given up just two in his previous 14 starts. The right-hander has lost both of his most recent starts, putting him three games below .500 for the second time this season. Meche is 1-0 against the Twins this season, although his ERA is a hefty 6.00. He is also only 1-4 at home, posting a 6.12 ERA in eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins delivered his best start since returning from the disabled list when he held the Cardinals to just one run over seven innings. The left-hander did not issue a walk and struck out three as he picked up his second win in the last three starts. Perkins said that he's been starting to find a feel for his pitches after missing a little over a month with an inflamed nerve in his left elbow. Next up Perkins will face the Royals in the series finale. He's 0-0 with a 4.40 ERA in five career appearances (two starts) against Kansas City.

home_pitcher_note: The heat and humidity in St. Louis seemed to take a toll on Slowey as he lasted just three innings and allowed five runs on six hits in a start against the Cardinals. The right-hander struggled to find a way to get Albert Pujols out and that was what cost him a chance at picking up a Major League leading 11th win in the contest. The right-hander will get another chance at that number when he faces the Tigers at home in the series opener. Slowey is 3-0 with a 4.57 ERA in four career starts vs. Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers called up the 23-year-old from Triple-A Toledo Sunday to work out of the bullpen before he makes his first Major League start Friday at Minnesota, replacing fellow Tigers prospect Alfredo Figaro. There's more a little bit of strategy involved in putting the left-hander up against a Twins lineup centered around left-handed hitters Joe Mauer and Justin Morneau, but French also has a very good case that he's been the best pitcher in the Tigers farm system over the last month. He has given up four earned runs on 16 hits with 26 strikeouts over 23 innings in his last three starts, though he hasn't won any of them. Further back he has lasted at least 6 2/3 innings with two earned runs or less in five of his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano delivered his best start of the season in St. Louis when he held the Cardinals to two runs on four hits over seven innings. The left-hander was finally able to get ground balls in the contest, with 12 of his outs coming on groundouts. Liriano has been struggling to deliver longer outings and his rotation spot was in jeopardy before the start. But now he'll see if he can continue the success when he faces the Tigers in the holiday contest. Liriano is 3-1 with a 4.50 ERA in eight career appearances (six starts) vs. Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson hasn't won in his last four starts, including a no-decision for his seven innings of three-run ball in the Tigers' comeback win Sunday at Houston, but his stinginess is all over the American League leaderboards. He's second in the AL to Zack Greinke in ERA, second in hits per nine innings, and third in WHIP ratio. Yet his 5.15 runs of support per nine innings as the pitcher of record ranks lowest on the Tigers staff and near the low among AL starters. His last outing with more than three earned runs allowed came against the Twins, who put up four seventh-inning runs on him in defeat May 4 at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn delivered his eighth straight quality start for the Twins in his last outing but had to work his way out of trouble a few times in his six innings vs. the Royals. Blackburn allowed three runs (two earned) on 10 hits -- only the second time he's given up 10 or more hits in a start this season. The right-hander said he gave up too many two-out hits but was pleased by his ability to work out of trouble. He'll next face the Tigers, a team he's 1-3 against in five career appearances (four starts) while posting a 5.76 ERA over 25 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello surrendered five runs on nine hits in 4 1/3 innings against the A's on Monday. He pitched his way into trouble in the fourth, but was able to limit the damage to two runs, inducing a double play ball to strand a runner at third. Porcello didn't have the same luck in the fifth. Mark Ellis hit a two-run shot to left, then Matt Holliday pushed the lead to 5-0 with a RBI groundout to knock Porcello out of the game. He'll look to rebound against a Minnesota lineup he held scoreless over seven innings on May 5.

home_pitcher_note: Baker labored through five innings in his last start against the Royals, throwing 111 pitches while allowing just one run to earn his sixth win of the season. His pitch count was driven up by many long at-bats, including a 15-pitch at-bat against Willie Bloomquist and an 11-pitch at-bat against Tony Pena Jr. While it was a hard-fought win, the right-hander is coming off a successful June in which he went 4-0 with 3.20 ERA in six starts. Baker will try to do more of the same in July when he faces the Yankees to open up the month. Baker is 2-0 with a 1.50 ERA in two career starts vs. New York.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia had a rare bad outing on Thursday night, allowing six runs in 5 2/3 innings to the Mariners while picking up the loss. Despite having what manager Joe Girardi called his best fastball of the season, he struggled to keep the ball down and was rocked for 10 hits, including a home run by Franklin Gutierrez. Nevertheless, the left-hander has remained the Yankees' best pitcher this season.

home_pitcher_note: With Glen Perkins running a fever right-hander Swarzak will start in Perkins' place. Swarzak originally rejoined the rotation in the place of Kevin Slowey, who is on the 15-day disabled list due to a strained right wrist. Swarzak  impressed during his first stint in the Majors, particularly after he held the Cubs scoreless over seven innings in his final start before being sent back down to Triple-A Rochester. This will be Swarzak's first career start against New York.
away_pitcher_note: Burnett has been brilliant of late, living up to the expectations the Yankees had of him when they signed the right-hander to a lucrative free-agent contract in the offseason. In his last start on Friday, he worked seven innings, allowing just two runs while striking out seven against the Blue Jays. Burnett has surrendered just three earned runs in his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano is expected to be moved up for this start after Anthony Swarzak was moved up a day to fill in for an ill Glen Perkins. The lefty picked up his second straight quality start, throwing seven innings while allowing three runs against Detroit in his last outing. His one mistake was a pitch he left up to Magglio Ordonez, who turned it into a three-run home run. Liriano didn't factor in the 4-3 Twins win, but he pitched well enough to keep Minnesota in the game. His eight strikeouts were his second-most all season, yet another sign that things are starting to come around for the lefty.
away_pitcher_note: Needing a replacement for the injured Chien-Ming Wang, the Yankees tabbed Aceves over Sergio Mitre, who had been excelling in Triple-A. One of the team's most effective relievers this season, Aceves has made only four career starts, all of them down the stretch last season. He was 1-0 with a 2.74 ERA in those outings, and has been perfect in two career innings against the Twins, coming on in relief to earn the victory in both of those games.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn's best pitch -- his sinker -- was at its best against the Tigers on Sunday, when the right-hander pitched his third complete game in his past four starts.
