Or is it the one with a flat slider and inconsistent command who struggled to five runs, four earned, on six hits in 3 1/3 innings last time out on Saturday at Chicago before the Tigers came back? How well Robertson commands his arsenal in the series finale could determine whether the AL Central remains a race into the season's final weekend.
away_pitcher_note: Thanks to quite a bit of offensive support, Baker was able to pick up win No. 14 of the season in his last start at Kansas City. Baker allowed four runs over 6 1/3 innings to the Royals as the Twins delivered a total of 11 runs in the blowout victory. The right-hander settled down for the middle of his outing at Kauffman Stadium, retiring a string of 13 straight batters after giving up back-to-back solo homers to start the second inning. The tests only get tougher for Baker, who will be the final pitcher in the Twins' critical four-game series with the Tigers. He's 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA in three starts vs. Detroit this season.

home_pitcher_note: Francisco Liriano made the last turn of the rotation in this spot, but he didn't make it out of the second inning against the Royals. So the Twins will instead turn once again to the man Liriano had replaced in the rotation, Manship. The rookie hasn't been effective in his four previous starts, pitching fewer innings in each one. His best start came against the White Sox on Sept. 1, when he allowed one run over five innings. Manship did pitch 3 2/3 innings of relief after Liriano's early exit vs. Kansas City and gave up one run on three hits with five strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: This will be DiNardo's last chance to make a favorable impression for next year. Since being called up from Triple-A Omaha, he's made four starts. The first two were pretty good; the last two not-so-good. He gave up eight runs in five innings to the Red Sox on Sept. 21 and seven runs in five innings to the Twins last Saturday night. Give him a break in the latter case; an error made only three of those runs earned. DiNardo, a lefty who doesn't throw that hard, needs to keep the ball down and induce ground balls to be successful.

home_pitcher_note: The Twins have decided that they will bring back Blackburn on three days rest for this start against Kansas City. Monday's rainout in Detroit pushed back Blackburn's scheduled start to the first contest of the doubleheader on Tuesday. Blackburn said after his solid start in that contest that he would be happy to pitch on short rest, but he's never done it in his Major League career. If the Twins are no longer in contention by Saturday, Blackburn could see a shortened start.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke makes his last push for the AL Cy Young Award against the Twins, the team he tamed last Sunday at Kansas City. Facing them for the first time, he held them to one run on seven hits in seven innings of a 4-1 win. Greinke now has given up just two earned runs in his last six starts, and he's 4-0 in that stretch with a 0.43 ERA. With 237 strikeouts, he's just seven shy of Dennis Leonard's Royals record of 244 set in 1977. In his 32 starts this season, Greinke has given up one or no runs in 18 of them. With a 2.06 ERA, he could post the lowest American League ERA since Pedro Martinez's 1.74 in 2000.

home_pitcher_note: The Twins looked to the veteran Pavano to deliver against the Tigers on Wednesday. A win would have pulled Minnesota to within a game of Detroit with another game to play against the Tigers. Instead, Pavano had his worst outing as a Twin, allowing seven runs on seven hits while lasting just 4 2/3 innings. He'll be going on just three days' rest when he takes to the hill in a game that could make or break Minnesota's playoff chances. He's 3-3 with a 6.63 ERA this season against Kansas City, but 2-1 versus the Royals as a Twin.
away_pitcher_note: The big inning always seems to find Hochevar. Last Monday night in the Bronx, the Yankees scored one run in the fourth, fifth and sixth innings, and just as Hochever seemed to be exercising good damage control, New York dropped a five-spot on him in the seventh before he could get a single out. After surrendering just two home runs in his previous seven starts, Hochevar gave up two to the Yankees including a grand slam. Twice this season, the right-hander has pitched complete-game victories, and in one nine-start stretch, he had a 6-1 record. But he has been 1-9 since.

home_pitcher_note: Baker will go for the Twins in game No. 163 against the Tigers in a game that will decide the AL Central champion. It will be the right-hander's second crucial game against Detroit in as many starts, as Baker also faced the Tigers Thursday to help the Twins split the four-game series. In that start, Baker picked up the win by pitching five innings, allowing only one unearned run. He's been Minnesota's strongest pitcher during the second half of the season, going 12-4 since July 12. He is 1-1 with a 6.75 ERA in four starts against the Tigers this season.
away_pitcher_note: The AL Central tiebreaker between the Tigers and Twins will be unlike any of Porcello's previous 30 starts this season. He has pitched in high-pressure situations like Fenway Park in midsummer, Busch Stadium in a big Interleague Play matchup, and the Metrodome a few weeks ago to start Detroit's key three-game series there. Still, the last time Porcello pitched in a true win-or-go-home situation was likely high school. "I'm sure he's pitched in a tough environment," manager Jim Leyland said, "but I doubt that 50 scouts down the right-field line freezing their tails off in New Jersey somewhere is going to be like this." Porcello has two quality starts in as many tries against the Twins over the past 2 1/2 weeks, but he received two runs of offensive support in those two games combined. At the Metrodome this season, he is 0-2 and allowed seven earned runs in 10 innings.

home_pitcher_note: One of manager Joe Girardi's easiest decisions this season was to give the Game 1 assignment to Sabathia, far and away his team's best pitcher this season. In the thick of the AL Cy Young Award race, Sabathia improved as the season went on, posting a 9-0 record and 2.04 ERA in August and September. Though Sabathia faltered a bit in his final regular-season start against the Rays, preventing him from winning 20 games for the first time in his career, he should be well-rested and prepared for his yet-to-be-determined Game 1 assignment. Against the Twins, he is 1-0 with a 1.29 mark.
away_pitcher_note: The Twins will put the rookie left-hander on the hill to start Game 1 against the Yankees. Duensing, who spent the early part of the season pitching for Triple-A Rochester, has made just nine Major League starts. After being moved into the rotation in on Aug. 22, Duensing has put up an impressive 5-1 record with a 2.59 ERA in nine games. The only time he has faced the Yankees in his career was in a relief role back in early July, in which he gave up four earned runs in 2 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The major news heading into the ALDS revolved around Burnett, who will pitch to Jose Molina rather than Jorge Posada in Game 2. Thats a testament to how well he has fared throwing to the Yankees backup catcher, who has caught each of his last six starts. With Molina behind the plate, opposing hitters are batting .221 off Burnett this season. With Posada, they are batting .270. Burnett has also pitched markedly better at home than on the road this season, with a 3.51 ERA at Yankee Stadium and a 4.59 mark everywhere else. Burnett, who hasn't lost a game since Sept. 12, has a 2.77 ERA against the Twins this season.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn gets the nod in Game 2 for the Twins and has experience in big games after pitching against Chicago in last season's tiebreaker game, a 1-0 White Sox victory. The right-hander hasn't lost since Sept. 11, a game in which he allowed six earned runs in just three innings against Oakland. Since that start, though, he's posted a 2-0 record in four starts with a 1.65 ERA. He made one start against the Yankees this season and was hit for four earned runs in 7 2/3 innings but didn't factor in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano, who will start Game 3 for the Twins, has the most postseason experience on Minnesota's pitching staff, as he pitched in the World Series with the Florida Marlins in 2003. Since joining Minnesota in early August, Pavano has posted a 5-4 record and 4.64 ERA in 12 starts. Pavano has faced the Yankees -- his former team -- twice this season, both while with the Indians. He didn't factor into the final decision in either game. He allowed just one run in six innings in an outing at Yankee Stadium back in April and held the Yankees to three runs in 7 1/3 innings in late May.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte was touched up for three earned runs on six hits and four walks in just 4 1/3 innings against the Rays on Saturday to fall to 14-8 on the season. Regardless, the veteran lefty said physically he felt fine and will be ready to go for Game 3 of the American League Division Series.  He is a career 9-5 with a 3.70 ERA when facing Minnesota.

summary: 2010-03-11 - Baltimore Orioles @ Minnesota Twins (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Slowey has showed he's plenty healthy, not to mention effective, by pitching 21 innings with a 1.71 ERA. He has 17 strikeouts against three walks on the spring.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia will make his first game appearance since being notified that he had won the competition to be the Cardinals' fifth starter. Garcia was excellent all spring, pitching at least as well as any other Cardinals hurler -- not just the other contenders for the fifth job.

home_pitcher_note: He doesn't throw in the mid-90s, and he doesn't scowl and growl on the mound, creating the image of a fierce competitor. But Weaver's strength -- apart from his cross-firing deception and wide range of pitches -- is his intense ability to focus and perform under duress. His poise and command are what should enable him to settle in as the Angels' ace, replacing good buddy John Lackey. Weaver led the staff in '09 with 33 starts, 16 wins (tying Joe Saunders), 211 innings and 174 strikeouts. In Game 2 of the AL Division Series against the Red Sox at Angel Stadium, he held Boston to a run on two hits across 7 1/3 dominant innings. He's 2-1 with a 2.61 ERA in postseason play, striking out 22 men in 20 2/3 innings with a 1.07 WHIP. His developing two-seam fastball complements his four-seamer, and his changeup and slider are top shelf. Weaver, who lost, 3-2, in the 2008 season opener in Minnesota, is 3-1 with a 3.51 career ERA in six outings against the Twins. He's 27-12 with a 3.27 mark in 53 career starts at home.
away_pitcher_note: Baker proved again this spring why he's at the top of the Twins rotation. The right-hander impressed the coaching staff by carrying over some of the changes that he made at the end of last season, particularly his ability to make adjustments within innings. And unlike last spring when he gave up a total of nine homers, he's been able to limit opposing hitters to just one home run through his first 19 1/3 innings of spring. After missing out on his Opening Day start last year due to right-shoulder stiffness, Baker is in line for the honor once again. This time it will come against the defending AL West champion Angels at Angel Stadium. In six career starts in Anaheim, Baker is 0-4 with a 5.88 ERA

home_pitcher_note: An All-Star in 2008, Saunders is hoping to carry his sizzling finish to 2009 into the new season. No pitcher in the game was hotter down the stretch than the lefty from Virginia, who won his last seven decisions in eight starts after spending 19 idle days allowing inflammation in his pitching shoulder to recede. The shoulder had bothered him off and on all season, but he pitched through the pain before finally going to the DL in early August. With Roy Halladay moving to the NL, Saunders has more wins (33) the past two seasons than any AL pitcher, changing speeds effectively behind a low-90s fastball. The Angels' Opening Day starter last year, he shut out the A's over 6 2/3 innings on three hits. He's 3-1 with a 4.10 ERA in four career starts against the Twins and 23-12, 4.43 in 52 outings at Angel Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Despite dealing with some usual spring soreness in his right knee, Blackburn’s spring went about as well as the pitcher could have hoped. Last year, Blackburn was a consistent presence in the rotation – putting together his second straight season with an 11-11 record and nearly identical ERA (4.05 in ’08 and 4.03 in ’09). The Twins rewarded the pitcher with a four-year, $14 million contract this spring – a year before he was arbitration eligible. Now they’ll see if Blackburn can continue to provide them with innings as he’s been right around the 200-inning mark in each of the past two seasons.  But Blackburn has struggled at Angel Stadium, going 0-2 with a 9.72 ERA in two career starts there.

home_pitcher_note: Motivated to return to 2008 All-Star form, when he was one of the AL's dominant starters with 214 strikeouts in 219 innings, Santana had a blip in the spring when he missed a start with an inflamed bursa sac in his right elbow after bumping against a chair. But he came back with lively stuff and is confident his premium mid-90s fastball is back, along with a darting slider and changeup. He lost 3-4 mph off his fastball last season after forearm stiffness cost him the first five weeks, and he returned to the DL. But he put together a strong second half (7-3, 3.90) to salvage the season, delivering at least six innings in 11 of his final 12 starts. He's 2-2 with a 5.13 ERA in seven lifetime outings against the Twins and always has been tough at home: 32-19, 3.74 in 69 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Last season Pavano's mission was to prove to people that he could still pitch in the Major Leagues. Coming off four injury-plagued seasons with the Yankees, Pavano got an opportunity at a second chance for his career with the Indians. He proved that he can still be a productive veteran by going a combined 14-12 with a 5.10 ERA in 33 starts between the Indians and Twins. Now that he knows he's healthy again, Pavano's goal is to pitch deeper into games and once again reach the 200-inning mark. He'll start off trying to do that by facing the Angels. He's 2-1 with a 5.13 ERA in four career starts against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: New team, new league, same game. Pineiro says he sees no reason why the formula that worked so well for him last season in St. Louis can't continue to create sinking strikes and groundball outs with the Angels. Making his two-seam fastball a major component in his arsenal, along with a quality breaking ball and changeup, Pineiro delivered his best work last year since 2003-04, when he was a combined 30-18 while averaging 203 innings for Seattle. He has evolved from a hard thrower to a location artist. Pineiro struck out 105 while walking only 27 in his career-high 214 innings in 2009. He led the Majors in fewest walks per nine innings (1.14) and highest percentage of ground outs (.641). He is 2-6 with a 4.32 ERA in 14 career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey saw an impressive 2009 season halted by a wrist injury that required season-ending surgery in July. It came after the pitcher delivered 10 wins before the All-Star Game, earning him mention as a possible All-Star selection. But despite coming off wrist surgery, the control pitcher has not shown any signs of it affecting him. The right-hander put up some solid numbers in Grapefruit League play and was pleased by how he was able to command all of his pitches with his surgically repaired wrist. First up will be a start against the Angels. He's 1-0 with a 4.76 ERA in two career starts at Angel Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Moving Danks to the fourth spot in the rotation gives the White Sox two left-handers to throw in the first weekend of the season against the Twins' left-handed-laden lineup. Danks is coming off his second straight stellar season, having set a career high with 13 victories and 200 1/3 innings pitched. He yielded just 184 hits, while striking out 149, but did walk 72 unintentionally. Danks focused much of Spring Training on getting his curve and changeup over for strikes consistently. He brings in a 4-5 career record against Minnesota and has a 13-19 mark at U.S. Cellular.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a strong winter ball performance in the Dominican Republic, Liriano was able to carry that success into Spring Training and beat out Brian Duensing for the fifth starter's spot. The left-hander has appeared to regain that nasty slider and has been better locating his fastball -- something he struggled with during a disappointing '09 season. With Liriano's confidence level as high as its been since he underwent Tommy John surgery in November of 2006, the Twins are hoping he can perhaps recapture some of the magic from his phenomenal rookie season. That will begin with Liriano opening up the series against the White Sox in Chicago. Liriano is 0-3 with an 8.50 ERA in three career starts at U.S. Cellular Field.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia returns full-time to the White Sox starting rotation for the first full season since 2006. It was a no-brainer for the team to pick up his $1 million option after Garcia posted a 3-4 record with a 4.34 ERA over nine starts in 2009. Garcia finished 3-2 with a 3.66 ERA in his final six starts of the year. The right-hander sits 40 games over .500 for his career, at 121-81, and has a 9-5 record with a 3.83 ERA against the Twins. He is 20-15 lifetime at U.S. Cellular.
away_pitcher_note: Baker got off to a shaky start in his first outing of the season, giving up four runs on five hits over 4 2/3 innings. Baker admitted to having a few jitters for his first start, which were likely compounded by the fact that it was his first career Opening Day start. The right-hander did retire nine straight batters at one point in and he appeared to get more comfortable as the outing went along. One thing that the starter can work on is making better two-strike pitches; he was hurt by them against veteran hitters like Hideki Matsui. Baker's next start comes against the White Sox at U.S. Cellular Field, where he's 2-1 with an 8.40 ERA in three career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Opening Day was darn near perfect for the White Sox left-handed ace during the team's 6-0 victory over the Indians at U.S. Cellular Field. Buehrle gave up three singles over seven scoreless innings, throwing 63 of his 95 pitches for strikes. He struck out three and walked one during his franchise-record eighth Opening Day start. Buehrle also made what just might be the defensive play of the year on the first day of the season, deflecting a Lou Marson fifth-inning grounder with his left shin on a hockey goalie-like kick-save and then scooping it with his glove with a no-look flip between his legs to first baseman Paul Konerko, who caught it barehanded for the out.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn didn’t appear to show any effects in his first start of being limited this spring by some right knee soreness. After some early adrenaline faded away, Blackburn used his sinker -- which has developed even more movement -- to keep the Angels off-balance for most of the night. Blackburn allowed just three runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking four in the contest. Blackburn said that he and catcher Joe Mauer will continue to work on making sure they have a good handle on his sinker’s movement. Next up, Blackburn will face the White Sox in Chicago. He is 2-4 with a 3.48 ERA in seven career starts at U.S. Cellular Field.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano will get the honor of starting the first regular-season game at Target Field, and considering the way he pitched in his last start, it's an apt choice. Pavano looked every bit the veteran pitcher while holding the Angels to just one run over seven innings. He scattered six hits and struck out six while working his way out of early-inning jams, including a bases-loaded, one-out situation in the second. As someone who pitches to contact, Pavano praised the Twins' defense and said it's given him confidence to be aggressive on the mound -- something the Twins hope he can continue to do all season. His second start of the season will come against the Red Sox, and he's 2-3 with a 7.07 ERA in six career starts vs. Boston.
away_pitcher_note: The power lefty will be the first opposing pitcher to throw a pitch in an official game at the Twins' new ballpark, Target Field. He labored in his first start, giving up five hits and four runs over five innings in a no decision against the Yankees. He threw 94 pitches, 53 for strikes. Lester has struggled throughout his career in April, going 2-3 with a 4.71 ERA. Lester is 0-1 with a 5.66 ERA in four career appearances against the Twins. Lester has held opponents to a .257 average lifetime in his career. He has made 47 career starts on the road, going 19-11 with a 4.17 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey delivered a solid outing in his first Major League game since last July when he faced the Angels in Anaheim last week. The right-hander held the potent Angels lineup to one run on seven hits over 5 1/3 innings. And there were no signs of trouble at all with his surgically repaired right wrist. Things weren't perfect for Slowey, as he worked his way in and out of trouble, but he managed to find his way out of jams -- including one in the fifth inning with runners on first and second and no outs. This will Slowey's first official start at Target Field. Slowey is 1-1 with a 4.63 ERA in two career starts vs. Boston.
away_pitcher_note: The big right-hander was everything he was advertised to be in his first start for the Red Sox, firing six shutout innings against the Yankees. Lackey left with a 1-0 lead, but wound up taking a no decision. This will be Lackey's first road start in a Boston uniform. In his career on the road, Lackey is 53-39 with a 3.91 ERA. Lackey has been almost equally successful against righties (.255 average) and lefties (.269 in his career. He will follow Jon Lester and become the second visiting pitcher to ever pitch at Target Field. Lifetime against the Twins, he is 6-5 with a 3.75 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a strong Spring Training in which he earned the fifth spot in the rotation, Liriano hoped to carry that success into the regular season. He showed flashes of brilliance in his first start against the White Sox. He needed just 15 pitches to get through the fourth and fifth innings but he also had some command issues, walking five over his six innings. He gave up three runs on four hits while striking out three. Liriano will next face the Red Sox in his first-ever start at Target Field. Liriano is 0-2 with a 13.50 ERA in two career starts against Boston.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer will close out this six-game road trip for the Sox when he makes his second start of the season. Wakefield pitched well his last time out in Kansas City, giving up two runs over seven innings. He left in position to get the win, but the Red Sox's bullpen squandered the lead. Wakefield is a career 26-22 pitcher in April with a 3.89 ERA, which is his lowest of any month. Lifetime against the Twins, Wakefield is 14-5 with 4.16 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After a shaky first start in Anaheim, Baker bounced back in his next start against the White Sox. He held the White Sox to one run on five hits over seven innings. It was a much-improved outing from when he was unable to make it out of the fifth inning in the club's Opening Day loss. Baker credited the ability to make a few mechanical adjustments for his turnaround, including getting the ball down and having an improved breaking ball. Baker is 7-3 with a 3.16 ERA in 12 career starts against Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke went winless in his first two starts, although he pitched reasonably well. On Opening Day against the Tigers, he went six innings and gave up just one earned run. In his second start against the Red Sox, he went 6 2/3 innings and gave up four runs. He was humming along nicely until being zinged by back-to-back homers. That illustrated how different his year has gone when contrasted against his spectacular 2009, when he was 6-0 with a 0.40 ERA in his first six starts and didn't give up a home run until June. There's no doubt that teams are trying to be patient against Greinke and lay off his normally devastating slider. That's made Greinke try to alter his bag of tricks, too. Last time out, for example, he tried more curveballs than usual.

home_pitcher_note: After a strong first outing in Anaheim, Blackburn got behind a couple of hitters in his second start against the White Sox and it proved troublesome. The right-hander allowed five runs on eight hits over 7 2/3 innings. He gave up three home runs in the contest and has now allowed four home runs in 14 1/3 innings this season. In the previous two seasons, Blackburn gave up a combined 48 homers, which tied teammate Scott Baker for the eighth-most in the American League over that span. Blackburn will try to limit the number of long balls when he faces the Royals in his first start at Target Field. He is 1-2 with a 3.40 ERA in seven career appearances (six starts) against Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Meche's first start was delayed by a stiff shoulder that he encountered in a Spring Training outing. That occasioned two games against Minor Leaguers in Arizona, and he didn't make his 2010 debut until last Sunday against the Red Sox. That did not go well. Meche lasted just 3 1/3 innings and gave up seven runs on eight hits, and he used up 88 pitches while he was at it. The good news was that his shoulder did not tighten on him. The bad news was that his release point was all over the place and he could not command his pitches very well. His fastball hit 95 mph, but almost all of them were up, and hittable, in the strike zone. In his career, Meche is 9-6 with a 4.64 ERA against the Twins, including 5-4 at their old home at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano has proven to be the steadiest of the Twins' five starters through two turns of the rotation. The veteran right-hander has managed to limit two potent lineups -- the Angels and the Red Sox -- to just two runs on 10 hits while striking out 10 over 13 innings. In his last start, the inaugural home opener at Target Field, Pavano pitched six innings and allowed just one run while working his way out of any trouble spots. He’s yet to give up a homer this year and the Twins hope he can continue that success when he faces the Royals in his next outing. Pavano is 4-4 with a 7.08 ERA in nine career appearances (eight starts) vs. Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Hochevar, in the season's seventh game, finally got the rotation's first victory despite a good run of pitching by the starters. He went five innings in Monday's 10-5 victory at Detroit, giving up four earned runs and six hits. His downfall came in the sixth, when he began the inning with two walks and a two-run double by Brandon Inge. Hochevar was miffed at himself for not throwing strikes when he had a five-run lead. Yet, in a rare occasion, the bullpen followed him with four straight scoreless innings. Hochevar was more effective in his first outing, also against the Tigers, when he worked 7 2/3 scoreless innings. In his career, he's 1-2 with a 6.04 ERA in four games against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: After two starts, Slowey is still trying to find his groove. Slowey was uncharacteristically wild in his last start against the Red Sox on April 14 at Target Field when he walked four batters in just five innings of work. Slowey also gave up three runs on five hits while striking out five Boston batters during his first loss of the season. In his first start of the season, Slowey earned a victory over the Angels by pitching 5 1/3 innings. Despite the fact that Slowey gave up seven hits, he gave up just one run, walked two and struck out three. Slowey is facing an Indians team that is struggling at the plate with just one hitter, Shin-Soo Choo, who is hitting better than .300.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson had a rough beginning to his start against the Rangers on Wednesday, but then he settled in. Trouble was, it was too late to avoid the loss. Masterson went six innings, allowing four runs, two of which were earned, on nine hits with no walks and nine strikeouts. He improved his performance against left-handed hitters, and he obviously had some dominant moments, as the strikeout totals indicate. Now he just has to apply what he did over the last three innings to the length of his next outing against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano had an impressive start in shutting out the Red Sox on April 15 at Target Field. The left-hander reminded the Twins how dominant he can be when he has his slider working. Liriano gave up no runs and just four hits while striking out eight and walking just two over seven innings of work. Liriano wasn't as impressive in his debut in a no-decision in an extra-inning victory over the White Sox on April 9, but still earned a quality start. Liriano logged six innings giving up three runs on four hits. He also walked five and struck out three. Liriano will look to extend his scoreless inning streak past seven when he next faces the Indians.
away_pitcher_note: Huff was masterful in a complete-game victory over the Rangers on Thursday. He turned in a 104-pitch effort, throwing 71 pitches for strikes. He never needed more than 16 pitches to complete an inning, and he threw exactly 12 pitches in five innings. He allowed a two-run homer to Michael Young in the fourth inning, but that was the only real damage against him. He walked one and struck out four. Huff has only 25 starts at the Major League level, and he's won 12 of them. He's an intense competitor who knows how to win. And if he keeps pounding the strike zone like he did against Texas, he's going to keep piling up the wins.

home_pitcher_note: Baker was effective for the second straight outing in a victory over the Royals on April 16 at Target Field. In a workman-like effort, Baker pitched seven solid innings and surrendered just two runs. Baker gave up seven hits, struck out six and didn't walk a Kansas City batter. The Twins' No. 1 starter should be fresh for his next start against the Indians, as he only threw 92 pitches against the Royals. Baker gave up just one run in his previous start against the White Sox and also pitched seven innings in a 2-1 win. He struck out three Chicago batters and walked just one.
away_pitcher_note: Talbot made his first win at the Major League level a memorable one Friday against the White Sox. He went the distance, allowing just two runs (only one of which was earned) on six hits with no walks and two strikeouts. He threw just 97 pitches, 68 of which went for strikes. He did a good job getting his sinker and cutter in on left-handed hitters. Talbot has a deep arsenal, including a changeup that can be devastating the second or third time through an opponent's lineup. The Indians want to see him be aggressive early and then work in the offspeed stuff. He was effective early, middle and late against the Sox and he hopes to take that momentum into his start at Target Field.

home_pitcher_note: It's been pretty frustrating for Meche as he tries to come back from a Spring Training setback caused by a stiff right shoulder. His first start against the Red Sox resulted in seven runs on eight hits in just 3 1/3 innings. The second outing, on Saturday at Minnesota, was better but he still gave up five runs in the second inning. However, it was encouraging that he rebounded from that and pitched four scoreless innings before retiring after a 109-pitch outing. Meche says there's no pain in his shoulder or in his back, a trouble spot in 2009. He's just still not happy with the way he's pitching. And now that the Twins got a good look at him in his last start, they get another shot at him in Kansas City. Meche is 9-6 against them in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano's first two starts of the year were outstanding, but his third against Kansas City on Sunday was a disaster. Pavano lasted less than four innings and gave up seven runs and 11 hits to the Royals. Every hitter in the Kansas City lineup, with the exception of one, had at least one hit off Pavano. The veteran right-hander struck out just two, but he avoided adding to his troubles by not walking any Kansas City batters. Pavano had won his first two outings, posting a 1.38 ERA, but Sunday's outing increased his ERA by more than three runs. Endurance should not be a problem for Pavano, when he gets another crack at the Royals when the Twins play at Kansas City, because he threw just 79 pitches Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: This means back-to-back starts for Hochevar against Minnesota, a team he beat last Sunday at Target Field. Hochevar wasn't at his best, doling out five walks along with six hits in his six innings. Yet he persevered, working his way out of tough jams and forcing the Twins to leave seven runs on base in the first four innings. And he finished strong, facing just six batters in his last two innings. Hochevar was very encouraged because he fared well even though he didn't have his best stuff or good command which is generally conceded to be a hallmark of a successful pitcher. He's 2-2 in his career against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: It was a second consecutive shaky start for Blackburn on Saturday at Target Field. Blackburn lasted just five innings and gave up five runs on seven hits. He threw just 73 pitches and complained about a throbbing in his arm after the start; he said it is similar to something he's experienced before and pitched through. The right-hander says he is not concerned that his arm discomfort is not anything serious. One thing plaguing Blackburn in the long ball. He gave up two more home runs on Saturday and has given up six home runs in fewer than 20 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister blamed himself for his poor outing against the Blue Jays on Monday, when he gave up seven hits, four walks and six earned runs in an 8-1 loss. He blamed his own preparation and a  lack of execution in making the right pitches. In another part of the clubhouse, Brayan Pena, who was making his first start of the season behind the plate in that game, pointed the finger of blame at himself. The catcher said he called a poor game and did not prepare properly and that it was not Bannister's fault. It would be safe to conclude that Bannister will be prepared for the Twins. He had two no decisions in his first two starts of the season, both against the Tigers. Each time he left with the lead. He had a complete-game win over the Twins on  April 13, 2008. He hasn't had a complete game since. Tough Twins vs. Bannister are Michael Cuddyer, 9-for-18 (.421), two homers and five RBIs; Justin Morneau, 9-for-25 (.360), two homers, four RBIs, Jim Thome, 8-for-24 (.333), three homers, four RBIs.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey was masterful in his last start, a win over the Indians, pitching eight innings while surrendering just one earned run on five hits. He struck out nine and did not issue a single walk. He threw 98 pitches, and it was the first time since last April he pitched so deep into a ballgame. Slowey had not pitched past the sixth inning in either of his two previous starts this season. Having walked a total of six batters over those two starts, Slowey looked more himself Tuesday -- the pitcher known for his strong command didn't issue a single walk in the contest. Next up for Slowey will be a start against the Royals in Kansas City. Slowey is 2-0 with a 2.50 ERA in three career appearances (two starts) at Kauffman Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: If the parallels between this year and Verlander's outstanding 2009 season ring true, as they seemingly have so far, this should be the start where Verlander's season turns for the better. He struggled through his first four starts last year, including outings in Seattle and Anaheim, before finding the form that dominated hitters for the next five months. The hitch to that theory is that Verlander admits he has mechanical issues he needs to work out in order to find his command, and that could take longer than a few days. He earned his first win of the season on Thursday against the Angels, but he needed 125 pitches over five innings to do it, something no Major League pitcher had done in a victory since 1997.
away_pitcher_note: Early on this season, Liriano has given the Twins glimpses of the pitcher who dominated the American League during his 2006 rookie season and was once considered one of the up-and-coming starters in the game. A little over three years removed from Tommy John surgery, Liriano is starting to trust his stuff once again. He's beginning to locate his fastball and use it to then set up his nasty slider and strong changeup. It's allowed the left-hander to get off to a strong start and look on the verge of perhaps becoming the Twins' top starter again. He'll have to continue the trend and next up is a test against the Tigers. Liriano is 3-1 with a 4.76 ERA in 11 career appearances (seven starts) against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer gave the Tigers exactly what they needed in his last start Friday against Texas, even if Detroit lost, 5-4. He went seven innings, helping provide a break for a bullpen that is pitching more than three innings per game. Scherzer has 17 strikeouts and seven walks in 24 innings. He has given up three home runs. He has been the Tigers' most consistent starter so far this season.
away_pitcher_note: Baker called his last start one of the "best-worst" outings of his career. In other words, the right-hander felt like he had really good stuff against the Indians but it didn't deliver the results he wanted. Baker allowed six runs on 10 hits over 5 2/3 innings. Twins manager Ron Gardenhire felt that Baker left a few too many pitches up against an aggressive swinging Indians ballclub and that it was something he could improve upon his next time out. Baker will get that chance when he faces the Tigers in Detroit.  He is 3-1 with a 3.76 ERA in six career games at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Willis missed Saturday's start against Texas with flu-like symptons. He came back still under the weather to pitch an inning in relief on Sunday, walking three and giving up a two-run single in an inning. Manager Jim Leyland wasn't going to make Willis go much further than that, wanting to get him a tuneup for Thursday. Willis' biggest problem in his comeback season this year has been his command. He has 10 walks in 18 innings. He also has allowed 21 hits, a recipe for having the 5.00 ERA that he takes into his start against a Minnesota team he's faced once in the last three-plus seasons, allowing two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano got some redemption in his second straight start against the Royals. After giving up seven earned runs on 11 hits in just 3 1/3 innings against Kansas City at Target Field to pick up his first loss of the year, Pavano rebounded in the series opener at Kauffman Stadium. The right-hander allowed just two runs on four hits over seven innings, throwing first-pitch strikes to 21 of the 24 batters he faced. Still, Pavano was critical of himself after the contest, feeling he got into too many 2-1 and 3-2 counts. It's something he wants to work on his next time out. Pavano will next face the Tigers, a team he had a lot of success against in 2009. He was 4-1 with a 3.00 ERA in six starts vs. Detroit last season, three of those wins coming in four starts at Comerica Park.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona is coming off his best start of the season, giving up just one run on seven hits -- all singles -- over 7 1/3 innings and picking up win No. 3 against the A's, a team he has struggled against. Carmona, as he has throughout the season, pounded the strike zone. Against Oakland, he didn't walk a batter for the first time this season. He's 3-6 lifetime against the Twins with a 5.11 ERA and has allowed 66 hits in 61 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a masterful eight-inning start against the Indians, Slowey had difficulty finding the strike zone in last outing against the Royals. He threw 104 pitches over 5 1/3 innings as he allowed four runs on eight hits while walking three. Slowey was all around the strike zone, manager Ron Gardenhire said, but he couldn't seem to make enough adjustments. While Slowey's strikeout-to-walk ratio last season was an impressive 5.00, third-best among all American League starters, this year he hasn't been able to deliver the same results as this year it's 2.11. Slowey is 1-1 with a 2.57 ERA in two career starts at Progressive Field.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson had his second straight rough outing Sunday in a loss to the A's. He gave up eight hits and seven runs and was chased without retiring a batter in the fifth after Kevin Kouzmanoff ripped a three-run double, putting the A's ahead, 7-0. Masterson again struggled with his control. He walked four and threw 96 pitches in his short stint. In his previous start, he walked five and threw 96 pitches in four innings against the Twins. He has now lost nine straight decisions and is 1-11 since coming to the Indians from Boston in a trade on July 31 last year.
away_pitcher_note: Manship will make his first start for the Twins this season, taking Kevin Slowey's place in the rotation after Slowey filled in for Nick Blackburn on Friday. Manship is 2-2 with a 3.48 ERA in four starts for Triple-A Rochester this season, and in sporadic appearances last season, he was 1-1 with a 5.68 ERA in 31 2/3 innings. His first two outings were against the Indians, and in a combined 2 2/3 innings, he allowed one hit and walked two, giving up no runs. Grady Sizemore, who drew a walk against Manship, is the only current Indian who has reached base against the right-hander.

home_pitcher_note: Huff didn't let walks get the best of him, as he had in his previous start against the Twins, but he nonetheless wasn't very efficient in a loss to the Angels on Monday. Huff allowed five runs on 12 hits with one walk and four strikeouts in just 5 1/3 innings. He worked his way out of a couple jams, but he gave up two home runs en route to his second loss in as many starts. When he tossed a complete game against the Rangers on April 15, Huff pounded the strike zone to induce quick outs. He needs to get back to that mentality when he faces the Twins for the second time in two weeks.
away_pitcher_note: One of the biggest questions for the Twins coming into the 2010 season was whether Liriano could duplicate his fantastic results from winter ball. So far it hasn't been difficult for the left-hander, whose 0.93 ERA is lowest among all American League pitchers. Liriano extended his career-high scoreless streak to 23 consecutive innings in his last start by shutting out the Tigers for eight innings. It's the second-longest active scoreless streak in the Majors behind only the Mets' Mike Pelfrey who has thrown 24 consecutive scoreless innings. A key for Liriano's success has been better command of his fastball as well as increase in confidence. He'll try to duplicate that success when he faces Cleveland for the second time this year. He pitched eight scoreless against the Tribe in that only start at Target Field.

home_pitcher_note: Baker is coming off back-to-back disappointing outings and he'll have to face the Tigers for a second straight time after they tagged him for five runs on nine hits over four-plus innings his last time out. The Twins had handed Baker a 6-1 lead heading into the fourth inning on Wednesday night, but Baker would give back nearly all of those runs in a tough inning. The right-hander got a lot of balls up in the zone during his start against Detroit, and he admitted that he didn't feel like he had good stuff at all against the Tigers.  He'll try to see if he can turn things around in his next start, this one coming at Target Field. Baker is 1-1 with a 5.68 ERA in two starts at the Twins' new home so far this season.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer had his first quick hook as a Tiger in his last start, chased in the fourth inning Wednesday by a three-run Twins rally. He'll get his chance at a rematch, this time starting the Tigers' first game at Minnesota's new Target Field, but he'll have to do a better job of keeping the ball in the park. He has given up five home runs over his last four outings, including two to the Twins, while his ratio of groundouts to flyouts is almost even. The good news for him is that he has quality starts in each of his previous three outings on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn is set to come off the family medical emergency list for Tuesday's game. The Twins put Blackburn on the list Friday so he could tend to an undisclosed family situation, moving Kevin Slowey ahead in the rotation. Blackburn has not won since his first start this season, although his last two outings have been no-decisions. Blackburn will have his first shot this season against the Tigers, against whom he was 1-1 in three starts last season. In 19 1/3 innings last season against Detroit, Blackburn allowed eight earned runs against the Tigers, striking out 11 and walking five.
away_pitcher_note: Not since 2006, his younger years with the Florida Marlins, had Willis thrown six-plus scoreless innings with six or more strikeouts until Thursday, when he commanded the strike zone against a Twins lineup that initially waited for him to throw strikes before trying to attack him early. The Twins get another shot at him Tuesday at Target Field, and they'll likely have Joe Mauer and Justin Morneau back in their lineup after they were missing in the finale. If Willis can continue to get the late movement on his fastball to get opponents to mishit balls, he has a good chance at continued success.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey will be pitching on normal rest after pitching a day ahead last weekend against the Indians, when Nick Blackburn was placed on the family medical emergency list. Slowey mostly stayed out of trouble until the fifth inning, but pulled out the win after allowing just three runs on nine hits and no walks. Slowey fanned six in that outing. Slowey hasn't faced Detroit this season. Last year, the right-hander went 1-0 in two starts, the victory resulting from an eight-hit, two-walk effort in which he allowed a run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello returns to the site of his AL Central tiebreaker gem looking to regain his old form. Both Porcello and the Tigers believe the 21-year-old is close to getting back his old sinker that opponents would beat into the ground for outs last year. A mechanical tweak to raise his arm angle and change his release point in his delivery helped him work the Angels for nine ground-ball outs over 5 1/3 innings Friday night at Comerica Park. He gave up five runs on eight hits in the process, but much of that damage came around when Torii Hunter jumped on a first-pitch slider for a three-run homer.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano took the loss in his last start, going the distance in a 3-0 setback on the road against Detroit. Across eight innings, Pavano had five strikeouts and scattered seven hits, walking two. Just two of the runs he allowed were earned. Pavano's solid outing was undone by Dontrelle Willis, Joel Zumaya and Jose Valverde combining for a shutout. Pavano is pitching on an extra day's rest after straining his neck in the loss to the Tigers. The last time Pavano faced the Orioles was in 2008, when Pavano was a Yankee. Pavano beat the Birds that day, walking one and giving up six hits and two earned runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bergesen made his first start on Saturday night since he was optioned back to Triple-A to regain confidence and conviction with his pitches. At times on Saturday, he appeared to have both, but he struggled to establish a consistent sink on his fastball, giving up two solo homers and allowing four runs over five innings. Bergesen called Saturday's win one of the ugliest victories he's been a part of, but the O's will take it. He will look to get closer to last season's form on Thursday in Minnesota. Bergesen has made one career start against the Twins, tossing six innings of three-run baseball.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano got off to a shaky start in his last outing against the Indians. His 23-inning scoreless streak came to an end in the first inning when he allowed two runs, one on a groundout and another on a balk. Part of the troubles were due to Liriano and rookie catcher Wilson Ramos trying to get on the same page during Ramos' Major League debut. Once the two went back to having Liriano throw mostly fastballs, he got back on track. Liriano threw a career-high 123 pitches over seven innings, finishing with nine strikeouts. He allowed three runs on three walks and eight hits. Liriano has only faced the Orioles once in his career, on June 11, 2006. He pitched seven shutout innings against them.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood entered Sunday's contest knowing runs would be at a premium given his mound counterpart, Boston's Josh Beckett. The veteran and ace of the Orioles' staff cruised through four innings before yielding a 402-foot homer to Jason Varitek with two outs in the fifth inning. J.D. Drew sent Millwood's first pitch of the seventh over the center-field wall to tie the game at 2. They were the only runs Millwood allowed all day. As has been the case in each of his six starts, Millwood gave the O's a chance to win, which they did, 3-2, in extra innings. But a "W" still eludes the right-hander, despite him  allowing more than three earned runs just once in six starts. Millwood will look to buck the trend against the Twins in their brand-new ballpark. He is a career 0-7 with a 5.90 ERA in 12 starts against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano got off to a shaky start in his last outing against the Indians. His 23-inning scoreless streak came to an end in the first inning when he allowed two runs, one on a groundout and another on a balk. Part of the troubles were due to Liriano and rookie catcher Wilson Ramos trying to get on the same page during Ramos' Major League debut. Once the two went back to having Liriano throw mostly fastballs, he got back on track. Liriano threw a career-high 123 pitches over seven innings, finishing with nine strikeouts. He allowed three runs on three walks and eight hits. Liriano has only faced the Orioles once in his career, on June 11, 2006. He pitched seven shutout innings against them.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie rebounded from his worst outing of the season to toss a solid start on Monday night against the Yankees. But while the Orioles right-hander shined for the better part of seven innings, it was a 1-0 pitch to unlikely hero -- and No. 9 hitter -- Randy Winn that erased any chance of Guthrie getting his elusive first win inside the concrete walls of the new Yankee Stadium. Like most of the O's starters, Guthrie is winless, but it's not due to poor performance. He has quality starts in five of his six outings this season and will try to add to that record on Saturday at Target Field. Guthrie is a career 1-0 with a 2.84 ERA in four starts against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: In his second straight start against the Tigers, Baker managed to do something that eluded him in his first outing -- hold onto a big lead. He held Detroit to just three runs on seven hits over seven innings. Coming off two disappointing outings in which he had allowed a total of 11 earned runs in 9 2/3 innings, Baker turned things around in his previous start. He cruised through his first three innings, retiring seven of eight batters in one stretch. Baker said he made a mechanical adjustment as well as trying to throw more balls in the strike zone, since the Tigers are an aggressive swinging club. Baker will see if he can deliver another solid start when he faces the Orioles. Baker is 3-0 with a 2.93 ERA in five career starts against Baltimore.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood entered Sunday's contest knowing runs would be at a premium given his mound counterpart, Boston's Josh Beckett. The veteran and ace of the Orioles' staff cruised through four innings before yielding a 402-foot homer to Jason Varitek with two outs in the fifth inning. J.D. Drew sent Millwood's first pitch of the seventh over the center-field wall to tie the game at 2. They were the only runs Millwood allowed all day. As has been the case in each of his six starts, Millwood gave the O's a chance to win, which they did, 3-2, in extra innings. But a "W" still eludes the right-hander, despite him  allowing more than three earned runs just once in six starts. Millwood will look to buck the trend against the Twins in their brand-new ballpark. He is a career 0-7 with a 5.90 ERA in 12 starts against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn struggled out of the gate this season, posting a team-high 6.85 ERA in his first four starts. And when asked about his struggles, Blackburn said that he felt he'd been overthrowing early on -- thus his pitches had flattened out. But in his last start against the Tigers, Blackburn rebounded thanks in large part to a resurgence of his sinking fastball as he pitched a complete game. He gave up three runs to the Tigers while scattering 11 hits over nine innings, throwing just 95 pitches. The right-hander got 18 of his outs via ground balls, and the Twins hope to see similar results in his next start against the Orioles. Blackburn is 0-2 with an 8.38 ERA in two career starts against the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: Matusz was dealt a tough loss in his last outing as the left-hander allowed three runs -- one earned -- to the Yankees at Yankee Stadium, but the O's were able to score only one run off A.J. Burnett. Matusz allowed three runs over five innings for a no-decision against the Twins last season.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey helped the Twins complete a sweep of the Tigers on Wednesday, improving his record to 4-2. In the game, Slowey pitched 5 2/3 innings and gave up three runs. All of his earned runs came off solo home runs, but he had the support of the Twins' bats to produce enough hits to hold off the powerful hitting Tigers. Before that game, Slowey hadn't given up more than one home run this season. In total, Slowey gave up seven hits in the game and walked two batters. He also had three strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: As the team's fifth starter, Garcia has been as consistent as any member of the White Sox rotation aside from John Danks. Garcia gave up just two runs on 10 hits over six innings in his last start, against the Royals, to pick up his first victory of the season. The win helped Garcia avoid an 0-3 start for the first time in his career. Garcia fanned four and didn't issue a walk, throwing a mere 84 pitches before giving way to the bullpen. Garcia took the loss in his only start this season against the Twins, but he gave up just two runs on three hits over seven innings. Garcia has a 9-6 career record with a 3.76 ERA against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano suffered some tough luck in his last start against Baltimore last Thursday. The Twins veteran right-hander pitched eight solid innings and gave up just two runs, while striking out eight Orioles batters. Pavano's lone mistake of the outing was a hanging breaking ball that went for a two-run homer in the 2-0 loss. Pavano yielded six hits and three walks in throwing 97 pitches against Baltimore. Since the Twins had an off-day Monday, Pavano should be well rested pitching on five days' rest when Minnesota welcomes the Chicago White Sox to Target Field.
away_pitcher_note: Danks will hope for a little more run support in his next trip to the hill, as he gave up two runs over seven innings on Thursday against Toronto, only to get the hard-luck loss when the offense was shut out. Six starts into the season, Danks has turned in five quality starts and has not allowed more than two earned runs in any of his six starts. Danks' first start of the campaign was against the Twins, as he went six innings and gave up two runs -- one of them earned. That got him a no-decision. The southpaw is 4-5 lifetime against the Twins with a 5.13 ERA. Even though Danks has started against the Twins more frequently than any other team in his career, this is his first start in the brand-new Target Field.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett will try to bounce back from his roughest start of the season when he takes the mound against the Twins, whom he last saw in Game 2 of the American League Division Series in New York -- a six-inning, one-run no-decision. Burnett had the ball on May 9 at Fenway Park and was belted for nine runs (eight earned) on nine hits in 4 1/3 innings, suffering his first loss this year after starting unbeaten in six starts. Burnett is 2-1 with a 3.72 ERA in six career starts against the Twins, including 1-0 with a 2.77 ERA in two regular season starts as a Yankee in 2009.
away_pitcher_note: Baker put up a solid performance last Saturday against Baltimore, increasing his career record against the Orioles to 4-0. He is also 2-0 with a 2.40 ERA in his last two starts combined. Baker retired the first 11 batters in Saturday's game, and allowed only three of the 27 total batters to reach base. He had eight strikeouts in the outing, which was his most since July 18, 2009. Baker pitched eight innings and gave up only one run on three hits. The one run he did give up came on a home run by Luke Scott in the fifth inning. The other two hits were singles. Baker threw 97 total pitches, 71 of which were strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte will try to stay unbeaten this year as he draws his seventh start, this one against the Twins. Pettitte was skipped a start, reluctantly, with an inflamed left elbow but said that he is ready to go against Minnesota. He left his May 5 start against the Orioles after five innings, allowing one run on six hits over 77 pitches in a 7-5 New York win. Pettitte won his only regular-season start against the Twins last year, hurling 6 2/3 innings of four-run ball on May 18 at Yankee Stadium. He is 9-5 with a 3.70 ERA in 19 career starts against Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano snapped a personal four-game win streak, recording a loss for the first time since Sept. 27, 2009, in his last outing against Baltimore Saturday. Liriano gave up five runs over six innings, the most runs he has allowed since August of last season. Two stolen bases led to two runs with help from the steady hits produced by the Orioles. Six different Orioles got hits off the left-handed pitcher, four of those players coming up with multiple hits. Baltimore's 10 total hits off Liriano are the most he has given up since May 25, 2009. Liriano threw 94 pitches and struck out three batters and walked one.

home_pitcher_note: Because of Wednesday's doubleheader, the Yankees will call on Mitre to start the finale of their series with the Twins. The right-hander's only start of the season came in his last outing, when he allowed the Tigers four runs (three earned) over 4 1/3 innings in a losing effort. Out of the bullpen, Mitre has a 2.79 ERA this year.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn had his best outing of the year in throwing seven shutout innings in a 6-0 victory over Baltimore on Sunday. It marked Blackburn's first career victory over Baltimore. The right-hander gave up just four hits and two walks. Blackburn used his defense as much as possible as he didn't strike out any Orioles hitters. Because of off-days Monday and Thursday, Blackburn will be pitching on six days' rest when he pitches at Yankee Stadium. Against Baltimore Blackburn threw a total of 100 pitches, 68 for strikes. He has done particularly well in the month of May with a career record of 7-3 with an ERA of 2.88.

home_pitcher_note:
After a strong start to the season, Eveland 
has hit a bit of a lull out of the back end of the Blue Jays' rotation. Over his past four outings, the finesse left-hander has gone 1-2 with a 7.40 ERA. The lone victory during that stretch came after Eveland logged seven shutout innings against the White Sox on May 6. One start later, the lefty surrendered six runs on six hits over four innings, during which he walked four and fired off 102 pitches. Eveland will aim to return to the form that he displayed against Chicago and over his first three appearances of the season. Out of the gates, he went 2-0 with a 1.93 ERA in three turns. Eveland has posted a 1.80 ERA in three career games against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: A trend has developed for Slowey so far this season and it's been his inability to pitch deep into outings. The right-hander had an eight-inning gem against the Indians on April 20 at Target Field, but it's the only one of his seven starts in which he has pitched past the sixth inning. Early on in Slowey's last start against the White Sox, it looked like he might be turning things around. Slowey needed just 39 pitches to get through four innings, but he threw 36 pitches while facing nine batters in the fifth as he couldn't even finish the frame. Slowey gave up five runs -- all in that fifth inning -- as he lasted just 4 2/3 innings against Chicago to pick up his third loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum only received three runs of support in his last outing, but that proved to be enough for the right-hander to avoid another no-decision or a hard-luck loss. On Wednesday in Boston, Marcum held the Red Sox to no runs on just two hits across seven sharp innings. He struck out six and walked just one. Over his past five starts, Toronto's No. 1 arm has fashioned a 2-0 record to go along with a tidy 2.06 ERA. Dating back to the start of the 2007 season, Marcum has opened an outing with at least six shutout frames. In his career against Minnesota, Marcum has gone 1-1 with a 4.26 ERA over three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano's record certainly doesn't necessarily reflect how well the veteran has been pitching for the Twins this season. Besides one abysmal start against the Royals in which he allowed seven runs, Pavano has been a bright spot in the rotation -- having not allowed more than two earned runs in six of his seven starts and pitching at least six innings in each of those outings. But it hasn't resulted in wins since Pavano has received the least run support of all the Twins starters. Having allowed just two runs over seven innings against the White Sox in his last start, Pavano will next face the Blue Jays. He is 3-4 with a 5.59 ERA in nine career starts against Toronto.

home_pitcher_note: Buchholz has struggled with his command of late, walking five batters in each of his past two starts. But unlike two starts ago when that lack of control hurt him in a loss to the Yankees, Buchholz thrived en route to a victory over Detroit in his last outing. He gave up just three hits and one run over 6 1/3 innings. Buchholz hasn't fared particularly well at Fenway this season, going 1-3 with a 4.84 ERA. Interestingly, he has been dramatically better on the road, posting a 3-0 record and a 1.86 ERA in three starts. Buchholz is 16-17 in his career. Opponents are hitting .269 against him this season.
away_pitcher_note: Baker pitched effectively for the majority of his last start against the Yankees, but it was in the seventh inning that he found trouble. After Baker gave up an infield single to lead off the seventh, Derek Jeter then hit a hard liner back up the middle that ricocheted off Baker's right leg and into shallow right field for a double. Baker would exit the game after being struck, but he was tagged for five runs on 10 hits over six-plus innings. He nearly matched his career high in strikeouts, falling one short with nine. And the best news was that Baker's right knee was fine the day after he was struck by that line drive. He is expected to stay in line for his next start and face the Red Sox. In his career, Baker is 0-1 with a 4.30 ERA in three appearances (two starts) vs. Boston.

home_pitcher_note: Lester has been Boston's best pitcher over the last few weeks. His last start wasn't quite as dominant as some of his recent outings, but he was still pretty effective, giving up four hits and four runs while walking four and striking out 10 over seven innings. Lester has gone seven innings or more in each of his past four starts. This will be his second outing of the season against the Twins. The first one wasn't very good, as he gave up nine hits and four runs over five innings in the debut game at Target Field. This time, Lester will be at Fenway, where he is 2-1 with a 3.98 ERA this season.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano was serviceable in his last outing against the Yankees, allowing only three runs on nine hits over six innings. While he earned the loss, there were plenty of positives to draw on. For starters, he had seven strikeouts against one of the toughest lineups in baseball. What may have been even more impressive was his ability to keep the Yankees -- third in the American League in home runs -- inside the ballpark, extending his season's homerless streak. On the negative side, Liriano has given up 19 hits over his past 12 innings. Although manager Ron Gardenhire institutes a pitch-to-hit pitching philosophy, this trend could be worrisome. The left-hander is 1-2 with a 7.20 ERA lifetime against the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn thrives on location in order to be successful, which is evidenced by his 13 strikeouts over 46 2/3 innings this season. Fortunately, Blackburn has been able to curb the home run trend that plagued him earlier in the season, allowing no home runs over his past 20 innings. He also has issued more than two walks in a game only once this season -- April 6 against the Angels. In his last start vs. the Yankees, Blackburn went seven strong allowing only three earned runs for his third consecutive quality start. The right-hander is 0-1 with a 6.36 ERA in two starts against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: Bush was bumped up a day for his last start when lefty Doug Davis suddenly went on the disabled list with swelling around his heart. Bush did reasonably well on short notice, delivering a quality start, but a trio of RBI doubles by the Phillies, including one by opposing pitcher Cole Hamels, were enough to finish a Philadelphia sweep. This will be a tough assignment for Bush, who is 1-5 in six career starts against the Twins despite a respectable 4.38 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: A trend has developed for Slowey so far this season and it's been his inability to pitch deep into outings. The right-hander had an eight-inning gem against the Indians on April 20 at Target Field, but it's the only one of his eight starts in which he's pitched beyond 5 2/3 innings. Even though Slowey only lasted five innings against the Blue Jays during his last turn in the rotation, he picked up the win and improved to 5-3 on the season with an ERA of 4.70. Slowey allowed three runs on eight hits with no walks to Toronto. His only major blemish was a two-run home run to American League Player of the Week Jose Bautista in the second inning. Next up for Slowey will be a start against the Brewers, a team he's 3-0 against with a 2.43 ERA in four career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Against the Reds earlier in the week, Gallardo battled command issues all night and issued a career-high six walks while throwing 120 pitches in six innings, just 66 for strikes. But he limited the damage to one run and six hits. "Certainly not your typical Yovani game," Brewers manager Ken Macha said. "A few too many walks. But you can't complain, just one run."

home_pitcher_note: Pavano has been solid in six of his eight starts this season, but when things go wrong for the starter they really go wrong. Such was the case in his last time out against the Blue Jays, when Pavano lasted just four innings while giving up six runs on 10 hits and throwing just 70 pitches. Pavano gave up runs in four consecutive innings to start the game, including two home runs, and saw his ERA inflate to 4.11 on the season. Although Pavano has delivered clunkers in two starts this year, he's pitched at least six innings and allowed two runs or fewer in each of his other six outings. The Twins hope he can find that form when he faces the Brewers. He's 2-2 with a 4.69 ERA in 11 career appearances (nine starts) vs. Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Scheduled Milwaukee starter Manny Parra was called into duty late Saturday when the Brewers went 12 innings in their 8-7 loss to the Twins at Target Field, leaving him perhaps available for duty, but not ready to start. Estrada will make his first Brewers start in Parra's place, despite throwing 21 pitches in relief Saturday while recording only one out. "I'm going to try to go as far as I can," Estrada said. "Right now, I feel good enough to pitch [Sunday]. I'll be ready." Estrada, claimed off waivers from the Nationals over the winter, made his only career start last season for Washington and allowed five runs and three hits in 2 1/3 innings of a loss to the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: After rain suspended Tuesday's game, Duensing will take the mound when the game resumes on Wednesday. Duensing has made an appearance in two games against the Yankees this season, pitching a combined one inning in those outings. He gave up one earned run and two walks in those appearances. It is his only earned run of the season. Duensing has allowed only two hits and has four strikeouts through 7 1/3 innings pitched this year.
away_pitcher_note: The Yankees did not announce who will be on the mound in the bottom of the sixth when they resume Tuesday's game on Wednesday, but Mitre is a likely candidate. The right-hander made two starters earlier this month, including one against the Twins on May 16. He allowed one run on four hits in five innings but did not get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: After rain suspended Tuesday's game, Duensing will take the mound when the game resumes on Wednesday. Duensing has made an appearance in two games against the Yankees this season, pitching a combined one inning in those outings. He gave up one earned run and two walks in those appearances. It is his only earned run of the season. Duensing has allowed only two hits and has four strikeouts through 7 1/3 innings pitched this year.
away_pitcher_note: The Yankees did not announce who will be on the mound in the bottom of the sixth when they resume Tuesday's game on Wednesday, but Mitre is a likely candidate. The right-hander made two starters earlier this month, including one against the Twins on May 16. He allowed one run on four hits in five innings but did not get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano will see familiar faces when he takes the mound Wednesday against the Yankees. This will be the second time Liriano faces New York in his past three starts. He gave up three runs on nine hits through six innings the last time he faced the team on May 15. That loss was followed by another loss in Boston where Liriano gave up five runs on five hits and two walks. The left-hander is on a three-game losing streak and is looking to rebound on home turf. After snapping his home winning streak against Baltimore earlier this month, he is looking to regain his composure at home and even his record against the Yankees this season. Liriano is 4-3 with a 4.04 ERA this season. He has 52 strikeouts through 52 2/3 innings. He had seven strikeouts in his May 15 outing against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte had by far his worst start of the season last Thursday against the Rays, surrendering seven runs (six earned) in five innings en route to his first loss of the season. It was also Pettitte's first loss in 14 starts dating back to October 2009. Pettitte was fabulous when he faced the Twins on May 15, shutting them out on two hits over 6 1/3 innings. The left-hander is 10-5 with a 3.53 ERA in 20 career starts against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn had a solid outing against the Brewers backed up by a strong offensive effort by the Twins. The only runs he gave up came on a three-run blast by Carlos Gomez in the seventh inning. Blackburn lasted 7 1/3 innings in that game, the fifth time this season he has made it to at least the seventh inning. In that game, he said he kept his pitches down to force the Brewers to hit grounders and gave up seven hits in that outing. Blackburn is set to face the Yankees for the second time in as many weeks. The right-hander recorded the only win against the Yankees in the previous three-game series. He gave up three runs and had four strikeouts in that contest. Blackburn is on a four-game winning streak and has an ERA of 4.50.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez was nothing short of phenomenal in his return to the rotation last Friday, holding the Mets to a single hit in six innings before leaving the game with a bruised finger incurred on a bunt. Vazquez had only 70 pitches at the time. It was the second straight good start and third consecutive impressive outing for Vazquez, who also pitched well in Detroit and in a rare relief role against the Red Sox. In 16 career starts against the Twins, Vazquez is 6-6 with a 5.11 ERA. He has not faced Minnesota since 2008 when, as a member of the White Sox, he won two of three decisions over the Twins despite a 6.61 ERA. Vazquez struggles in particular with Justin Morneau, who is 14-for-40 with six home runs off the right-hander.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Brewers, Slowey lasted 5 2/3 innings and gave up only two runs. He made it through four complete innings before allowing a runner to cross the plate. His other run came off a solo home run by Corey Hart in the sixth inning; he was pulled after that hit. Slowey gave up six hits and had five strikeouts in that outing. Slowey has lost only two of his 12 Interleague starts since the start of his career. The right-hander has had difficulty lasting deep into the game this season. He has lasted past the sixth inning only once this season, when he pitched eight innings against Cleveland on April 20. Slowey is on a two-game winning streak and has 43 strikeouts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis pitched six innings while giving up one run on five hits with four strikeouts in a 2-1 win over the Chicago Cubs last Friday. It was his first win since April 25, an 8-4 win over Detroit. In one career start and four relief appearances against the Twins, Lewis is 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA. In five starts on the road this year, Lewis is 1-2 with a 3.77 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano pitched well in his last outing against the Brewers, pitching eight innings and striking out five batters. Pavano allowed four runs in the game, three coming off home runs. The right-hander was given the loss due to lack of run support by the Twins, who left 14 men on base in that game. That has been a tough spot in Pavano's starts this season. The pitcher has the lowest ERA of the Twins starters, but has the least amount of run support with Minnesota scoring only 23 runs in his nine appearances. Pavano has lost four of his last five starts and is currently on a two-game losing streak. Despite his losing record, Pavano has pitched at least six innings in seven of his nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Cubs, Wilson suffered through a four-run first inning and finished the game with five runs allowed in 6 1/3 innings. Over his last two starts, Wilson's ERA is 10.80. Wilson has given up three home runs in his last two games after putting together 87 2/3 homerless innings dating back to last season. In 17 games against the Twins, Wilson is 0-1 with a 2.35 ERA and three saves. This will be his first career start against Minnesota.

home_pitcher_note: Baker pitched a solid five innings in his last start against the Yankees on Tuesday. Although the game was suspended after the fifth inning, Baker was strong throughout. He allowed only three hits and faced more than three batters only once in the game. The right-hander pitched down in the zone and struck out two batters in the outing. Baker continues to prove his strength at home, where he has a record of 3-1 and allowing only 12 of his total 18 earned runs this season. Baker walked only one batter against the Yankees, and has given up one or fewer walks in his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Cubs, Holland pitched six innings while giving up three runs on four hits with five strikeouts. All three runs came on home runs. In two career starts against the Twins, Holland is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA and seven strikeouts. But for his career, he is 2-6 with a 4.98 ERA in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Fister continued his impressive start to the season when he limited the Tigers to just three runs (two earned) over seven innings on Tuesday. He simply pitched to contact as he didn't allow a walk and struck out just one batter. Fister will be facing the Twins for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano has dropped his last three decisions after starting the season 4-0. In that stretch, he has given up 15 of his 21 total runs. However, Liriano looked good in his last outing, leaving the game with the score tied. He gave up only two runs and struck out seven batters Wednesday against the Yankees. He pitched through seven innings in that outing, the longest he has gone since his May 2 start against the Indians. He is holding left-handed batters to a .191 average, whereas right-handers are hitting .271 off Liriano. The left-hander has struck out 59 batters this season, 23 since his last win, which was also on May 2.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas was solid against the Tigers on Wednesday, allowing just two runs, but he lasted only five innings for his shortest start of the season. He suffered from some command issues as he walked three batters and needed 109 pitches to get through five frames, but proved he can get results even without his best stuff. He's made one career appearance against the Twins in relief, holding Minnesota scoreless for 1 1/3 innings when he faced the club last season.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn was strong in his last outing against the Yankees on Thursday. He pitched seven innings and gave up only two runs off nine hits. Blackburn is the only Twins pitcher who has been able to record wins against the Yankees in the past two seasons, getting two in the past two weeks. The right-hander is on a five-game winning streak and hasn't dropped an outing since April 11 against the White Sox. Despite his success, Blackburn credits his wins to the Minnesota offense. In his nine outings, the Twins have managed to put together 57 runs -- the most run support for any starting pitcher. This is compared to the 29 runs Blackburn has allowed this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lee shook off a shaky first inning in which he allowed two runs -- keyed by his wild throwing error to home plate -- but was simply sensational after that rocky first frame against the Angels on Friday. He allowed just three runs (two earned) over eight innings, allowing just four hits and two walks while striking out 10. He also recorded nine straight outs by strikeout, but was so locked in while on the mound he didn't even realize it until he was told after the game. The left-hander is 8-3 with a 3.57 ERA in 17 career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing Friday, Slowey held the Rangers to only one run and six hits through 6 2/3 innings.
