That start is the longest outing Slowey has had since he threw eight innings on April 20 against Cleveland. Pitching late into the game has been an issue for Slowey as he has made it past the sixth inning in only two starts this season. Pitching coach Rick Anderson said the right-hander has been working on his command and separating his hands quicker on his pitches, and that work showed in Friday's outing. Anderson said Slowey often overthinks his pitches, but his past two outings have been solid and Slowey is gaining confidence. Slowey had five strikeouts against the Rangers and gave up only one walk. His six wins are tied with Nick Blackburn for the most for the Twins and tied for second in the AL.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez didn't hesitate to call his performance against the Angels on Saturday his best of the season. The right-hander allowed only one run over eight-plus innings, with seven strikeouts and just six hits allowed. But he received just one run of support and remained winless for his seventh straight start. He is 3-3 with a 2.77 ERA in nine career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Pavano held the division-leading Rangers to only two runs on seven hits. Pavano has pitched well nearly all season, but the Twins' offense has not been able to give him much support in his starts. Entering his start Saturday, he had the least amount of run support of any Twins starter. However, after an eight-run effort by Minnesota in his last outing Pavano is now right along with his fellow starters. Pavano has allowed two runs or fewer in seven of his 10 starts this season. His one strikeout against the Rangers was his lowest mark of the year. He has 42 total strikeouts this season. In his last outing, he managed to get his ERA below the 4.00 mark for the first time since May 12.

home_pitcher_note: Braden, who left his May 25 start early due to a sprained left ankle, returned to the mound against the Tigers and surrendered five runs on 11 hits while walking one and striking out five in six innings. The ankle gave the A's lefty no trouble, but he allowed Detroit's leadoff hitter to reach base in each of his six frames. Two doubled, one homered and five scored, although manager Bob Geren insists it was simply about the Tigers finding holes. Braden will look to turn it around vs. the Twins, against whom he owns a 1-1 record with a 5.79 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Although he picked up the win in his last outing, Baker admitted it was his toughest performance of the season. The right-hander gave up three runs on eight hits to the Rangers. He also tied his season high of three walks, which was set in his April 28 outing against the Tigers. He said his difficulties came from not being able to get the ball down in the zone. In Sunday's outing against the Rangers, Baker snapped his personal two-game losing streak and improved his record to 4-1 in his last six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill has won his past three starts, the latest coming in a 4-1 win at Detroit on Monday. He allowed an earned run on five hits and a season-high four walks over 6 1/3 innings while striking out three. The 22-year-old has finished at least six innings in each of his last four starts and hasn't allowed more than three runs in the six starts since his season debut. After starting the season with Triple-A Sacramento, Cahill's spot in the rotation has been cemented with Justin Duchscherer's season-ending hip injury. Cahill is 2-0 with a 0.77 ERA in two home starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano picked up his first win since May 2 in his last outing against the Mariners. The lefty held Seattle to three runs on eight hits over six innings. Although Liriano wasn't as dominant in May as he was in April when he won the AL Pitcher of the Month Award, the lefty has delivered quality starts in three of his last four outings. His strikeout numbers have been solid and he's been giving his team plenty of opportunities to win. Now he'll try to see if he can continue that trend against the A's. Liriano is 0-2 with an 8.31 ERA in four career starts at Oakland Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez's string of three consecutive quality starts came to an end on Tuesday in a 9-4 loss at Boston. Gonzalez left the game with a 4-3 lead after the fifth inning, but the A's bullpen gave up six runs to give Gonzalez the no-decision. He struggled with his command on the evening, walking four batters and allowing seven hits over five innings while striking out five. The 24-year-old southpaw has thrown a career-high 108 pitches in each of his last two starts. Lefties are hitting just .145 against Gonzalez this year while righties are batting .250.
away_pitcher_note: May was a terrific month for Blackburn as he went 5-0 with a 2.65 ERA in five starts, but he didn't get off to a strong start in June. Blackburn lasted just 3 2/3 innings, allowing five runs on 10 hits in his shortest outing of the season. Prior to that outing, the Twins had lost only once in the past 13 starts Blackburn had made, dating to September of last season. The problem this time was that Blackburn couldn't get his sinker working and all of his pitches were coming out flat. He'll try to see if he can make the mechanical tweak to get his stuff going when he faces the A's in Oakland. Blackburn is 0-0 with a 5.79 ERA in three career starts at Oakland Coliseum.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing against Seattle, Slowey lasted deep into the game, pitching seven innings. That was his deepest start since going eight innings on April 20 against Cleveland. Slowey gave up one run on five hits and had three strikeouts in that outing. The right-hander had some difficulties in his last start against Kansas City on April 25. He pitched only 5 1/3 innings and gave up four runs on eight hits. He had a season-low two strikeouts in that game. Slowey is 4-1 in his last seven starts and has 27 strikeouts in that span.
away_pitcher_note: The last three times that Greinke has pitched, the Royals have scored zero runs while he's been in the game. Not that he was perfect himself. He had his worst outing of the season against the Rockies, leaving in the fourth inning behind, 7-0. The next time, it was a 1-0 loss at Boston. And the latest was against the Angels who went ahead, 4-0, before he departed. In the latter game, Greinke ran up 116 pitches in six innings, a high count for him and indicating he didn't have sharp command. A year ago, after 12 starts, Greinke had an 8-2 record and was heading toward the American League Cy Young Award. This year he lost his third start at Minnesota, giving up four runs (two earned) in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano's losing record is deceiving to the way he has been pitching this season. He has given up only 33 earned runs in his 11 starts, but the Twins have been unable to produce enough run support in those starts. However, Pavano did struggle in his last outing against Seattle. He gave up four runs on eight hits and walked two batters -- only the third time this season he walked more than one batter. He continued to prove he is the Twins' deep man, lasting seven innings, something that has been a tough spot for the starting rotation this season for Minnesota. This season, Pavano has given up nine runs on 11 hits in two games against Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a start in which he did not have his best stuff, Davies looks to rebound as the Royals travel to Target Field to take on the Twins. In his last start, against the Angels, Davies lasted four-plus innings, while giving up eight hits and six earned runs as he picked up his fourth loss of the season. Davies lacked control against the Angels as he walked two with no strikeouts. This will be Davies' first start against the Twins at Target Field. Davies is 4-5 with a 4.80 ERA in nine career starts against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Baker helped break a Twins losing skid in his last start when he pitched 7 1/3 innings against Oakland. He gave up four runs on six hits and had three strikeouts in that outing. He had a good start on April 16 against Kansas City. He gave up only two runs on seven hits. He also had six strikeouts and didn't walk a batter. Baker has had more success at home this season than on the road. He has only a 3.49 ERA at Target Field, but has a 5.66 ERA on the road. He has walked only 17 batters this season.
away_pitcher_note: Chen will make his third start of the season as he continues to fill in for an injured Gil Meche. The Royals had hoped Meche would be back in the rotation by June 10, but with Meche still injured, Chen will get the nod. In two starts this season, Chen is 1-0 with 3.00 ERA. In his last start, Chen pitched five innings, allowing only two earned runs on four hits. The two earned runs were charged to Chen after the bullpen gave up a homer with two of Chen's batters on base.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano had a solid outing against Oakland last time out to bring the Twins out of a downward slide. He pitched seven innings and gave up one run on five hits. He had 10 strikeouts in that game, tying his season- best that he set on April 27 against Detroit. Liriano has been good at keeping the ball in play this season, allowing only two home runs in 11 games. He has had more success against left-handed batters, holding them to a .179 average. That is compared to his .274 average against right-handed batters. The left-hander has walked only 21 batters through 72 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson's last outing on Sunday against the Dodgers was perhaps his worst outing of the season, and still, the 34-year-old yielded only three earned runs while completing seven innings. The right-hander has been just that good during his 2010 campaign. And recently -- especially since May 1 -- you'd be hard-pressed to find a pitcher who's been better. In his last eight outings, Hudson has completed 52 2/3 innings with a 2.05 ERA. And if not for rain shortening his start against the Marlins on May 27, Hudson would have completed at least 5 2/3 innings in every outing this season.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn had a tough outing against Oakland on Sunday, preventing the Twins from recording a sweep. He gave up five runs on 10 hits through 2 2/3 innings in that game. He had no strikeouts. He has pitched a combined 6 1/3 innings in his past two starts. In his past 10 games, he has given up five runs in half of them. He has a 14.21 ERA through the first two weeks of June after finishing May with a 5.86 ERA. His strength comes in his ability to not allow walks. He has given up only 14 this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe's past start severely skewed his recent pitching numbers. In four innings against the D-backs, the righty allowed seven earned runs and eight hits. But in his previous five outings before that one, the 37-year-old was 4-1 with a 2.45 ERA. Further, the righty continued his career-long characteristic of eating up the innings -- completing 33 innings during that period. Lowe has yet to complete a scoreless outing this season, but he does have three starts where he surrendered just one run. The forgettable D-backs start and a poor showing on May 7 against the Phillies have skewed upward Lowe's ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey was impressive in his last start against Kansas City on Tuesday. Slowey pitched seven innings, giving up no runs on three hits. He put no runners on base through the first four innings. He also had three strikeouts. Slowey is 5-2 in his past 10 starts and has given up only 23 runs in that span. He has an ERA of 0.64 in two June starts and hasn't allowed more than two runs in game since his May 17 outing against Toronto, in which he gave up three. He hasn't walked more than one batter since his May 9 start against Detroit, in which he walked two.
away_pitcher_note: In his most recent outing on Tuesday against the Twins, Medlen was forced to leave early due to a left shoulder injury that occurred when he slid into home plate. Prior to his exit, the 24-year-old completed five innings while allowing four earned runs. He's continued that trend during his last five starts. In them, Medlen has completed 30 1/3 innings with a 3.86 ERA. In three of those starts, he surrendered just two runs in each. Medlen's season-high innings total is 7 1/3 innings on June 1 against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing against Kansas City Wednesday, Pavano proved again he can pitch deep into a ballgame. He lasted eight innings for the fourth time this season. Pavano struggled with his command early in the game, giving up his only two runs in the third inning. However, he said he settled down after that and was able to pitch the way he had planned. This is not the first time the right-hander has struggled with his command early on, saying he can link it back through the past couple games. His two runs against Kansas City came off two four-pitch walks, something that is uncharacteristic of Pavano. He has walked only 13 batters this season. In his 12 starts this season, he has given up more than two runs in a game only four times.
away_pitcher_note: Cook held the Astros to two runs in seven strong innings in his last start, but the team's offensive woes led to a 6-2 loss at Coors Field. Cook has gone to his slider out of necessity because the sinker hasn't been as effective, but he used both effectively and forced 16 groundouts against the Astros. Cook is 0-3 with a 6.81 road ERA, but he held the D-backs to three runs in five innings and left his last road start with a 6-3 lead.

home_pitcher_note: Baker had a rough outing against Kansas City Thursday. He gave up back-to-back home runs early and finished his five-inning stint with five earned runs against him. That was his first loss since May 19 against Boston and was only the second time he lost at home this season, the first coming on April 22 against Cleveland. The right-hander has given up four home runs in his last two starts after giving up only seven in his first 11 starts. He has given up five or more runs only four times this season. Baker couldn't keep the ball down in the zone against Kansas City and the Royals took advantage of that. He has gone 3-4 in his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin struck out eight in six innings against the Astros on Thursday. He pitched well early, but Rockies manager Jim Tracy said the young righty allowed Houston too many chances.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano had a remarkable outing against Atlanta on Friday. He had a season-best 11 strikeouts, the most he's thrown since he threw a career-best 12 against Detroit on July 28, 2006. He had seven strikeouts in a row from the third to the fifth innings, which tied a Twins' best which was set by Jim Merritt on July 21, 1966, against Washington. He struck out hot-hitting Jason Heyward three times in that game and struck out two other batters multiple times. He improved to 87 strikeouts on the season after throwing double-digit strikeouts for the third time this season. Liriano didn't walk a batter in that game, also the third time he has done that this season. The left-hander is undefeated in Interleague Play in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez struggled a bit in the rain and cold during a rain-shortened 5-3 win against the Blue Jays in his last appearance. He still earned the win, his big league-best 12th of the season, and struck out six in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton is trying to recover from one of the worst starts of his career. He allowed nine runs in four innings Saturday in a 10-2 loss to the Boston Red Sox at Fenway Park. He is 1-5 with a 7.28 ERA after eight starts. Interestingly, he was 2-3 with a 7.11 ERA through eight starts last season. He went 10-5 with a 3.16 ERA in his final 23 starts, which is a silver lining for Blanton. He has been in dire straits before. He is hoping he can recover like he did last season.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn had a solid outing against the Braves on Saturday. He gave up only two runs on six hits through his seven-inning outing. His five strikeouts in that game were the most he has had this season. After going undefeated in his starts during the month of May, Blackburn has gotten off his hot streak, recording a record of 0-2 in three starts in June. He has an ERA of 8.10 in June as well. Blackburn is not known to walk batters, walking only two against the Braves. He hasn't walked more than two batters in a game all season.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels stepped up and shut down the Red Sox to avoid a sweep at Fenway Park on Sunday, giving his fifth straight quality start (not counting the rain-shortened outing against Atlanta on June 1). Hamels allowed only five hits and one run in seven innings while striking out eight to earn his first win since May 21. Since the beginning of May, the left-hander has a 3.08 ERA. More importantly, he's given up seven home runs in nine starts since allowing four in one start in Arizona on April 23.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey had a rough outing against the Braves on Sunday. He gave up four runs -- three earned -- in the first inning alone. He ended his 4 2/3-inning stint with five earned runs (six total) on nine hits. He gave up two home runs that night and also had a wild pitch. The outing snapped a personal three-game winning streak and was Slowey's first loss since May 11 against Chicago. One bright spot in that outing against Atlanta was his six strikeouts, which were the most he has had since he recorded six against Cleveland on April 20.

home_pitcher_note: In a much-anticipated matchup between Halladay and Yankees ace CC Sabathia at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday, Halladay came up short, allowing six runs in six innings to drop his fourth game in his past six starts. Halladay didn't have his cutter working as effectively as he wanted, and he tied a career high with three home runs allowed. He also wasn't too pleased with home plate umpire Lance Barksdale's strike zone. It's the second time this season Halladay has dropped back-to-back starts, but he hasn't lost three in a row since last August.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano had a solid last outing against the Rockies on Tuesday. He gave up three runs off of five hits, two of those runs coming off of solo blasts. He pitched seven innings, marking Tuesday's game as the 10th time this season he has pitched seven or more innings. He had five strikeouts and one walk in that game. His strength this season has come in being able to successfully use all of his pitches, with his breaking ball being able to easily throw batters off balance. Pavano has the least amount of run support of any Twins starter, but his offense rallied behind him on Tuesday, scoring nine runs.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson has surrendered at least four earned runs in four of his past five starts, including a poor outing against the Angels on Wednesday in which he allowed four runs and a pair of homers in his first pass through the batting order. But presented with the premise that Narveson was struggling, manager Ken Macha dug deeper into the numbers. Narveson's win over the Rangers on June 11 was a good one. In his previous start, June 5 against the Cardinals, he surrendered four runs in the first inning but followed with five shutout innings after that. On May 31 against the Marlins, Macha wanted to pull Narveson after five innings in the South Florida sunshine on Memorial Day, but he was short in the bullpen because of Todd Coffey's thumb injury. The Marlins scored seven times in the sixth inning to erase a 4-0 Brewers lead, and five of the runs were charged to Narveson. So you have to go back to May 26 to find a truly poor outing. "He's been all right," Macha said. "He has to avoid the homers and the big innings."
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing against the Rockies, Baker put up one of the best performances of his career. He tallied a career-best 12 strikeouts, marking only the second time in his career with 10 or more strikeouts. The first time came in a 2009 game against Cleveland. Baker didn't give up a run through the seven innings he pitched and allowed only two hits and one walk in that outing.

home_pitcher_note: Parra limited the Rockies to two runs in six innings on Friday, and didn't walk a batter for only the fourth time in 63 career starts. The last time he made a walk-free start was Aug. 27, 2008. It continued a string of solid performances for the left-hander, who has allowed three or fewer runs in all five of his starts since a move from the Brewers bullpen. He has 23 strikeouts in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: In a great pitching matchup against Colorado's Ubaldo Jimenez, Liriano struggled in the first inning of what could have been a duel. He gave up three runs on four hits in that inning as well as hit two batters and give up a walk. He had only hit one batter prior to that start. However, he settled down after that and gave up only one more hit and two walks in the last six innings of his outing. He had six strikeouts. He has 93 total strikeouts in his 13 starts and has walked 24 batters this season.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo notched nine strikeouts and limited the Rockies to one run on four hits in six innings on Saturday, but his seventh win slipped away from reliever Carlos Villanueva along with a 4-1 lead. Gallardo has 19 strikeouts in his last two starts, but no wins to show for them. Before his loss to the Rangers on June 13, he had won six straight decisions, but took a no-decision against the Twins on May 22 after allowing four runs on six hits in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Like Nick Blackburn, Slowey has been going through a tough stretch in his last two outings. Against the Phillies, Slowey allowed seven runs on seven hits in just 1 2/3 innings. Over his past two starts, Slowey has given up 12 earned runs in 6 1/3 innings, raising his ERA from 3.45 to 4.58 over that stretch. Pitching deep into contests has been an issue for Slowey this season -- he's been unable to complete six innings in 10 of his 14 starts this year. Slowey will try to see if he can last later into a ballgame when he faces the Mets at Citi Field on Friday. It will mark his first career start against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey failed to log a quality start for the first time in his past seven starts last time out. The Yankees tagged him for five runs in seven innings, but the righty settled down late after a rocky first few innings. Pelfrey has continued to pitch well for the Mets this year after a surprisingly great start and has pitched at least six innings in each of his past seven outings. His strikeout numbers aren't too impressive (61 in 93 2/3 innings) but his sinker has produced plenty of ground balls and kept hitters in the ballpark, as he's only allowed five home runs all year.
away_pitcher_note: Like Nick Blackburn, Slowey has had a tough stretch in his past two outings. Against the Phillies, Slowey allowed seven runs on seven hits in 1 2/3 innings. Over his past two starts, Slowey has given up 12 earned runs in 6 1/3 innings, raising his ERA from 3.45 to 4.58 over that stretch. Pitching deep into contests has been an issue for Slowey this season, as he has been unable to complete six innings in 10 of his 14 starts this year. He will try to see if he can last later into a ballgame in his first career start against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Santana will take on his former team, the Twins, for the first time in his career at Citi Field on Saturday. Santana spent eight years and won two Cy Young Awards with the Twins before coming to the Mets in 2008. The lefty has allowed four runs in each of his past three starts, and for a pitcher who led the Majors in strikeouts for three seasons in a row from 2004-06, he can't seem to fan anyone. He has recorded 62 in 98 innings this year and just five in his past three starts.
away_pitcher_note: When Pavano has been good this year, he's been very good. That was the case in his last start when he pitched a complete game against the Phillies on the road while giving up just one run on four hits and striking out two. Pavano has a 2.17 ERA in his eight wins this season and he is also 3-1 with a 2.90 ERA in the month of June. Pavano has also been a key at keeping the bullpen rested, pitching at least seven innings in 11 of his 14 starts this season. Next up for Pavano will be a start against the Mets. He's 7-7 with a 3.60 ERA in 20 career appearances (19 starts) vs. New York.

home_pitcher_note: Mets manager Jerry Manuel decided to leave Niese in after a one-hour rain delay in his last start against the Tigers after Niese didn't allow a single hit in his first three innings of work before the rain came. The lefty was clearly affected by the time off and surrendered six runs while lasting just 4 2/3 innings. Niese earned a no-decision, breaking a run of three consecutive wins for the 23-year-old. It was the first unremarkable start since coming back from the disabled list on June 5. Provided there's no rain delay, Niese will look to regain his impressive form against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a career-high 12 strikeout game against the Rockies, Baker couldn't deliver a duplicate performance against the Brewers his last time out. Baker gave up five runs on nine hits in six innings with most of the damage coming in one inning when his club held a 3-0 lead. Baker acknowledged after the start that he wasn't commanding his breaking pitches and turned to his fastball too much in a four-run inning by Milwaukee. Baker will work to mix in all of his pitches when he faces the Mets in his next start. He is 1-0 with a 3.60 ERA in one career start vs. the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano didn't get a chance to deliver yet another quality start for the Twins, as National League play forced the pitcher out after just five innings in his start vs. the Brewers. Despite having allowed just three runs and throwing 77 pitches, Liriano was removed in the top of the sixth when his turn to bat came with the Twins trailing by one and runners on first and second. Still, Liriano managed to strike out seven in the contest and improve his K/BB ratio to 100/25 on the season. He'll next face the Tigers, who he held scoreless over eight innings in his only start against them so far this year.
away_pitcher_note: The basic numbers from Bonderman's last outing Wednesday against the Mets -- four runs over six-plus innings -- probably don't reflect how he pitched. He needed just 66 pitches through six innings and had 70 when he was lifted following back-to-back singles leading off the seventh. With one early-count ground ball after another, it continued his maturation from the young power pitcher of 2005-06 to a more efficient, pragmatic hurler looking for quick outs and deeper outings. He'll face the Twins for the first time since his plunking of Delmon Young last October drew a three-game suspension.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn's rotation spot has become tenuous, as he's gone 0-4 with a 12.05 ERA in his last five starts. Blackburn has been unable get through four innings in four of his past five starts, and an inability to command his sinker could be to blame.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga owns just eight strikeouts over 32 innings in June, but his work to pitch to contact is working. His six innings last Thursday against the Mets earned him his first win since his would-be perfect game June 2, but the Tigers have won all five of his starts this month.

home_pitcher_note: Like teammate Nick Blackburn, Slowey has been going through a rough stretch of late, going 0-2 with a 12.41 ERA over his past three starts. The right-hander said after his outing against the Mets that he needs to make better two-strike pitches and minimize the big innings.
away_pitcher_note: Oliver made a solid first impression with his poise Friday against the Braves but lost a pitchers' duel in his big league debut despite two runs on five hits over six innings. His 95-97 mph fastball gives the Tigers their first power lefty since former first-round pick Andrew Miller.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano continues to prove he can last deep into the game, pitching two complete games in his last two starts. The right-hander gave up only one run on seven hits in those two games combined. He has gone seven innings in nine of his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Niemann allowed one run on six hits in 7 1/3 innings on Friday, but he took his second loss of the season as Arizona's Edwin Jackson no-hit the Rays. He is 4-0 with a 3.02 ERA in seven road starts this season. He is 1-0 in two career appearances against the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Baker struggled in his last outing against the Mets. He lasted only 4 1/3 innings and gave up six runs on 11 hits in that span. The right-hander has had difficulties pitching deep into outings, making it to the seventh inning or farther only three times in his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Price had one of his best outings of the season in his last start, against Arizona, tying a career high with 11 strikeouts and walking only one batter in eight innings. He surrendered two runs, winning his American League-best 11th game and lowering his ERA to 2.44.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano continues to struggle as he recorded his third consecutive loss in his June 28 start against the Tigers. He gave up four runs off five hits in the first inning alone. He did settle down after that -- a trend that has happened as of late -- and gave up only one run.
away_pitcher_note: Davis worked a season-high 7 1/3 innings against the D-backs. Despite losing his fifth straight start, it seemed as if the advice he got from pitching coach Jim Hickey worked, as he allowed two runs on four hits and threw 73 of his 104 pitches for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn snapped his five-game winless streak against the Tigers on Tuesday. He gave up four runs on seven hits in seven innings. Prior to that outing he had a 12.06 ERA in June. His four strikeouts against Detroit were his most since June 12, when he fanned five.
away_pitcher_note:
Shields took his seventh loss in eight starts Tuesday night against the Red Sox when he allowed five earned runs in five innings.
This will be Shields' first start at Target Field; he had an 0-1 record with a 6.19 ERA in three career starts at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: Litsch allowed just two runs on four hits over six innings on the road against the Indians on Wednesday, but he walked away with a loss due to a lack of run support. The righty struck out two and walked two in his fourth start since being activated from the disabled list.
away_pitcher_note: After throwing consecutive complete games, Pavano gave up three runs on seven hits against Tampa Bay before being pulled in the seventh inning. Two of those runs came with two outs in an inning, and the right-hander said it was those mistakes that cost his team the game.

home_pitcher_note: With Shaun Marcum on the disabled list (right elbow), Rzepczynski steps into the rotation after opening the year with Triple-A Las Vegas. The lefty went 4-3 with a 6.66 ERA in nine starts for Vegas, but was 3-0 with a 2.41 ERA in his past three outings.
away_pitcher_note: After going 0-2 through three starts, Slowey recorded a win over Detroit Wednesday. He allowed only one run on four hits in six innings. The Twins a wanted a longer outing, but Slowey was pulled after taking a ball to the ankle. He is expected to be fine for this start.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching on his 24th birthday on Friday, Cecil earned a no-decision after holding the Yankees to one run on four hits over six innings. The lefty walked six and struck out five, but he limited the damage. Cecil was 0-3 with a 9.19 ERA in his previous three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Baker got back on track on Friday after losing two in a row prior to that start. He gave up only one run off of six hits in a pitching duel against Tampa Bay ace David Price. He had eight strikeouts and no walks through his seven innings pitched.

home_pitcher_note: A win Friday would give Verlander 11 before the All-Star break for the first time in his career. Considering his first victory this year didn't come until April 22, it's quite a feat. He has rolled off five wins in his last six starts and nine in his last 12.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano put up good numbers in his last start against the Rays on Saturday. The lefty fanned 10 batters and walked only one. That is the most strikeouts he has had this season since retiring 11 on June 11. He pitched seven innings and gave up only one run on four hits.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman's pattern of quality outings gone unrewarded in low-scoring games has been replaced by struggles in his last three starts, allowing 15 runs on 25 hits in 16 1/3 innings. His normally nasty slider has been inconsistent and hit hard when it doesn't snap.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn's rotation spot had become tenuous after he went 0-4 with a 12.05 ERA in his first five June starts. The majority of those struggles came on the road, and his next start will be in Detroit for an important series against the Tigers to finish off the first half.

home_pitcher_note: Oliver fell victim to inconsistent command and bad defense behind him in a loss at Minnesota last week, but Jim Leyland likes the idea of pitting his lone lefty starter against Joe Mauer and Justin Morneau. Oliver was knocked out in the second inning of his last start.
away_pitcher_note: The Twins flip-flopped Pavano and fellow starter Kevin Slowey in the last turn of the rotation. It allowed the club to get an extra start before the All-Star break from its most consistent starter.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey has been scuffling of late, like many of the Twins starters. But he threw two perfect innings in relief during the club's last series before the All-Star break on his usual side session day.
away_pitcher_note: Danks briefly flirted with history in his last start, holding the Angels hitless for six innings until Reggie Willits lined a single up the middle for the Angels' first hit of the ballgame. It didn't matter, however, as Danks pitched a shutout to win 1-0.

home_pitcher_note: One problem for Liriano of late has been his inability to keep himself calm in the early innings of big games. The lefty has been overthrowing in those situations, which has resulted in him putting his team in a hole.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd held the Royals scoreless through his first seven innings, but in the eighth the Royals pushed across a run to get on the scoreboard. By that time, the White Sox had already scored five runs and the game was well in hand.

home_pitcher_note: His teammates have called Pavano the club's stopper and he certainly has been their most consistent starter. Pavano is 5-0 in his last seven starts and has been a steadying force in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle pitched a game that had his former teammate and current Royals leadoff hitter Scott Podsednik calling a "vintage Buehrle" performance. He danced in and out of trouble, at one point stranding four runners on base in two innings to earn the win.

home_pitcher_note: Twins manager Ron Gardenhire has decided to keep Blackburn in the rotation for now, but he has to pitch better to remain there. Too many fastballs and sliders in Blackburn's last start vs. the Tigers resulted in trouble.
away_pitcher_note: Garcia earned his team-high ninth win in his last start, holding the Angels at bay for six innings, giving up five hits and two walks. Garcia has made a habit of earning wins against the teams at the top of the standings, as he has pitched his best in those games.

home_pitcher_note: Baker has gone 3-5 in his last 10 starts and struggled against Toronto before the break. He gave up five runs through six innings. He walked only one batter that outing, bringing his season total to a lowly 19.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty surrendered three runs on seven hits and three walks while striking out just one batter in a losing effort Saturday. Laffey had trouble throwing pitches for strikes (56 of his 102 against the Rays), but he was successful in forcing groundouts like he aims to.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey has been struggling of late -- similar to some of the other Twins starters. His last start was no exception. He was pulled in the fourth inning after giving up five runs off of nine hits. He threw 75 pitches in that time.
away_pitcher_note: Masterson gave up five runs -- four of them earned -- on eight hits and three walks in five innings while earning a no-decision vs. the Rays in his last start before the break. Although he wasn't at his best, he said he was pleased with how he pitched in the first half.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty shook his early inning jitters that have come about as of late and didn't allow the White Sox to cross the plate until the fifth inning. In his 7 2/3-inning outing on Friday, he gave up only two runs on six hits. He had eight strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Westbrook needed 105 pitches to get through 5 2/3 innings against the Tigers on Friday, but he limited the damage to two runs on five hits with a walk and five strikeouts. Westbrook hasn't gone more than six innings in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood is expected to be activated from the DL and start on Thursday against the Twins. He has been on the DL since July 6 with a strained right forearm. Millwood stumbled to a 2-8 record with a 5.77 ERA this season prior to his injury.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano's mustache has perhaps been helping him out, as he threw his fourth complete game of the season on Saturday. The right-hander is 6-0 in his past eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie is coming of a dominant outing against Toronto, in which he allowed only a leadoff homer to Fred Lewis over 6 2/3 innings. Guthrie showcased a fastball that topped out at 97 mph and struck out two in the no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Duensing, who has a 1.67 ERA in 43 relief innings, will replace the struggling Nick Blackburn in the rotation. Duensing made nine starts for the Twins in 2009, going 5-1 with a 2.73 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Matusz is coming off his worst start of the season, a 10-1 Orioles loss to the Blue Jays on Sunday. He allowed six runs on five hits in only 1 2/3 innings. All six runs came in the second inning after a scoreless first. Matusz is 0-1 in two career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Baker's struggles continue as he has gone 1-4 in his last five starts. In those five starts he has combined for 23 runs off of 43 hits. Against Cleveland, he gave up six runs off of 10 hits in his 4 2/3-inning outing.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta allowed five earned runs over 5 1/3 innings on Tuesday against the Rays. The rookie walked four and struck out one and will be facing the Twins for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey saw improvements in his game against the Indians. In his first two starts in July, he put up a 7.94 ERA, giving up 10 earned runs off of 19 hits.  However, he gave up only three runs off of six hits on Tuesday against Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander, who beat Toronto in his last start, was the winning pitcher in two of the Royals' last four victories. While Kansas City is among the American League leaders in many offensive categories, they have averaged just 3.6 runs in Greinke's 20 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano put up a good outing for the second start in a row. He pitched seven scoreless innings against Cleveland, allowing only six hits and striking out eight. Only two of Cleveland's batters reached first base multiple times while Liriano was on the mound.

home_pitcher_note: This will be the 11th start for Chen since he took over for injured Gil Meche, now rehabbing in the Minors. Over his 10 starts, Chen is 4-4 with a 4.64 ERA and one of those victories was over the Twins even though he gave up five runs on 10 hits in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano hasn't lost in nine starts since June 3 and has complete games in his past two outings. With five complete games, he's emerged as the most reliable member of the rotation. Pavano blanked the Orioles on five hits in his last start Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Bannister was 0-1 in his first three starts when he finally won against Minnesota on April 25. He'll be trying to end another skid when he faces the Twins Wednesday. He's 0-4 in five starts since defeating the Nationals on June 23.
away_pitcher_note: Duensing will be making his second start and comes off a decent first start of 2010 -- five innings of one-run ball against the Orioles on Friday. The lefty was limited to 66 pitches in that outing, and may get a bump to 75 or 80 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Baker appears to have put the elbow tendinitis that plagued him before the All-Star break behind him. The right-hander is 2-4 over his last six starts but he'll try to build off his last start when he held the Orioles to two runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander attempts to win his first game since May 14, when he was cruising along with the best ERA in the AL, and end July on a positive note. This is his second start of the year against the Twins who saddled him with his third loss.

home_pitcher_note: Like Nick Blackburn, who was moved out of the rotation, Slowey had appeared to be on tenuous ground for his starting spot. But Slowey has turned things around by attacking the strike zone and trusting his catcher more in his last two outings.
away_pitcher_note: Felix has managed to keep his cool despite consistent lack of run support. He has pitched nearly as well this season as he did during his 19-win breakout a year ago, but has received just seven runs of support in his seven losses.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano has been on a tear since the All-Star break, going 3-0 and allowing just two runs in 21 2/3 innings. Another positive sign was Liriano's ability not to get flustered in his last start when his slider wasn't sharp early in the outing.
away_pitcher_note: French, promoted from Triple-A Tacoma on Tuesday, hopes he can pick up where he left off in the Minors, where he went 11-3 with a 2.94 ERA and earned a spot on the PCL All-Star team. He relies more on good location than high velocity.

home_pitcher_note: The Rays will call up Hellickson for his Major League debut. He is not expected to remain in the rotation, just giving the rest of Tampa Bay's starters an extra day between starts.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano continues to be hot as his record over his past 10 starts improved to 8-0 with a win against Kansas City. In that game, Pavano gave up only one run on five hits through five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Niemann was not at his best Wednesday against the Tigers, to the point that he said he probably didn't deserve to win. He gave up four runs and two homers in six innings, but the Rays lineup and defense picked him up as he won his ninth.
away_pitcher_note: Since being moved to a starting role, Duensing has had two successful outings. He pitched 11 innings, allowing three earned runs on 12 hits and five strikeouts. He recorded his first win as a starter against the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Price took over the AL lead and tied a club record with his 14th win of the season Thursday. Pitching off his dominant fastball, he struck out nine while allowing two runs in 6 1/3 innings against Detroit.
away_pitcher_note: Baker improved his record to .500 after recording a win against Seattle on Friday. Although he got into a bases-loaded situation early, he managed to give up only three runs on seven hits through 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Davis finished a great month with a seven-inning, two-run outing vs. the Yankees on Friday. He gave up two runs and three hits in the first inning but just one hit over the next six. He went 4-0 with a 3.03 ERA in five starts in July.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey put up one of his best performances of the season on Saturday, giving up only three hits through eight innings in the Twins' shutout victory. It was his longest outing since tossing eight on April 20 against Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: Gomez, who was called up from Triple-A Saturday, pitched five innings on only three days' rest, giving up two runs on five hits. His second start for the Indians also allowed him to capture his second win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano put up a gem in his seven-inning outing against the Mariners. He fanned 11 batters and gave up only two hits while walking two batters as well. The 11 strikeouts tied a season high set on June 11 against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Silencing the Red Sox in his last start Monday, Carmona gave up two runs (one earned) while striking out five in seven innings. It capped off a run of allowing three earned runs or fewer in eight of his past 10 road starts.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano pitched well but took his first loss since June 3 on Monday vs. the Rays, ending his career-high eight-game winning streak. He allowed four runs on nine hits and two walks. A 32-pitch fifth frame that featured three doubles was the difference.

home_pitcher_note: Thanks to two home runs he gave up Tuesday against the Red Sox, Huff took his 10th loss of the season. In 5 1/3 innings, the lefty gave up seven hits on three runs and struck out two. With the loss, he falls to 0-7 on the road with a 7.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Duensing tossed six innings of three-run ball Tuesday in a no-decision against the Rays. The 27-year-old lefty is 1-0 with a 3.18 ERA in three starts since joining the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia has 10 victories this season but should have 12 if not for closer Bobby Jenks failing to protect three-run leads for him in Minneapolis and in his last start at Detroit. Garcia has a 10-6 career mark against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Baker earned a no-decision after arguably his best start of the season against the Rays on Wednesday. The right-hander threw eight scoreless, three-hit innings, gave up one walk, hit one batter and was on pace to pick up his 10th win of the year.

home_pitcher_note: The first three batters reached against Danks in the Orioles' extra-inning win on Friday. Only three other batters reached the rest of the way over Danks' seven innings of one-run baseball. Danks is 1-1 vs. the Twins this season and 5-6 lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: After having his bullpen session canceled Sunday, Kevin Slowey will miss this start due to soreness in his elbow. Glen Perkins, who is 4-9 with a 6.08 ERA in 23 Triple-A starts (but 3-1 with a 2.70 ERA in his past seven), is likely to get the start.

home_pitcher_note: Pitching before nearly 30 friends and family members, Floyd returned home to Baltimore and picked up his fourth straight victory. His streak of innings without a home run ended at 77 1/3 Saturday, but he still has a 1.19 ERA in his past 12 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano's 21-inning scoreless streak came to an abrupt halt Friday, when he yielded three runs in the first inning of a no-decision against the Indians. He allowed four runs on seven hits and six walks with six strikeouts in 4 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano scattered seven hits over seven innings of two-run ball Saturday against the Indians for his American League-leading eighth road victory. The 34-year-old righty last won more than 14 games in 2004, when he notched 18 for the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez tossed seven shutout innings in a 6-2 win over the Rangers on Saturday, using an effective curveball and throwing a lot of strikes. Gonzalez faced the Twins on June 6 in Oakland, limiting them to two runs over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Duensing on Sunday yielded four runs on nine hits with no walks and three strikeouts over a career-high 7 1/3 innings in a victory against the Indians. The 27-year-old lefty is 2-0 with a 3.33 ERA in four starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill allowed two unearned runs over eight strong innings in Sunday's 3-2 win over the Rangers. Cahill is 3-0 with a 0.00 ERA in his past three starts, a span of 25 innings. He's finished at least eight innings in each of those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Slowey missed his last start due to tendinitis in his elbow, but he threw a bullpen session on Thursday and said he felt good to go. He is 3-1 with a 5.33 ERA in his last 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro worked around a rough first inning to toss seven innings of three-run ball against the Mariners on Monday, but he was charged with the loss in a 3-1 defeat. Mazzaro tossed a season-high 113 pitches, 69 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Baker will face the White Sox for the second time in as many starts. In his last outing, on Wednesday, he gave up four runs on eight hits through six innings. He had five strikeouts that night.
away_pitcher_note: Danks saved the bullpen after Freddy Garcia's abbreviated effort Tuesday by going eight innings in Wednesday's victory. They were eight quality innings, with Danks permitting one run on six hits, striking out seven and walking two.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano recorded a win in his last outing, against the White Sox on Thursday, giving up only one run on seven hits in 5 2/3 innings. He had four strikeouts, his fewest since he recorded only one against Detroit on July 9.
away_pitcher_note: Gavin Floyd had his worst start since June 2 in his last start, surrendering six earned runs in a 6-1 loss to the Twins. Floyd gave up his fourth career home run to Jason Kubel in 32 career at-bats. That one was a three-run home run in the seventh.

home_pitcher_note: Although Pavano got his 15th win in his last start -- the first time doing so since the '04 season -- he fought through 6 1/3 innings. He gave up two runs on 10 hits, only the third time he has allowed double digits in hits this year.
away_pitcher_note: After picking up win No. 146 and moving 40 games over .500, Buehrle preps for his second start of the second half in Minnesota. Buehrle is 24-17 vs. the Twins, his highest win and loss total vs. a team.

home_pitcher_note: Duensing had a fantastic outing on Saturday against the A's. He threw his first career complete game, shutting out Oakland. He gave up only three hits in the game, all of those coming in the first three innings.

away_pitcher_note: Bell was rolling along in Detroit in his most recent start when he ran into trouble in the middle innings and began forcing the issue, overthrowing and overthinking, rather than relaxing and letting his talent flow. He's progressing in each start.

away_pitcher_note: Weaver is coming off one of his few rough outings of the season, giving up more than four runs for only the third time this season. The Angels have averaged 2.27 runs in his past 11 starts, giving him no more than four runs in any of those games.

away_pitcher_note: Blackburn gets this start in place of Kevin Slowey, who was forced to the disabled list after experiencing pain in his right triceps. As a starter with the Twins this year, Blackburn has a 6.53 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: Verlander hasn't strung together back-to-back wins in more than a month, but he'll have a chance to do so in his next start, against the Twins, whom he held to two runs over 5 1/3 innings in a victory on July 9.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn has been on a roll since returning to the Twins rotation following a brief stint in the Minor Leagues to work on his mechanics. He's 2-1 with a 1.78 ERA in four starts for Minnesota since coming back on Aug. 23.

away_pitcher_note: Gomez was rocked for seven runs on seven hits across three innings in Wednesday's loss to the Angels. The rookie righty is winless across his past five outings after going 3-0 with a 1.54 ERA through four Major League starts.

home_pitcher_note: It was another quality start for Blackburn, who has delivered one in all five starts since returning from a brief stint in the Minor Leagues. He's 2-2 with a 1.91 ERA in five starts for Minnesota since rejoining the rotation on Aug. 23.
away_pitcher_note: After three no-decisions this month, Carlos Carrasco got that first Major League victory he was longing for Friday in Kansas City. He worked six innings, allowing three runs on eight hits. It was his fourth quality start since his Sept. 1 promotion.

away_pitcher_note: Despite being bothered slightly by a stiff neck in his last two starts, Pavano managed to pick up win No. 17 in his last start against Chicago. Pavano gave up five runs over five innings, but now sits one win away from his career high (18).

away_pitcher_note: Duensing will be the starter for Game 3 of the Twins' opening playoff series. But he'll need to get through his start on Sunday first. His last outing was a rough one. The lefty matched his career high with four walks, yet only gave up three runs.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Hochevar's fourth start since missing three months with a strained elbow. He's 1-2 in his previous three starts. His actual return came Sept. 7 with three innings of relief against the Twins in which he gave up three runs on five hits.
away_pitcher_note: Like Kevin Slowey, Baker is competing for a long-reliever spot when the Twins open the playoffs. Baker hasn't lost since July 19 and has a 5-0 record in nine starts since then. In his last outing on Sept. 22, he held Cleveland to a run on five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano left his last start early with flu-like symptoms, but has been given a clean bill of health. He has been chosen to pitch Game 1 of the American League Division Series.
away_pitcher_note: Against Seattle on Thursday, Hill earned his first win since April of last year. Making his third start after spending most of the year rehabbing from his second career Tommy John surgery, he logged five shutout innings and struck out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano will be trying to rebound from a tough start in Detroit. He was touched for three home runs in the fourth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Romero will aim for a career-best 14th win when he pitches at Target Field for the first time. Saturday, the lefty walked away with a no-decision after holding Baltimore to three runs over five innings, ending with three strikeouts and five walks.

home_pitcher_note: Duensing surrendered five runs over 6 2/3 innings in his last start at Detroit. All the runs came off homers by Miguel Cabrera and Ramon Santiago.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start on Sunday, Marcum was in fine form, limiting the Orioles to one unearned run on four hits over seven innings. The righty struck out seven and walked two, picking up the win and his seventh quality start in his past eight outings.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn was touched for eight runs over 4 1/3 innings in a loss at Kansas City last Tuesday. Blackburn gave up two homers to Kila Ka'aihue.
away_pitcher_note: At home against the Yankees on Wednesday, Rzepczynski piled up nine strikeouts in a solid five-inning performance. The lefty picked up a win, improving to 2-0 with a 3.31 ERA over his past three starts.

home_pitcher_note: The Twins turn to their hard-throwing lefty for the critical start in Game 1 of the ALDS vs. the Yankees. Liriano is coming off a season with a career-high 14 wins while posting a 3.62 ERA. This will be his first ever postseason start.
away_pitcher_note: The Yanks' easiest decision of the playoffs was naming Sabathia the Game 1 starter. Sabathia made five playoff starts last year, pitching Game 1 in all three rounds. He was 3-1 with a 1.98 ERA, limiting each opponent to three earned runs or fewer.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano has been the veteran leader of the Twins staff, recording a team-high 17 wins while posting a 3.75 ERA in 221 innings and stabilizing the rotation when needed. The right-hander is 2-1 in nine career playoff appearances (three starts).
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte comes into the postseason having made three starts after missing two months with a groin strain. The reliable performer leads all Major Leaguers in career playoff wins (18) and innings pitched (249).

home_pitcher_note: Hughes picked up his 18th victory with a one-inning relief appearance at Boston. The Yankees skipped his last start, so he'll be well rested. He did not pitch well during last year's playoffs, allowing six runs in 6 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After the Twins' rotation hit a speed bump in the middle of July, the Twins turned to Duensing to help stem the tide. They moved him from the bullpen into a starting role on July 23. Since then, he is 7-2 with a 3.05 ERA in 13 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Romero will begin the year as the No. 1 starter though he is entering just his third full season. The 26-year-old suffered through an up and down spring in part because of inflammation in his left middle finger.
away_pitcher_note: Pavano will be making his second career Opening Day start when he takes the mound against the Jays. His first go-round came with the Yankees in '07, when he allowed four runs in 4 1/3 innings in a loss to Tampa Bay.

home_pitcher_note: Top prospect Drabek earned a spot in the starting rotation thanks in part to a successful Grapefruit League season. The 23-year-old made his Major League debut late in the 2010 season but went winless in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano is looking to continue his ascent as a top pitcher after a breakout season in 2010 in which he posted a 3.62 ERA and 201 strikeouts. But he needs to work on his control, as walks plagued him in Spring Training.

away_pitcher_note: Blackburn struggled last season with an uncharacteristic 5.42 ERA after posting similar ERAs in the low 4.00s in the previous two seasons. But he had a great spring and is a prototypical ground-ball pitcher.

home_pitcher_note: Nova won the fourth starter's slot after posting a 1.80 ERA in 20 spring innings. He appeared in 10 games (seven starts) last year for New York, and going deeper into games is a focus for the promising right-hander.
away_pitcher_note: Baker was the Twins' Opening Day starter a year ago but came into camp battling Kevin Slowey for the final spot in the rotation. He won the job with an impressive spring and is looking to stay healthy this year.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia makes his second turn in the rotation after drawing New York's Opening Day start. The ace lefty didn't face the Twins in the regular season last year but was a winner in Game 1 of the ALDS against Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Duensing helped lead the Twins to the playoffs last season when he joined the rotation in late July and posted a 3.05 ERA in 13 starts down the stretch. He's hoping to have similar success over a full season as a starter.

away_pitcher_note: Pavano gets a chance to exact revenge on his former team when he starts against the Yankees. Pavano is coming off a rough outing, as he allowed seven earned runs over four-plus innings in an Opening Day loss to the Jays.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett will look to build on his victorious five innings of three-run ball against the Tigers despite illness and a lack of stamina. Burnett was 1-0 with a 1.54 ERA in two starts against the Twins in 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano had control problems in his first start of the season when he walked five in just 4 1/3 innings, while also giving up two homers in a loss to the Jays. He is 0-2 with a 3.12 ERA against the Yankees in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Pavano's scheduled start was pushed back due to rain, causing him to miss a chance at pitching against his former club, the Yankees. But he will take the mound for the Twins' home opener against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson put together a strong first outing, surrendering just one earned run with six strikeouts in six innings against the Mariners. The left-hander was forced to throw 108 pitches, though, preventing him from working deeper into the game.

home_pitcher_note: Rain prevented Blackburn from pitching the home opener, so he will start the second game against the A's. He pitched well in his first outing, allowing just one earned run over 5 2/3 innings in a win over the Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez was effectively wild in his first start against Seattle, throwing just 67 of his 116 pitches for strikes but surrendering just one run in seven innings. The lefty, who walked four in the game, walked 92 batters in 200 1/3 innings last year.

home_pitcher_note: Baker was victimized by the long ball in his first start of the season, against the Yankees on Monday, when he allowed four runs on two homers over six innings. He is 4-0 with a 3.62 ERA in five career starts against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: The effective righty utilized just 89 pitches in eight innings in his A's debut against the Blue Jays, surrendering four earned runs on seven hits with two strikeouts. It marked McCarthy's first big league start since his 2009 Rangers season.

home_pitcher_note: Outside of a pair of early home runs leading to four runs, Duensing pitched well against the Yankees on Tuesday, when he struck out seven over six innings. He will start the opener against the Royals after rain pushed his start back.
away_pitcher_note: Francis has had two solid starts, giving up just three earned runs in 13 2/3 innings. He's also issued just two walks along with 13 hits. In Francis' last start against the White Sox, he worked six scoreless innings before hitting a two-run snag.

away_pitcher_note: Davies was unable to command his fastball last Friday at Detroit. In only 3 2/3 innings, he walked five, hit a batter and made three wild pitches. He also gave up five runs. Davies is 4-6 vs. the Twins, but lost his only start at Target Field.

home_pitcher_note: Shields, who had his start rained out vs. the Red Sox on Wedneday, allowed three home runs in a six-inning no-decision Friday night vs. Chicago. He adjusted his mechanics during the offseason and has seen good results thus far.
away_pitcher_note: After having his scheduled start bumped back due to rain, Pavano bounced back from a rough Opening Day to toss eight innings in the home opener against the A's, giving up just one run on four hits in the Twins' 2-1 victory.

away_pitcher_note: Despite giving up just one run on five hits over six innings, Blackburn remained winless against the A's in his career after the Twins' 1-0 loss Saturday. He has allowed one earned run in 11 2/3 innings pitched this season.

away_pitcher_note: Baker has had trouble keeping the ball in the park, as he's allowed four homers in two games, accounting for six of the eight runs he's given up this season. Baker is 2-2 with a 3.21 ERA in six career outings against the Rays.

away_pitcher_note: Making his first home start of the year, Duensing tossed six solid innings before nearly letting things get out of hand in the seventh. Thanks to some impressive pitching out of the bullpen, he came away with the no-decision.

away_pitcher_note: Liriano held K.C. hitless through three innings before getting touched for six runs on eight hits in the fourth during his last outing. Ron Gardenhire attributed Liriano's continued middle-inning woes to the lefty getting "overhyped" about mistakes.

away_pitcher_note: Blackburn took the loss in his last start after allowing six runs, but the numbers weren't as bad as they seemed: The righty held Tampa Bay scoreless over five innings before a messy sixth, something that could be corrected as he gains strength.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie began the season with two quality starts, allowing just a run in his first 14 innings. In his third outing, against the Indians, he crashed back to earth, allowing six runs on 10 hits and a walk and striking out only two in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Baker worked seven strong innings, but got a no-decision when the 'pen faltered. The righty had good movement that he used to strike out six, but also proved himself able to work out of several jams along the way.
